author: Unknown
title: Elisée Reclus - The Vivisection of China
content:
Author

: Elisée Reclus

Title

: The Vivisection of China

Date

: 1898

Notes

: From the September 1898 issue of The Atlantic

Source

: Retrieved on October 22, 2026 from an archived copy of https://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/1898/09/the-vivisection-of-china/636369/


 THE great events which are creating such an excitement in the West Indies over the last shreds of the ancient colonial empire of Spain will undoubtedly have consequences of extreme importance, and become, in the fullest sense of the term, a part of history. But, however intense their interest, and however marked the change which they are certain to occasion in the equilibrium of the world, they remain altogether inferior in real significance to the revolutions which are taking place in the Far East.


 War of some sort between America and Spain on the subject of Cuba had long been unavoidable. No less than a century ago, — at the time when France lost her plantations in San Domingo, and the republic of Hayti was born, — it was easy to foresee the rupture of the ties which had bound to the Spain of Cortez and Pizarro the insular fragments of the great hemisphere appropriated by Pope Alexander VI. The various colonies were sure to break away, one by one, from their metropolitan stepmother, set up for themselves, and live their own life. Cuba and Porto Rico, sucked into the whirlpool of war, are but accomplishing their “manifest destiny,” and fulfilling the prophecies repeatedly uttered by the historians of the last generation but one.


 The progress of events in the eastern portion of the Asian continent had by no means been so fully anticipated. One might certainly have ventured to predict that there, also, populations long crushed by civil and military oppression would one day lay claim to the rights of free men; but it could never have been foreseen under what amazingly dramatic conditions the claim would be asserted. Our ancestors, at the beginning of the nineteenth century, would never have harbored, in their wildest dreams, the fantastic notion that Japan, the empire of the Rising Sun, would spontaneously transform itself into a “European power;” European, at least, if not in language, history, and traditions, in the complete recasting of its administration, institutions, customs, and theories, in its devotion to science, and in its entire and unreserved acceptance of a policy based on observation and experience.


 This is the great event of the century, — one which casts into the shade all the other occurrences of an epoch which has nevertheless been rich in memorable events. And it will be no solitary

avatar;

 there are unmistakable signs that other transformations of the same character are about to take place in the vast empire of China, and in all those countries where inhabitants of different race, yellow, red, or black, are brought into close contact with the men of our own Aryano - Greco - Latin civilization. So vanishes that oft-repeated assertion of the ethnologists, that

race

 is a final and irreducible fact, and that no possible progress in the perception of scientific or moral truths can ever prevail against it. It is from this point of view that the recent history of the Far East presents phenomena to which it behooves us to devote our most serious attention.


 There are those, of course, who tell us that all these events are illusory; that the prodigious changes which have taken place in the Japanese world are a lying phantasmagoria and a vain show; that the national mind and character have undergone no real modification; and that the Japanese are sure to escape, sooner or later, from the sphere of European attraction. We hear them compared to savages, who, having learned in the schools of London or Paris the customs of civilization, make haste, as soon as they get back to their forests and savannas, to cast aside their conventional garments, and array themselves in the toggery consecrated by ancestral instinct and hereditary custom.


 Such assertions appear to us to rest on a complete misconception of indisputable facts. The Japanese have most certainly entered into that realm of civilization on which Bacon and Darwin have set their seal; for if imperial caprice and the spread of bourgeois fashions have power to alter the external aspect of a nation, such influences can have but little effect on its underlying moral sense, its religious beliefs, its educational theories, and the essential principle of its …

author: Joe Mullin
title: Canadians Are Running Out Of Time To Oppose The Dangerous C-22 Surveillance Bill
content:
Canada’s Parliament is debating a massive expansion of surveillance powers that will threaten the privacy and security of millions of people. Bill C-22, also called the Lawful Access Act, has already passed the House of Commons, and is now before the Canadian Senate. 


Canadians still have an opportunity to speak out and stop this dangerous legislation. The Canadian Civil Liberties Association (CCLA) is

urging all Canadians

 to

sign its petition

 opposing the bill. (The petition on CCLA’s website is governed by CCLA’s privacy policy.) 


Take action


Tell the canadian senate to stop C-22


As we

wrote earlier this year

, Bill C-22 gives the government new powers to force digital services—including telecom companies, messaging apps, and more—to help with government surveillance. Worse, it allows Canada’s Minister of Public Safety to order companies to create a backdoor to their services for law enforcement, as long as it doesn’t lead to a “systemic insecurity.” That’s a clear recipe for weakening the encryption we all rely on. 


It also requires services to retain metadata for up to a year, which reveals who people communicate with, where they go, and what services they use, even when they are not suspected of any crime. 


Researchers at CCLA and Citizen Lab published a

detailed analysis

 of C-22 and its serious constitutional and cybersecurity problems. The analysis points out that the bill needs more than cosmetic changes—it calls for entirely withdrawing Part 2 of Bill C-22, the section that establishes the surveillance and data retention regime. 


Bill C-22 could also expand the sharing of Canadians’ personal data with foreign law enforcement, including the United States. Canada has been negotiating a cross-border data-sharing agreement with the U.S. that would allow American police to get information about Canadian internet users without any Canadian court oversight. 


Some Canadian senators have already

expressed concerns

 about the bill, and rightly suggested, as CCLA and Citizen Lab have, that it may not be compatible with privacy protections in the Canadian constitution. 


If you’re in Canada, read and sign CCLA’s petition opposing Bill C-22 today. Don’t let the Senate allow this dangerous expansion of government surveillance to become Canada’s new reality. 


Take action


Canadians: defend your privacy and security

author: Tam Saavedra
title: The UN CRPD Guidelines on Intersectionality Just Changed the Game for Disability Rights—Here’s What You Need to Know
content:
Big news for women with disabilities and all feminist disabled advocates, allies, and organizations worldwide!

 


During its 35th Session in August 2026, the

UN Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UN CRPD)

 officially adopted the historic

Guidelines on Identifying and Addressing Intersectional Discrimination Against Girls, Adolescents, Women, and Older Women with Disabilities

.

 


This milestone represents a monumental step forward for disability rights. For the first time, States have explicit, actionable guidance to support their obligations at the intersection of gender and disability.

 


Read the official CRPD Guidelines here

 


What Are the CRPD Guidelines on Intersectional Discrimination?}


The Guidelines serve as an authoritative framework developed by the UN


CRPD Committee to help States better prevent, monitor, and address intersectional discrimination.

 


Throughout years of UN CRPD country review processes, the Committee identified a persistent, critical gap:

the specific rights of women with disabilities and the complex, intersectional discrimination they experience are rarely understood or adequately addressed by governments.

 


As the UN CRPD celebrates its 20th anniversary, these Guidelines were issued to bridge that gap—ensuring the convention is implemented to benefit

all

 women, girls, and gender-diverse persons with disabilities across their lifespans.

 


Why Are These Guidelines a Game


–

Changer?

 


International documents rarely explicitly focus on the detailed, lived experiences and rights of women with disabilities. These Guidelines clearly name and elaborate on the systemic barriers

’

 women and gender-diverse persons with disabilities face daily across the globe, including:

 


Sexual & Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR):

 Addressing and preventing enforced sterilization, forced contraception, lack of accessible healthcare, restrictions on abortion, and lack of perinatal, menstrual, and menopause care.

 


Gender-Based & Disability-Based Violence:

 Exposing institutional violence, digital/online abuse, and the widespread lack of support services for victims.

 


Caregiving Recognition:

 Validating women with disabilities as active caregivers and mothers, rather than only recipients of care.

 


Economic & Educational Exclusion:

 Highlighting barriers in the labor market, economic and exclusion from education during puberty.

 


Crisis & Climate Response:

 Tackling compounded exclusion during environmental disasters, climate emergencies, and humanitarian relief efforts.

 


…just to name a few.

 


7 Key Breakthroughs in the Framing of the Guidelines 

 


What makes this document uniquely transformative is its progressive, structural approach:

 


Explicit Inclusion of Gender Diversity:

 The Guidelines explicitly encompass the rights of transgender, intersex, non-binary, and other gender-diverse persons with disabilities and ask for gender diversity – inclusive interpretation of all obligations described. 

 


Recognition of Historical Root Causes:

 The Committee explicitly addresses the legacy and ongoing impacts of

colonialism and enslavement

, establishing that States benefiting from these historical systems bear a particular responsibility to remedy their ongoing effects.

 


An Open Catalogue of Diversity:

 The text recognizes that women with disabilities belong to multi-marginalized communities—including Indigenous, Black, Dalit, Adivasi, refugee, asylum-seeking, religious minority, and pastoralist groups or persons living in informal settings, among others —while leaving space for all intersecting identities.

 


Structural & Preventive Approach:

 Moving beyond a strictly punitive, reactive model, the Guidelines demand the dismantling of systemic oppression (such as ableism, audism, racism, and patriarchy) through early intervention, education, and public policy reform. 

 


Decriminalization

 is also a disability issue:

The guidelines recognize impacts of criminalization of abortion, homosexuality, gender identity and expression as well as

restricting marriage or consensual relationships as an important intersectional disability rights issue.

 


Holding digital platforms accountable:

Call for international and regional cooperation on human rights-based regulation of digital platforms and artificial intelligence systems to address technology-facilitated violence, algorithmic bias and discrimination …

author: Jenny Brown
title: Tampa TSA Union Averted   Privatization Disaster
content:
TSA agents noticed something was up. “We started seeing people around the airport that you wouldn’t normally see, people in suits,” said Mark Harris, Transportation Security Officer and union steward in Tampa, Florida.


That’s when he realized the airport was a target for the TSA privatization program he had been reading about—the $13 billion Gold+ program. Harris, and his union Government Employees (AFGE) Local 556, swung into action.


Transportation Security Administration workers have been winning battles lately. Twice in two years the Trump administration has tried to cancel their union contract, and twice it has been stopped by the courts. Now things are mostly back to normal, with the contract in force and grievances being processed.


But Gold+ would undermine the union by outsourcing TSO jobs to private companies. As the dimensions of the plan became clear, Harris said his co-workers “felt like they had been kicked in the gut. You know, everything that they had worked for, their federal pension, careers, everything.”


Tampa is a model airport that consistently ranks at the top in customer satisfaction. That’s why TSA picked it for the Gold+ privatization effort, Harris said. “They don’t want to give it to a poor airport or a failing airport. That would be disastrous for TSA, right?”


DOWN THE RABBIT HOLE


Harris first became aware of Gold+ from

Against Giants

, a website maintained by an ex-TSA agent. As he went down a research rabbit hole, a fellow steward took on some of his union work so he could focus.


Harris, a former police detective, was able to ferret out government documents to back up the union’s case. The agency “seemed like they were trying to do it under the cover of darkness,” he said. The program wasn’t officially acknowledged until July 21, and even then AFGE had to sue to get documents.


Although TSA insisted that the private jobs would pay the same, Harris found that they were saying the opposite to prospective contractors. He found that staff and wage cuts were essential to the program.


When confronted, TSA officials told the workers they didn’t know what the private companies would pay, but also reassured them that their pay wouldn’t change. “That kind of got me… We’re not being truthful about this, right?” Harris said.


The local’s president, Chris Finlay, had worked at a smaller airport at Sanford, Florida, where a private security company came in. At first they hired people at their former pay, but after a few weeks, “they brought them all in one by one. They said, sorry, we can no longer pay you that. We can only pay you this starting pay,” Harris said.


PRESSURE POINTS


The union figured out who would be deciding on Gold+ in Tampa—the airport’s board of directors—and then organized pressure from workers and the community.


The union argued that if privatization came in, salaries would be cut and that would affect local businesses: TSOs wouldn’t take their families out to dinner, or to a football game. If TSOs had to suddenly relocate, it would depress housing prices. Harris created pre-written letters from business owners, airport workers, and others, and union members asked everyone they knew to send the letters.


For workers, the stakes were clear, Harris said. When jobs are privatized, “we know there’s no union protections. But when you work for Homeland Security, when you work for TSA, it’s a career.”


That career was hard-won. Airports used a patchwork of private security companies until TSA was founded in 2001. But it was the union that built TSO jobs into sustainable ones, by winning first union representation and then a contract in 2011. Finally in 2023, TSA workers were included in the federal pay schedule. AFGE now represents 47,000 TSA workers.


Local 556 leadership met with the mayors of Tampa and neighboring St. Petersburg, along with congressional representatives. Airport workers raised questions and objections at in-person town hall meetings with TSA and airport leadership.


Finally, on August 24, Tampa airport leaders decided not to adopt the program. It was apparently a fatal blow—TSA cancelled the entire project right after Tampa’s decision. Private companies had already advertised jobs for the contracts they anticipated.


The union expects the push for privatization

to continue

, but workers definitively won this round.

author: Taylor Noakes
title: ‘Snipped And Posted’: How Pro-Oil Groups Generate Viral Content Online
content:
In December 2025, former B.C. Premier Christy Clark gave an interview on Global News where she described Canada’s west coast ban on oil tankers as a “ridiculous” constraint on the Canadian economy.


A clip of Clark’s interview then began to circulate online, where it was shared by several Canadian conservative influencers and aggregator accounts on platforms including X and Facebook with captions including “reality check,” “huge truth bomb” and “economic self-sabotage.”


Within days, the interview clip was spreading across the social media feeds of people in B.C. and beyond, eventually surpassing 1.6 million views.


But this was not necessarily a case of west coast residents suddenly deciding organically they wanted to overturn the ban on coastal oil tanker traffic brought in by former Liberal Prime Minister Justin Trudeau.


The digital media amplification of Clark’s comments was orchestrated in part by Canada Action, a pro-oil industry advocacy organization partly funded by

Cenovus Energy

, Canada’s third-largest oil and gas company.


It was one example of “showcasing Canada Action’s content leadership influencing the public discussion,” according to an internal slidedeck from the Calgary-based group. That slidedeck, which hasn’t yet been reported on, was obtained by Greenpeace Canada and published in its October 2026 report

Manufacturing Petro-Populism

.


Screenshot from a Canada Action Slidedeck called “Extended Third Party Reach: Showcasing Canada Action’s content leadership influencing the public discussion”.


These and other presentation slides from Canada Action demonstrate how fossil fuel interests manufacture the appearance of consent for increased oil and gas production in Canada, according to experts who study the spread of climate disinformation online.


“Most people can pretty easily see through messages coming directly from the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers (CAPP) or industry CEOs,” said Shane Gunster, a professor at Simon Fraser University’s School of Communications, in a statement to DeSmog. 


“But when the message comes from people in their social network, local business leaders, their family and friends, they’re far more likely to engage with it and maybe even be persuaded by it. And this is especially true for growing segments of the public that don’t consume a lot of news.”


Canada Action didn’t respond to DeSmog’s questions about the slidedeck.

Get the weekly intelligence you need to hold polluters accountable


Email Address


Sign Up


Send me intelligence from:


All


US/Global team


UK/Europe team


‘Snipped And Posted’


Canada Action was founded in 2012 by

Cody Battershill

, a Calgary-based realtor. Though Canada Action claims to be a grassroots effort, it has

numerous


reported

 ties to the fossil fuel sector and its lobbyists. According to the Greenpeace report, Canada Action spent $1.9 million CAD on marketing in 2024, and $1.5 million CAD in 2023.


The presentations were made in the context of a funder session for the group Canadian Energy Prosperity (CEP), through its Energy in Action (EIA) initiative, and held at the Calgary Petroleum Club in January 2026.


According to the Greenpeace report, Energy in Action is an oil-industry backed network of thirty organizations that advocate for the fossil fuel sector, including front groups, charitable organizations, companies, media organizations and lobby groups. EIA is itself funded by Canadian Energy Prosperity.


Though neither of these are public facing organizations, members of EIA’s network are prominent pro-oil and gas voices in Canada. They include, among others, the

Fraser Institute

,

Canada Action

,

Energy United

,

Debunk

,

Canadians for Affordable Energy

, Young Canadians for Resources,

Resource Works

, Energy Creates, and The News Forum.

 


Two of those organizations, Resource Works and Energy United, prepared a slidedeck for the Calgary Petroleum Club event describing environmental groups as “opponents” and Indigenous rights as a “problem,” as

reported previously

 in the Narwhal.


 Many of the groups that are funded by CEP also receive funding from Gwyn Morgan, a Canadian fracking magnate who has financed a climate misinformation ecosystem with nearly

$10 million in funding to right wing

 anti-regulation lobby groups. Morgan is also linked to Cenovus (which has funded Canada Action), as well as

Second Street

, a libertarian advocacy organization …

author: Mehk Chakraborty
title: Inside the resistance to Spain’s crackdown on migrants in Ceuta
content:
This article

Inside the resistance to Spain’s crackdown on migrants in Ceuta

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


On July 30, images streamed across TVs, social media feeds and newspapers of thousands of people approaching a fence along the beach, in boats and by foot. Migrants, including children and families, were attempting to cross into Ceuta, a Spanish enclave bordered by Morocco. Facing violent border guards and the threat of drowning, over 70,000 people made it to Ceuta, with hopes of eventually reaching the Spanish mainland. Officials in Ceuta

said

 that 100 people died in the crossing — either by drowning or being crushed — and sources on the ground believe the number was higher. 


“I lost my phone, my money, my ID card, everything I had,” one Moroccan teenager recalled. “At one point I got pulled to the bottom, so far down that my feet touched the sand. When I looked around me, I saw women and babies who had drowned.”


“There was no proper humanitarian response from the local authorities — whether it is basic hygiene, food or shelter,” said Ric Fernández, coordinator and spokesperson for humanitarian and migrant advocacy group No Name Kitchen, or NNK, about the first days after the mass crossing. “Instead, there was an institutional response of pressuring people to ‘voluntarily’ return to Morocco. … There was repression, violence against people on the move in every form — legal, administrative and physical, and the forced expulsion of people.”   


Facing intense pressure and violence from both the Spanish police and military, within 96 hours most people returned to Morocco. Estimates about how many migrants remain are in flux, but the Spanish government

said

 in late September that up to 10,000 people are still in Ceuta.


While the global mainstream media quickly moved on from this story, the situation in Ceuta has

remained tense

 over the last three months, with increased violent harassment by the police, evictions and collective expulsions. In recent weeks,

“voluntary returns” and evictions

 from makeshift camps on the beach have ramped up.


Embed from Getty Images


Irene Estébanez Gutiérrez, a family and community doctor in Madrid, spent two weeks in Ceuta as a volunteer. “An information campaign has been waged that portrays people on the move as invaders, violent and dangerous,” she said. The

media coverage

, she believes, has failed to adequately address “the resulting humanitarian crisis, the systematic violation of rights, the lack of protection for minors, and the systematic violence and discrimination to which people are being subjected to, particularly by the military.”


Those who remain include Moroccan men and women, alongside Sudanese, Syrians, Palestinians, Malians and Nigerians. According to NNK, a significant number are minors. They are still stranded; the majority of them have slept in the street or in makeshift tents since they crossed into Ceuta over two months ago. 


Kora, who uses a pseudonym as an activist to protect her identity, arrived in Ceuta to volunteer in early August and found the violence and the lack of access to basic necessities particularly angering. The authorities were “not letting them access the supermarkets to get food or water,” she said. “They turned off the publicly and freely accessible water [to shower or drink] on the beaches and beat them or scare them in the middle of the night … to purposefully making their lives more miserable.” 


Organizing solidarity, facing criminalization


This

violence

, however, did not prevent activists and migrants from developing forms of organizing and resistance. Hundreds of migrants

staged a protest

 on a popular beach in Ceuta in August to demand asylum. On Sept. 21, Migreurop, a Euro-African network of organizations, activists and researchers that monitors European migration policies, noted in a

joint statement

 with over 100 organizations: “We have witnessed forms of resistance in everyday survival practices.” They mentioned the sharing of information, food and medicine, as well as safety and protection practices.

We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


Besides migrants’ self-led efforts, civil society has stepped up to help, with the Spanish Red Cross

distributing food

 at Trampolín Beach, the site of one makeshift camp. Other local charities like Luna Blanca, have been

author: Equality Now
title: The 2026 Equality Now “Make Equality Reality” Gala celebrates courage and those who choose it, honouring Virginia Roberts Giuffre, Gisèle Pelicot and Caroline Darian
content:
22nd October 2026


The 2026 Equality Now “Make Equality Reality” Gala celebrates courage and those who choose it, honouring Virginia Roberts Giuffre, Gisèle Pelicot and Caroline Darian


6 min read


Press Releases


United States


New York, 22 October 2026 –

Last night in New York City, global leaders, activists, and artists gathered in a celebration of courage and the power of legal reform at Equality Now’s

2026 Make Equality Reality Gala

, held at Cipriani 25 Broadway.


The 15th annual event focused on choosing courage in a world where women’s and girls’ rights are being undermined, bringing together changemakers who use their voices, platforms and influence to stand side by side for equality, dignity and justice.


To a standing ovation, Gisèle Pelicot and her daughter Caroline Darian were presented with the Equality Now Trailblazer Award for their ongoing advocacy that has brought much-needed attention and action to the global reality of drug-facilitated sexual assault and consent. 


Mariska Hargitay honored Virginia Roberts Giuffre in a moving tribute to her profound legacy in challenging those in privilege who abuse their power. Giuffre’s brother and sister-in-law, Sky and Amanda Roberts, accepted the award, reflecting on the shared responsibility of achieving Virginia’s hope for a safer world for women and girls through Virginia’s Law.


Equality Now’s CEO

 S. Mona Sinha

 captured the evening’s spirit in her opening remarks, illuminating the connection between each honoree’s story, the urgent need for institutions to fully address sexual violence, including Cornell, and a call for legal reform if survivors are to find justice. Sinha applauded all who share their power to stand up for women and girls, saying,

“Use your influence. Open your networks. Invest your resources. Stand with survivors. Help us change the laws and institutions that have failed them.” 


Hosted by Joyelle Nicole Johnson, the program included performances by Tony Award-winning playwright, performer and activist 

Sarah Jones

, the Brooklyn-based band

Brass Queens

, and a

headline performance by pianist/composer/producer

Ray Angry

, accompanied by

Leah Rich

.


Sponsors included The Montag Family Foundation, Melony and Adam Lewis, the Kering Foundation, Britta Jacobson, the Sinha Family Fund, the Stardust Fund, Kimberly Agnew and Melony Lewis. The evening exceeded its fundraising goal, raising over

1 million

.


Guests included

Monica Lewinsky, Saara Chaudry, Amrit Kaur, Jackson Katz, Mohammadreza Eyni, Sara Khaki and Sheetal Sheeth.


About Equality Now


Equality Now is a worldwide human rights organization dedicated to securing the legal and systemic change needed to end discrimination against all women and girls. Since its inception in 1992, it has played a role in reforming more than 140 discriminatory laws globally, positively impacting the lives of hundreds of millions of women and girls, their communities and nations, both now and for generations to come. Working with partners at national, regional and global levels, Equality Now draws on deep legal expertise and a diverse range of social, political and cultural perspectives to continue to lead the way in steering, shaping and driving the change needed to achieve enduring gender equality, to the benefit of all.


About S. Mona Sinha, Chief Executive Officer, Equality Now


Mona Sinha is the Chief Executive Officer of Equality Now and a globally recognized advocate for gender equality, philanthropy and social change. In September 2026, she was inducted into the National Women’s Hall of Fame. The recognition reflects a lifetime of leadership advancing women’s rights and mobilising significant resources for gender equality. Her other honors include the Ellis Island Medal of Honor, the Smith College Medal, and recognition from Forbes and Apolitical for her leadership and impact.


For more information please contact: Monica Sheldon

monica.m.sheldon@gmail.com

.


For more information on the “Make Equality Reality Gala 2026”, please visit


www.equalitynow.org/gala

.

author: Archipelago Anarchist Archive
title: Pengarsipan Anarkis: Kritik & Kritik-Diri #1
content:
Belum selesai menghadapi permasalahan ekonomi yang bagai melempar api setitik ke padang ilalang itu, muncul permasalahan baru yang kini menghantui pengarsipan anarkis, permasalahan yang lebih halus dan bahkan tidak dipermasalahkan karena tidak tampak bermasalah di permukaan.

Kata-kata yang dicetak dan diterbitkan (atau bahkan yang tidak diterbitkan sekalipun), seperti buku, pamflet, leaflet, zine mendapat tempat yang signifikan di kalangan anarkis. Karena media tersebut terbukti mampu menyimpan berbagai pengalaman dan pemikiran banyak individu, yang bahkan dalam kasus tertentu, jika terdapat intervensi terhadap media cetak tersebut, eksistensinya akan tetap bertahan—untuk tidak menyebut abadi—lebih lama dari umur para individu yang mengalami pengalaman dan yang mencetuskan pemikiran tersebut. Dan individu-individu yang secara lengkap menyimpan kata-kata yang dicetak serta diterbitkan itu pun kemudian akan mendapatkan suatu manfaat, seperti dapat memiliki akses untuk melihat kembali “praktik untuk mencapai emansipasi” (gerakan dan perjuangan) yang terdahulu.

Itulah mengapa, menurut Baker (2023) ketika meneliti budaya tandingan—atau proses perubahan evolusioner—anarkis Spanyol, banyak perpustakaan anarkis dibangun untuk menyediakan akses terhadap koleksi lengkap kata-kata tercetak yang telah lama tidak diterbitkan kembali. Sayangnya, sejarah pertumbuhan budaya tandingan atau proses perubahan evolusioner anarkis ini tidak terjadi secara mulus atau bahkan macet di Indonesia. Karena Indonesia mengalami periode otoritarianisme—dalam artian paling kerasnya—yang berkepanjangan. Para anarkis tahun 1920-an habis dibuang ke Digul pasca pemberontakan 1926; sedangkan para individu berkecenderungan (anarkis-)sindikalis yang muncul pada tahun 1940-an disingkirkan secara paksa oleh rezim Orde Lama Karno dari pabrik-pabrik yang mereka swa-kelola dan disingkirkan secara perlahan dari arena pemikiran/intelektual oleh PKI; dan menjadi sama sekali tidak terlacak eksisensinya pasca genosida 1965 dan naiknya rezim Orde Bau Harto ke tampuk kekuasaan (Bima, 2018).

Walaupun, periode otoritarianisme berkepanjangan tersebut tidak khas dialami oleh para anarkis di Indonesia saja. Periode otoritarianisme keras yang berkepanjangan, yakni rezim Komunis Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej (1948-1965/17 tahun) dan Nicolae Ceaușescu, menjadikan para anarkis di Rumania dan di Indonesia memiliki—tanpa menafikan perbedaan dampak dari pasca-komunis di Rumania dan pasca-kolonial serta pasca-otoriter-militer di Indonesia yang menciptakan perbedaan yang kompleks—kesamaan dalam hal sejarah perkembangan budaya anarkis mereka. Karena ketika rezim komunis naik ke tampuk kekuasaan para anarkis disingkirkan mulai dari ditekan pergerakannya sampai dibunuh, dan sebagian yang hidup harus pergi mengasingkan diri ke luar negeri atau tetap di Rumania tetapi memilih untuk mengambil sikap tiarap total (Anarhiva, 2021). Situasi ini akhirnya, menurut Tataran (2026), membuat para anarkis yang bermunculan di Rumania pada masa-masa keruntuhan rezim komunis pada 1989 atau setelahnya, yang mayoritas bergerak di skena anarko-punk, hanya memiliki pengetahuan yang secuil atau bahkan tidak memiliki sama sekali pengetahuan tentang para anarkis yang eksis sebelum mereka, sehingga secara otomatis mereka tidak memiliki pengalaman kolektif yang dapat dijadikan rujukan ketika mereka menjalankan praktik anarkis/anti-otoritarian.

Sejalan dengan Adrian Tataran, Ucok (2026) dalam diskusi buku Unfinished Nation yang diselenggarakan di Perpustakaan Bunga di Tembok pun mengatakan hal yang nyaris sama. Menurutnya, sebelum buku Perang yang Tidak Akan Kita Menangkan karya Bima Satria Putra terbit—jauh setelah reformasi—pada tahun 2018, para anarkis yang bermunculan—dan sama seperti di Rumania, yang banyak pula bergerak di skena anarko-punk—saat masa-masa kejatuhan Harto beserta rezim Orde Baunya dan masa setelahnya tidak memiliki pengetahuan tentang gerakan anarkis terdahulu, sehingga sempat terbersit dalam pemikiran mereka kalau diri mereka adalah anarkis generasi pertama di Indonesia. Alhasil, tanpa pengalaman dan memori kolektif yang diwariskan dari para anarkis terdahulu, para anarkis yang hadir kemudian tersebut harus mulai membangun dari awal; berbanding terbalik dengan otoritarianisme yang walaupun dikatakan runtuh, mereka sudah memiliki birokrasi, struktur, militer, yang telah dibangun selama berdekade dan mapan serta siap diwariskan, sehingga bukan hal yang sulit untuk kembali ke tampuk kekuasaan …

author: Unknown
title: Ephéméride des luttes : 23 octobre
content:
Dans l'éphéméride des luttes du 23 octobre, on hésite entre grève insurrectionnelle et changement de méthodes. Mais ce qui est sûr, c'est qu'on se rend encore une fois bien compte du rôle contre-révolutionnaire du Parti Communiste.


1886 :

 A Bruxelles, parution du premier numéro du journal communiste-anarchiste "La Liberté".


1905 :

 A Ekaterinoslav, en Russie, la police tire sur les ouvriers grévistes de l'usine Briansk, faisant trois blessés. Un chef de l'usine sera abattu le 26 mars 1907 en représailles par l'anarchiste Mezhenniy.


1915 :

 A New York, 33.000 femmes marchent sur la Cinquième Avenue pour exiger leur droit de vote.


1921 :

 Dans toute l'Europe, des manifestations massives ont lieu en soutien aux anarchistes italiens Sacco et Vanzetti, menacés d'être condamnés à mort aux Etats-Unis.


1956 :

 En Hongrie, grève générale insurrectionnelle :

"interdite puis autorisée par le gouvernement, la manifestation rassemble en fin d'après-midi 100 à 150 mille manifestants, étudiante au départ, elle se grossit à partir de 17 heures des ouvriers qui sortent des usines.


20 heures : le gros de la manifestation reste place du Gouvernement, réclamant le retour de Nagy au gouvernement ; une partie des manifestants se rend au monument Staline, la statue est abattue, une délégation se rend au palais de la radio pour faire lire les résolutions.


Refus de la radio qui est gardée par 5 à 600 AVH (police politique) ; vers 23 heures la police politique ouvre le feu sur les manifestants qui essaient de pénétrer dans le palais de la radio, des unités de l'armée hongroise envoyées en renfort se laissent désarmer par les manifestants ou passent de leur côté ; des ouvriers retournent vers les usines où les équipes de nuit arrêtent le travail et s'emparent des dépôts d'armes de la milice ouvrière et des stocks des usines d'armement ; un peu partout dans Budapest, des combats s'engagent contre la police politique

".

Repris de la chronologie des événements publiés dans "

Socialisme ou Barbarie

,

L'insurrection Hongroise

".


Cette insurrection ouvrière sera sauvagement réprimée par le pouvoir soviétique dès le 4 novembre à l'aide de chars d'assaut. Le Parti Communiste Français se déclare favorable à la répression. Le numéro de Socialisme ou barbarie contient notamment un "questionnaire" aux membres du PCF qui critique très durement le parti et est assez drôle à lire.


1977 :

 - A Milan, la colonne Walter Alasia des Brigades Rouges tire huit coups de pistolet dans les jambes du conseiller communal de la Démocratie Chrétienne (le parti au pouvoir depuis l'après-guerre) Carlo Vincezo Arienti.


 En France, le journal 'Libération' est occupé par 150 autonomes suite à la prise de position du journal vis-à-vis des prisonnier-e-s de la Fraction Armée Rouge (RAF) mort-e-s en prison quelques jours plus tôt.


1983 :

 - Dans toute l'Europe, de grandes manifestations antinucléaires ont lieu.


 A Beyrouth, un attentat a lieu contre les armées française et américaine, tuant 297 soldats.


1988 :

 En Italie, des prisonniers des Brigades Rouges écrivent dans un document que la période de la lutte armée est terminée.


2001 :

 En Irlande du Nord, l'IRA Provisoire commence le désarmement.


2014 :

 A Athènes, le cabinet médical d'un médecin membre du parti néonazi Aube Dorée est ravagé.


2016 :

 - A Calais, des affrontements ont lieu contre la police à quelques jours du début du démantèlement de la Jungle.


 A Brême en Allemagne, 18 véhicules de l'armée partent en fumée aux premières heures. Les dégâts sont estimés à près de 15 millions d'euros. Ce qui n'est pas sans rappeler l'incendie de 42 engins de l'armée à Dresde le

13 avril

 2009, ce qui avait été revendiqué par un groupe autonome antimilitariste.


Voir

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 23 octobre.

author: Unknown
title: Le sens de l'émeute / une émission de Minuit Décousu
content:
Pendant que l'ensemble du monde politique s'occupe à bomber son torse de facho, personne ne semble essayer de comprendre comment et pourquoi on arrive à avoir des dizaines de milliers de personnes qui cassent, brûlent et pillent des trucs dans tout le pays. Comment et pourquoi on a vu des émeutes historiques ce 17 octobre. Comment et pourquoi tous ces gens ont pris le risque d'être arrêté, emprisonné, blessé ou mutilé pour laisser éclater leurs colère.


Des plateaux télé aux réseaux sociaux, la figure fantasmé du casseur bas du front lobotomisé par

LFI

, l'ultragauche, les frères musulmans ou peut-être même les francs-maçons évacue la dimension politique de l'évènement. Pourtant rien que son ampleur montre bien qu'il se passe quelque chose qui dépasse à la fois le pilotage politique et le plaisir de taper dans une vitre ou une planche d'

OSB

. Alors comme d'habitude, on a décidé de faire chauffer nos micros pour s'y coller, cette semaine dans Minuit Décousu, on se demande ce qu'est le sens de la casse.


L'émission s'écoute sur notre

audioblog

, ici, et un peu partout en podcast. Bonne écoute

 

!


Minuit Décousu, c'est un fanzine radiophonique nocturne sur

Radio Canut

 (Lyon et alentours),

Radio Vassivière

 (Limousin) et

Cause Commune

 (Paris/

IDF

). Semaine après semaine pendant une heure, on en découd avec la nuit et on tire les fils de sons, de textes, d'archives et de voix qui s'entremêlent.

author: Unknown
title: Arnavutluk: Öğrenci isyanı dinmiyor; akademisyenler boykotta, Başbakan Rama'nın istifası isteniyor
content:
Başbakan Edi Rama'nın istifasını isteyen öğrenci hareketi, 10. gününde başkent Tiran'da parlamento ve başbakanlık binaları önünde gösterilerini sürdürdü. Üniversite öğrencileri ve liselilerin başlattığı protestolara akademisyenler, öğretmenler ve toplumun değişik kesimlerden Arnavutluk yurttaşları katılıyor.


Perşembe sabahı parlamento önünde toplanan göstericiler "İstifa!", "Rama hapse, Berisha hapse!" ve "Bizi temsil etmiyorsunuz!" sloganları attı. Meclis içinde iktidar ve muhalefet milletvekilleri arasında sert tartışmalar yaşandı; oturuma ara verildi.


Öğleden sonra Başbakanlık binasına yürüyen öğrencilerin sayısı akşam saatlerinde arttı. News24, öğrencilerin 24 Ekim Cumartesi günü ülke çapında yeni bir gösteri çağrısı yaptığını duyurdu.


Sosyalist Parti lideri Edi Rama, 2013'ten beri iktidarda. Mayıs 2025 seçimlerinde dördüncü dönemini kazanan Rama, istifa çağrılarına kulak asmıyor. Göstericiler ise mevcut siyasi düzenin değiştirilmesini istiyor.


Akademisyenlerden süresiz boykot


Arnavutluk Üniversite Çalışanları Sendikası (SPUSH), 20 Ekim'de aldığı kararla 21 Ekim'den başlayarak bütün devlet üniversitelerinde süresiz ders boykotu ilan etti. 


Sendika, yayımladığı açıklamayla öğrencilere yönelik polis müdahalelerinin durdurulmasını, olayların bağımsız biçimde soruşturulmasını ve öğrencilerin taleplerinin karşılanmasını istedi: 


"Öğrencilerimiz sokaklarda dövülürken öğretim üyeleri hiçbir şey olmamış gibi derslerine devam edemez."


Akademisyenler, boykot nedeniyle yapılamayan derslerin daha sonra telafi edileceğini belirtti. Rektörlüklere de protestolara katılan öğrenciler ve akademisyenler hakkında disiplin işlemi yapılmaması çağrısında bulundu.


Öğretim üyeleri her sabah saat 10.00'da Tiran Politeknik Üniversitesi önünde toplanıp gösterilere katılıyor. Perşembe günkü yürüyüşte "Öğrencilere dokunmayın!" ve "Öğrenciler yalnız değil!" pankartları taşındı.


Üniversite sendikasının boykot kararının bütün devlet üniversitelerini kapsaması hedefleniyor; ancak her bir üniversitedeki fiilî katılımın hangi düzeyde olduğuna ilişkin henüz yeterli bilgi yok. 


Öğretim üyeleri geçici hükümet istiyor


Akademisyenlerin 19 Ekim'de yayımladıkları bir başka açıklamada Rama'nın istifası ve bir geçici hükümet kurulması istendi.


Siyasi Diyalog Forumu aracılığıyla yayımlanan bildiride, öğrencilere yönelik şiddet kınandı. Polis görevlilerine hukuka aykırı emirleri uygulamama, yurttaşlara ise öğrencilerle dayanışma çağrısı yapıldı.


Öğretim üyeleri, 1991'de Arnavutluk'ta tek parti yönetiminin sona ermesinde önemli rol oynayan öğrenci hareketini hatırlatarak şöyle seslendi:


"Üniversite amfilerinde biz önderiz; bugün meydanda öğrenciler, bizim önderimiz."


Bildiride göstericilerden kamuya ve özel kişilere ait mülklere zarar vermemeleri de istendi. Akademisyenler, bu tür eylemlerin hükümet tarafından polis müdahalelerini gerekçelendirmek için kullanıldığını savundu.


Perşembe günü Emekli Polisler Derneği (SHPPL-2013) de bir açıklama yayımlayarak polislerin protestoculara karşı orantısız güç kullandığı iddialarına dikkat çekti.


Dernek, görevdeki polisleri hukuka uygun davranmaya çağırdı:


"Hiçbir emir, baskı ya da siyasi çıkar hukukun üzerinde olamaz!"


Dernek üyelerini 24 Ekim'deki gösteride gençlerle dayanışmaya çağırdı.


"Diplomalarımız göç pasaportundan başka bir şey değil"


13 Ekim'de Eğitim Bakanlığı önünde yeniden başlayan protestoların başlıca talepleri arasında eğitimin niteliğinin yükseltilmesi, üniversite yurtlarının iyileştirilmesi, eğitim masraflarının azaltılması ve gençlere iş sağlanması yer alıyordu.


Tiran'daki Tıp, Hukuk, İktisat ve Politeknik fakültelerinden öğrencilerin yanı sıra Elbasan'daki Aleksandër Xhuvani Üniversitesi öğrencileri ve bazı liseliler de ders boykotlarına katıldı.


13 Ekim gösterisinde Citizens.al'a konuşan üniversite öğrencisi Redjan Shkëmbi, yurtlardaki koşulları eleştirerek şöyle dedi:


"Üniversitelerimizden aldığımız diplomalar, bir göç pasaportundan başka bir şey değil."


Öğrenci Laura Kërtalli ise hareketin yalnızca eğitim kurumlarındaki sorunlarla sınırlı olmadığını belirtti. Kërtalli, hükümetle pazarlığa karşı çıkarak 2018'deki öğrenci protestolarını hatırlattı:


"Bu sistemle ve Rama-Berisha partiler üstü klanıyla müzakere edilemeyeceğini biliyoruz."


Öğrencilerin hem iktidardaki Sosyalist Parti'yi hem de eski Başbakan Sali Berisha'nın liderliğindeki Demokrat Parti'yi hedef alan sloganları, protestolarda geleneksel siyasi partilere yönelik tepkinin …

author: ACG
title: CITIZENSHIP LAWS IN IRELAND
content:
The coalition government in the south of Ireland is proposing to change the rules surrounding citizenship. At the moment it takes 5 years to become a naturalised citizen. The intention of Minister for Justice, Home Affairs and Migration James O’Callaghan, is that it will require 8 years. In addition, you can’t have had welfare payments in the last 2 years of that period. Plus you need to show you have a certain level of ability in Irish or English. Let’s look at what is driving these revisions.


The change seems to come out of nowhere. One of  O’Callaghan’s explicitly declared reasons for the modification of the law is a technical one. He says that Ireland is an outlier in European Union (EU) terms and should be brought into line with EU norms. He cited Germany as an example of a country that requires an 8 year wait. The trouble is, this is just factually not true. Germany actually reduced its requirements from 8 to 5 years in 2024 (https://www.bmi.bund.de/SharedDocs/kurzmeldungen/EN/2024/06/mod-staatsangehoerigkeitsrecht.html).


 In reality, there are a variety of conditions across the EU. Twelve of the 27 member states have a standard residence requirement of five years for naturalisation, according to a report published in 2025 by the Robert Schuman Centre for Advanced Studies (https://globalcit.eu/new-globalcit-study-compares-conditions-for-citizenship-acquisition-by-immigrants-and-their-descendants/).


Another argument employed was that the changes “…seek to ensure that citizenship reflects a demonstrated, durable connection to Ireland, knowledge of the state and its institutions, and a sustained commitment to participation in Irish society” (Dublin People, 7/10/26). Even if you accepted the desirability of these qualities, how can such vague and subjective things be adequately measured? We are expected to believe that 5 years would not prove a durable connection or a commitment to participation in “Irish society” but 8 years has magically achieved that? It is really just an arbitrary number.


There is clearly more at work behind the scenes. One possible reason for the adjustment is the current Taoiseach/Leader of the Government Michael Martin is seen as vulnerable on his Right flank and O’Callaghan senses an opportunity to look tough as part of a future bid to depose him. So in that aspect, socially vulnerable sectors of society are being used as pawns in an elite power game.


Besides the personally ambitious dimension, there’s also the ideological one of using immigrants as a red herring or scapegoat for failures of the system. By putting pressure on relative newcomers, longer term residents and those born on the island are expected to divert attention towards those supposedly less worthy than themselves. It’s not big business, landlords and their friends in government who are to blame for the housing crisis, energy prices or the general cost of living. It’s Maria the cleaner and Pedro the kitchen hand who have been in Ireland ‘too long’ and need to be discouraged from staying. In other words, classic divide-and-rule.


The new amendments clearly have a class element to them. Imagine you have saved some money and decide to embark on a long journey to start a new life. You secure a job undertaking physical labour, probably one not many of the locals want to do. You work hard for 5 or 6 years. Then you have an accident or develop a disability. Or maybe you lose the job because a tanker is bottle-necked in a canal overseas or a madman running a rogue state starts a war against a small oil rich nation causing delays in supply lines, an increase in prices and lay offs. Or perhaps AI and the development of robots means employers are less reliant on human labour. Any number of reasons beyond your control could cause you difficulty. You’ve paid taxes. You apply for welfare support. Great, don’t expect citizenship now. It’s your own fault, you foreign parasite.


A common phenomenon is one where as an immigrant you take a job that makes it difficult for you socially. Its not uncommon to have a graveyard shift working alone or with fellow immigrants. Likewise you might have to live with people from a similar background. That’s either due to discrimination or lack of finances to take up other options. In reality, due to the cost of living you may actually have to take-on another job as well, just to get ahead. Somehow in such a schedule you have to find time for sleep and to become highly articulate in another …

title: Agricoltori e autotrasportatori campani: i blocchi e presidi continuano
content:
Come viene riportato da 

questo articolo

 su Altra Agricoltura, l’obiettivo della giornata di oggi per gli agricoltori campani era quello di portare la richiesta di dichiarazione dello stato di crisi all’attenzione della Regione:


“I due Coordinamenti territoriali della Campania della Confederazione Sindacale Altragricoltura, quelli di Campania Nord (Caserta, Napoli e Benevento) e quelli di Campania Sud (Salerno e Avellino) si mobilitano con due prime manifestazioni contro la crisi da giovedì 22 ottobre con due obiettivi: reiterare la richiesta fin qui inascoltata al Governo Nazionale e al Parlamento di dichiarare lo Stato di Crisi delle piccole e medie imprese dell’agroalimentare e del diritto al cibo per adottare un pacchetto di emergenza che scongiuri la chiusura delle aziende e quello di avviare un confronto con la Regione per istruire la declaratoria sullo stato di crisi dell’agroalimentare della Campania da inviare al Governo e attivare misure urgenti e un tavolo di confronto partecipato sulla crisi”.


Il governo intanto mostra il pugno duro, tramite identificazioni di massa ai blocchi in autostrada e procedimenti di indagine per verificare le supposizioni portate da Lollobrigida e Urso in merito a infiltrazioni mafiose nella protesta per screditarla. Nonostante questo i blocchi e i presidi vanno avanti e si allargano i settori coinvolti, come i panificatori e i pescatori. Oggi al vaglio del governo anche un decreto apposito. 


Gli scaffali dei supermercati sono vuoti e inizia a scarseggiare il diesel alla pompa, l’appello che giunge dagli agricoltori campani è quello di unire le lotte da Sud a Nord e continuare a mobilitarsi.

title: 3 ноября - День рождения антифашиста Юрия Михеева
content:
Ему исполнится 21 год. По сообщению проекта «Огни свободы», это его третий день рождения в неволе.

В ноябре 2023 года 18-летнего Михеева задержали на территории военной части в подмосковном Дмитрове по обвинению в подготовке поджога военной техники. В феврале 2025 года ему вынесли приговор - 7 лет лишения свободы по делу о «приготовлении к диверсии». Вместе с Юрием были осуждены братья Матвей и Тимофей Мельниковы, получившие 20 и 19 лет заключения соответственно.

До ареста Михеев жил в Лобне, учился в Дмитровском техникуме на тракториста-механика, занимался тхеквондо. Относит себя к SHARP (Skinhead Against Racial Prejudice - скинхеды против расовых предрассудков), которые противостоят расистам и неонацистам. Он не поддерживает российскую агрессию против Украины. Любит фэнтези и фантастику, интересуется археологией и историей.

title: Guerra alla guerra! Verso le mobilitazioni internazionaliste contro la guerra indette dalla CIT
content:
Siamo di fronte ad uno scenario di guerre in continua espansione, dall’Ucraina al genocidio palestinese, all’Iran e in tanti luoghi nel mondo. Guerre che stanno provocando migliaia e migliaia di morti, distruzione di intere città e interi territori, producendo una economia di guerra che è causa principale del peggioramento delle condizioni di lavoro e di vita delle classi lavoratrici e della parte più povera della popolazione.


Ormai tutti i governi parlano di prospettive di guerra, di aumento delle spese militari, di reintrodurre il servizio di leva militare per fornire carne da macello per i nuovi conflitti, di trasformazione di aziende civili in produzioni di armi per incentivare il commercio di una merce sempre più richiesta e che sta realizzando enormi profitti.


Tutto ciò ci sta portando verso il baratro di una terza guerra mondiale che potrebbe essere l’ultimo atto di autodistruzione dell’intera umanità, per le potenti armi distruttive in mano ai vari governi, se non riusciremo a fermare questa corsa suicida.


È in considerazione di tale quadro disastroso che all’interno della CIT (Confederazione Internazionale del Lavoro), su sollecitazione di USI, le varie organizzazioni anarcosindacaliste aderenti hanno deciso una mobilitazione contro la guerra, con uno sciopero generale internazionale nella giornata del 30 ottobre e con manifestazioni nella giornata del 31 ottobre. Come USI CIT ci siamo mossi già da giugno convocando per due volte le varie sigle del sindacalismo di base per allargare la partecipazione allo sciopero contro la guerra proposto dalla CIT. Abbiamo fatto presente che USI ha aderito a tutti gli scioperi unitari contro la guerra e che i contenuti dello sciopero proposto erano ampiamente condivisi dalle varie componenti in quanto obbiettivi di scioperi precedenti. Inoltre si trattava di uno sciopero internazionale per cui era stato indispensabile stabilire già una data concordata con le varie componenti sindacali dei vari paesi che compongono la CIT. Al primo incontro hanno partecipato Sgb e Sgc, mentre interesse è stato dimostrato dalla rappresentanza del SiCobas, nella loro prospettiva di uno sciopero generale contro l’introduzione della 146 nella logistica in quei settori dove c’era la presenza, anche parziale, di materiali deperibili.


A questo punto USI CIT aveva la necessità di proclamare lo sciopero per il 30 ottobre per occupare quella giornata prima che le norme restrittive sulla regolamentazione degli scioperi non la rendessero più praticabile. La piattaforma dello sciopero è la seguente: contro tutte le guerre, taglio delle spese militari, ritiro delle missioni militari all’estero, aumento dei salari, più spese per sanità, scuola, edilizia pubblica, stop militari nelle scuole, stop sfratti e affitti calmierati, no al petrolio causa di inquinamento e di guerre ma sviluppo delle energie alternative e pulite, stop genocidio del popolo palestinese. Una proclamazione di cui diversi organi d’informazione hanno dato notizia e lo stesso canale 1 della RAI ne ha dato l’annuncio.


Il 25 settembre è stato promosso da Cub, Sgb, AdL Varese un incontro del sindacalismo di base con la proposta di uno sciopero generale. Nella stessa giornata in cui si svolgeva il Congresso della CIT a Massenzatico. In quell’incontro la nostra proposta è stata quella di convogliare unitariamente nello sciopero generale del 30 ottobre, ma si è preferito convergere nella prima data utile per lo sciopero che, per la regolamentazione in materia, li ha portati a proclamarlo il 4 dicembre, contro la finanziaria.


Nel frattempo Usb, nell’ambito del coordinamento dei sindacati internazionali di cui fa parte, comunicava la decisione del blocco dei porti a livello internazionale, contro la guerra e il transito delle armi, nella stessa giornata del 30 ottobre, con l’adesione del sindacato ORSA di Gioia Tauro. In un secondo momento, il 6 ottobre, anche Usb proclamava lo sciopero generale nella giornata del 30 ottobre, con l’adesione del Cobas Poste Usb. Successivamente anche il Cobas Scuola Sardegna proclamava lo sciopero nella giornata del 30 ottobre. Nel momento in cui si scrive inoltre è arrivata la comunicazione che la CUB Sanità italiana ha aderito a livello nazionale con il settore pubblico e privato allo sciopero generale USI del 30 ottobre. title: Heilige Drecksarbeit – Die deutsch-israelischen Militärbeziehungen und die Staatsräson
content:
Der vorliegende Text ist eine gekürzte Fassung des gleichnamigen Beitrags aus dem Sammelband „

Trümmer auf Trümmer. Zur Kritik der deutschen Staatsräson

“, erschienen bei der Buchmacherei. Das Autor:innenkollektiv beschäftigt sich hier ausführlich mit der historischen Genese der militärischen Beziehungen zwischen der Bundesrepublik und dem zionistischen Staatsprojekt sowie der Geschichte des Existenzrechts Israels als deutsche Staatsräson. Neben diesem Beitrag finden sich im Sammelband zahlreiche weitere Texte, die sich aus historischer, juristischer und politischer Perspektive mit dem Thema der „Staatsräson“, deren Bedeutung für einen neuen deutschen Nationalismus, dem Phänomen der „Antideutschen“, kolonialen und antikommunistischen Kontinuitäten und der aktuellen Bedeutung im Bezug auf den Genozid in Gaza auseinander setzen.

von

AK Beau Séjour


Wirft man einen vergleichenden Blick auf die Zahlen der deutschen Waffengeschäfte im Jahr 2024, so fällt auf, dass Israel mit 161 Mio. Euro nur an sechster Stelle steht. An erster Stelle stand im Jahr 2024 die Ukraine mit 8,1 Milliarden Euro, gefolgt von Singapur (1,21 Mrd. Euro), Algerien (558,7 Mio. Euro), den USA (319,9 Mio. Euro) und der Türkei (230,8 Mio. Euro). Es gehe, so wird immer wieder zu Recht angemerkt, den Herren Rheinmetall und Thyssenkrupp nicht um die konkrete Tötung palästinensischer Kinder, sondern um das allgemeine Geschäft mit dem Tod. Die militärischen Beziehungen zwischen Deutschland und Israel müssen, das ist fraglos richtig, auch als gewöhnliche deutsche Handelsbeziehungen zwischen handelsüblichen Schurkenstaaten betrachtet werden. Doch dieses profane globale Geschäft mit dem Tod braucht, insbesondere in Deutschland, einen robusteren Überbau als das Geschäft mit Autos oder Kosmetikartikeln. Laut Marx spricht die »scheinheilige und heuchlerische Ideologie der Bourgeoisie ihre aparten Interessen als allgemeine Interessen« aus.

1

 Und in Bezug auf Wirklichkeit und Ideologie der bürgerlichen Familie schreibt er weiter, dass »[i]hrer schmutzigen Existenz […] der heilige Begriff in offiziellen Redensarten und in der allgemeinen Heuchelei« entspricht.

2

 Die schmutzige wirkliche Existenz deutscher Außen- und Handelspolitik muss in vergleichbarer Weise sakralisiert und den Deutschen als ihr allgemeines und moralisches Interesse verkauft werden, insbesondere deshalb, da sich nach 1945 jedes deutsche Großmachtstreben verbot. Gerade hierbei spielt Israel eine zentrale Rolle. Die umfassende und bedingungslose Unterstützung Israels wird in einen Akt höchster Sakralität verwandelt – eine sakralisierte Beziehung, hinter der sich, wie noch zu zeigen ist, die aparten Interessen der deutschen Bourgeoisie verbergen.


Diese Sakralisierung staatlicher Gewalt drückt sich in zahlreichen Reden deutscher Politiker:innen aus. So verkündete Angela Merkel in ihrer berühmten Staatsräson-Rede von 2008: »Deutschland und Israel sind und bleiben – und zwar für immer – auf besondere Weise durch die Erinnerung an die Shoah verbunden«. Die ehemalige deutsche Außenministerin Annalena Baerbock leitete aus dieser Erinnerung zum ersten Jahrestag des 7. Oktober im deutschen Bundestag die Legitimität von Gewalt ab: »Die Sicherheit Israels ist deutsche Staatsräson, unabhängig davon wer regiert, unabhängig davon, wer Außenpolitik macht […] Das Selbstverteidigungsrecht Israels ist auch unsere Verantwortung. Dazu stehen wir nicht nur mit Worten, sondern auch mit Taten, und zwar jeden Tag.« Zwar gehören, so Baerbock, laut deutscher Staatsräson »das humanitäre Völkerrecht und das Existenzrecht Israels auf das Engste zusammen«, doch Selbstverteidigung bedeute selbst verständlich auch die vollständige Zerstörung des Gegners und »wenn sich Hamas-Terroristen hinter Menschen, hinter Schulen verschanzen, dann kommen wir in ganz schwierige Bereiche. Deswegen habe ich vor den Vereinten Nationen auch deutlich gemacht: Dann können auch zivile Orte ihren Schutzstatus verlieren; weil Terroristen diese missbrauchen. author: Mostafa Hosny
title: ‘Citizens’ health’ session at Egypt Forum 2026 boasts spending success with no mention of declining hospital bed numbers
content:
On Tuesday, the second day of Egypt Forum 2026, Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar described the political leadership’s support for the healthcare sector as unprecedented.


Speaking at the “citizen’s health”

session

 of Egypt Forum 2026, he said the approach dated back to the beginning of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s presidency in 2014, when, he

said,

 Egypt faced a massive “disease burden,” with a lack of data and years of inadequate budget allocations that had failed to meet developmental ambitions for the system, particularly as population growth accelerated.


The minister said the state’s development plan had delivered gains in the sector, citing 16 presidential initiatives that had benefited 95 million citizens at a cost of LE44 billion. 


Abdel Ghaffar stressed that success in healthcare should not be measured by spending levels, but by the results citizens ultimately experience.


Mada Masr looked into some of those results, drawing from government

data

 published by the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS).


One clear result over the time period is the notable decline in the number of beds in public hospitals between 2013 and 2024, with a drop from around 98,291 to 84,225. 


Over the same period, the number of beds in private hospitals rose from 26,009 to 36,014. 


Still, the combined total of beds in public and private hospitals fell from 124,300 in 2013 to 120,239 in 2024.


While Abdel Ghaffar portrayed inadequate budget allocations as a problem of the past, the state

has consistently fallen short

 of the constitutionally mandated minimum for healthcare spending.

 Article 18 of the Constitution requires the state to allocate at least three percent of gross national product to public healthcare starting in FY 2016/17 and gradually increase spending over time. The state has not met this threshold since the Constitution was adopted in 2014. Since then, healthcare spending has not exceeded 1.7 percent of GNP in most years.


The government allocated 1.51 percent of GNP to healthcare in the current fiscal year’s budget, half the constitutional minimum. 


Meanwhile, the government has

introduced

 a different method for calculating budget allocations that allows it to claim it is meeting the minimum spending threshold.

 


Rather than using its previous classification, which was based on the Health Ministry’s expenditure, the government now uses a “broader and more comprehensive” definition. Under this new definition, healthcare expenditure also encompasses spending by a number of off-budget economic authorities and companies as well as “any other entities providing healthcare services, such as police and military hospitals, Al-Azhar hospitals, the comprehensive health insurance system and its associated programs,” a Finance Ministry source previously told Mada Masr. Without publicly available data on these entities’ healthcare spending, it is impossible to verify whether they bring total annual healthcare spending to the constitutionally mandated minimum.


The same expansion of what constitutes annual “health spending” also allows the government to include the budgetary allocation for these entities’ debt repayments as investment in the sector, according to the same source.


The president

confessed

 three years ago that the state is not meeting the constitutional requirements, saying in a public address that “the required numbers aren’t available, folks.”

 His comment came days after the government’s assertion that it was meeting the required spending levels.


Aside from its commentary on expenditure, the government’s Egypt Forum 2026 also highlighted the Universal Health Insurance System, one of the leading presidential health initiatives.


Egypt’s Healthcare Authority head, Ahmed al-Sobky,

described

 the system as a comprehensive reform of Egypt’s healthcare sector, capping an “enormous leap forward” under Sisi, following earlier historic transformations under King Fouad I and former President Gamal Abdel Nasser.


Shortly before the forum, the government began promoting the second phase of the Universal Health Insurance System, launching a pilot phase in Minya Governorate. 


The first phase launch in the governorates of Port Said, Ismailia, Suez, South Sinai, Luxor and Aswan began in 2018 and was

completed

 in 2025.

 


Sobky said the system had achieved its objectives by strengthening social justice and reducing poverty by lowering …

author: Moussa Traoure
title: The Palace Guard Against the Trenches : What the Mutiny in Niamey Revealed
content:
The mutiny that broke out in

air base 101 in Niamey

 in the night of 29 August 2026 failed. The real question now is to understand why it took place. Those who took up arms against General Abdourahamane Tiani were young soldiers from the front lines, those who fought the ‘jihadists.’ For all of the Sahel, it’s a much more worrying sign than any plot from the army high command.


Until Saturday morning, fighting took place in the Nigerien capital near to Diori Hamani airport, the presidential palace, and the public television channel RTN.

Loyalists retook control only with the support of the Russian Africa Corps

.

The state television broadcast

 the live arrest of several tens of soldiers being arrested, most of them extremely young.


Three juntas, one promise


In Mali, in Burkina Faso, and in Niger, soldiers took power putting forward the same argument: civilian leaders had failed in front of the ‘jihadists,’ and the army would now do better. Assimi Goïta carried out two coups in Mali in 2020 and 2021. Ibrahim Traoré took control of Burkina Faso in September 2022 and overturned another putschist, Paul-Henri Damiba. Tiani deposed President Mohamed Bazoum in July 2023.


The French were asked to leave, and the Russians invited to come in. The three countries concerned founded the Alliance of Sahel States and

withdrew from ECOWAS in January 2025

. Each then solidified its grip on power through legislation. In Mali,

political parties were banned in 2025

, and the leadership was granted a

five-year renewable term in office

—without elections.

Until 2030, Tiani will remain president of the transition

. In Burkina Faso,

all political parties were dissolved in January 2026

, clearing the way for the regime to consolidate control.


The promised security, however, never materialised. This gap between promises and actions has fuelled anger—an anger that is now festering in the barracks.


Two armies in one


Niger effectively has two armies

: the Presidential Guard, and everyone else. Tiani commanded the Guard for twelve years; since the coup, it has received the best equipment and the most secure and comfortable postings. Meanwhile, regular units stationed in the southwest and along the Nier’s borders are losing personnel in the fight against the Islamic State in the Sahel and the al-Qaeda-linked JNIM.


According to observers, it is these soldiers who have mutinied. US researcher

Alex Thurston

 that most accounts align: regardless of infighting at the top, it is the anger of the rank-and-file that has driven the revolt.

Paul Melly, of Chatham House

, aptly summari the sentiment among young officers: three years ago, things seemed to be improving; today, the opposite is true.


When dealing with generals, a regime can either negotiate or simply swap out loyalists for other trusted figures. But for soldiers suffering from a lack of ammunition and reinforcements, a reshuffle within the high command changes nothing.


Niamey, Niger.


How the juntas protect themselves


The first pillar: the purges. In Mali, following a

reported coup attempt in August 2025

, two generals and more than fifty military personnel were arrested. At the end of December,

a decree mandated the forced retirement

 of several high-ranking officers, including the former intelligence chief. In Burkina Faso, after a plot was uncovered in January 2026, Damiba—identified by Ouagadougou as one of the organizers—

was extradited to Togo

. Tiani has taken a more cautious approach: on 11 September,

he replaced Chief of Staff Moussa Salaou Barmou with Mamane Sani Kiaou

. Former Defense Minister

Kalla Moutari has been arrested

, and former RFI journalist

Moussa Kaka

 has been shot. According to Thurston, this reaction suggests that

Tiani does not wish to appear fearful

.


The second pillar is the law. With political parties banned and terms of office extended, the opposition has no remaining legal path to power.


The third pillar is an external protector.

Between 200 and 300 fighters

 from the Russian African Corps are stationed in Niger, with their headquarters located south of Base 101. Russian Ambassador

Viktor Voropaev maintains that Niamey merely requested assistance

. According to Thurston,

the Algerian air force also provided support

 to the loyalists. For the first time, forces tasked with fighting jihadists have openly opened fire on soldiers from the very countries that employ them.


Does a failed coup …

author: Mzi Velapi
title: Austerity under fire as Godongwana pauses fuel levies and low-cost housing
content:
Residents, activists, members of trade unions and civil society groups took to the streets of Cape Town earlier today against budget cuts. This was before the Medium Term Budget Policy Statement was delivered by the Minister of Finance, Enoch Godongwana. Led by Cry of the Xcluded, some of the protesters’ demands included the right to decent work, an end to exclusionary access to free basic services, an end to privatisation, an increase in health, education and policing, and an universal basic income amongst others.


Equal Education’s secretary general, Itumeleng Mothlabane said that the budget cuts in education have resulted in the existence of plain pit latrines in schools, overcrowded classrooms and learners having to walk on dangerous roads when they go to school.


“We reject a budget that continues to deprioritise the education of a poor black learner. We demand an increase in the allocation that is given to each and every learner. We demand an increase in the school infrastructure budget in Limpopo, KwaZulu-Natal, the Eastern Cape and all the rural provinces,” Mothlabane said.


Lusanda Dyan from Rural Women’s Assembly said they are calling for the allocation of land to women and youth in rural areas and funding of centres that offer assistance to victims of gender-based violence in the rural areas. “Give us 2 hectares of land, seeds and access to water and we will feed this country,” she said.


The protesters also demanded land with water redistribution, and for the government to deal with the housing backlog.


Member of the Movement for Change and Social Justice, Lindiwe Mvandaba said the austerity measures that are implemented by the government are a political choice. “We reject the R370 SRD [social relief of distress] grant because it is not enough for us to feed ourselves and families,” she said.


Speaking to

Elitsha

, SRD grant recipient, Bernice Benjamin from De Doorns said that she is only able to buy bread, electricity and a few toiletries with the R370 that she receives. Benjamin is currently unemployed and gets support from her parents who receive an old age grant. “My R370 and my parents’ old age pensions only allow us to buy food for two weeks. For the rest of the month, we have to buy food on the book [credit] and we have to get loans for electricity and other stuff that we need. If you borrow R100, you must return it as R150,” she said.


Another SRD grant recipient from Ceres, Wendy Samson said that her R370 is enough to pay her municipal bill only. “We demand that the grant be increased,” she said.


Protesters called for an end to budget cuts because of their negative effect on the poor. Photo by Mzi Velapi


The South African Communist Party leader in the Western Cape and former provincial legislature member for the African National Congress, Benson Ngqentsu told the crowd that the aim of the budget cuts is to hollow the capacity of state entities so that the government can privatise them. “All police stations in this province and around the country do not have enough detectives and police vehicles,” Ngqentsu complained. He was a member of the standing committee on police oversight in the Western Cape legislature.


“We know that Godongwana will announce neo-liberal policies in local government in order to pave the way for privatisation. We therefore say no to the auctioning of solid waste, and water and sanitation departments,” he said.


Cosatu and Saftu united


Zwelinzima Vavi, the general secretary of the South African Federation of Trade Unions (Saftu), called for unity between the federation and the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu). Vavi shared the stage with the newly elected president of Cosatu, Mike Shingange.


“I want to propose that we have a meeting now in October and next month with Cosatu that will result in a joint 77 notice to the government and inform them that in February next year, during the budget speech, all workers in the Western Cape and around the country, will demand an end to austerity measures and we say voetsek Godongwana,” Vavi said.


Shingange said that the next austerity protest in February should lead to a national shutdown. “Workers have no luxury to be divided because of the badge on their T-shirt or colour of their T-shirt. The enemy knows no name of the union, colour or badge. They only know exploitation and will exploit workers irrespective of the union they belong to,” he said.

author: Tosin Durodola
title: Deported to Liberia, again
content:
In 1816, a group of white people in the US created the

American Society for Colonizing the Free People of Color of the United States

 (later simply the American Colonization Society), aimed at resolving the “problem” of a growing population of free black people in the country. Both slave owners, fearing that large numbers of free black people would lead to slave uprisings, and some white abolitionists, who viewed their presence as either a security threat or a barrier to emancipation, joined hands in a plan to quite literally deport free black Americans and freed slaves to a settlement they hoped to create in the African motherland. 

This is the origin story of the African state of Liberia, one where race, racism, and anti-black slavery meet yet another type of forced movement: deportation. And in a continuum with centuries past, the African continent, which had solved a problem of lack of (free) labor for white US elites and landowners, now solved yet another perceived problem for their descendants: a population of free black people they considered undesirable. As Jonathan Ort

has shown

, today’s deportation system revives that colonial blueprint.

A little more than 200 years later, an overwhelmingly white US executive power again uses Liberian territory as a deposit for its undesirables, with one difference: the constructed enemy deported from the white nation is another racialized figure, the immigrant. The US has

historically applied a racialized migratory policy

, restricting on racial and class grounds those welcomed into the nation while profiting from the cheap undocumented labor those restrictions produce. Many of these workers are non-white immigrants from Latin America, a pattern shaped by geographical proximity and by a long

US imperial presence in the region

. Continuous political and economic interventions have fueled conflicts, generalized violence, and socioeconomic chaos in Latin America while enriching the US, and those fleeing have formed a cheap workforce in the north as temporary laborers, undocumented workers, and asylum seekers. However,

migrants have become the scapegoats

 for everything that challenges the US’s self-perception of “greatness.” And while the US has long detained and returned Latin Americans, the current government has not only entered

a new era of interventions in the region

 but also further escalated forced returns.

Thus far, the second Trump administration (Trump 2.0) has signed largely secretive bilateral agreements for (forced) returns with at least 35 countries, overwhelmingly in the Global South. Migrants, including asylum seekers and people whom US judges have protected from return to their home countries, are the bargaining chips in these unequal agreements. Partner countries end up taking part in one of the cruelest return practices the US has used: removing people with almost no warning and little chance of defense to countries where they have no ties and may face inhuman treatment or torture, as

UN human rights experts warned

 in September.

In a chilling roundabout way, Liberia once again becomes a place where unwanted deportees arrive on its shores, with little to no say in the matter, and with no medium-term plan for their protection and well-being, or that of local communities. On August 18, 2026,

Liberia’s government announced

 that it would accept up to 1,200 third-country nationals, one of the largest agreements struck by Trump 2.0. Two days later, about 20 people landed at Roberts International Airport;

14 stayed

, from Cameroon, Eritrea, Venezuela, Honduras, Colombia, Brazil, and Guatemala. Most had won US court protection against return to their home countries because they faced persecution or torture there, and

some only learned their destination mid-flight

. None of the Latin Americans interviewed wants to remain in Liberia. Housed in a hotel and fed by the

International Organization for Migration

, free to apply for asylum but unable to work, they have been

separated from their families

 and long for a safe place with ties, a shared language, the right to work, and a community. Is Liberia that place? And what does their arrival mean for Liberians?

The imbalance of power between Liberia and the US is part of the answer. In June 2025, a State Department memo

placed Liberia among 36 countries

 facing a possible US travel ban and suggested accepting deportees as a way out. Washington had already
