author: Girard Mariano Lopez
title: Taipei Grand Mosque Board Faces Eviction Threat, Sparking Protests
content:
A DISPUTE OVER control of the Taipei Grand Mosque has spilled into protest after court enforcement against its board’s bank funds—raising concerns about donations, charitable services, and management of the historic religious site.

Dozens of Muslims from more than 10 countries gathered outside the Chinese Muslim Association’s office on October 16th. Organizers said demonstrations would continue every Friday after prayers until association leaders publicly addressed their concerns.

Yaser Cheng, chairman of the Taipei Grand Mosque Foundation, said the dispute threatened resources supporting a congregation that includes migrant workers and international students.

“They took the money from us,” Cheng said in an interview, describing funds he said included small donations from Indonesian workers and other worshippers. “It’s not from our board pocket.”

The Chinese Muslim Association, or CMA, has yet to respond to requests for an interview.

The conflict centers on competing claims over property rights and the authority to manage the mosque, which opened in 1960 and became a Taipei municipal historic monument in 1999. It remains a place of worship and a gathering point for Taiwan’s international Muslim community.

Cheng said the foundation had managed the mosque continuously for 66 years and should retain responsibility for its operations. He argued that its longstanding work gave it experience essential to maintaining religious services and community activities.

An analysis of court and banking documents supplied by Cheng supports a court-enforced collection of NT2,835,977 dollars from the foundation’s funds on September 24th, including a NT250 dollar fee. The bank transactions reconcile with the amount authorized in a Sept. 17 court order.

Cheng described the financial demands as rent and interest, saying the charging of interest was upsetting to worshippers because of Islam’s prohibition on riba (interest).

The documents, however, do not provide an itemized breakdown establishing how much of the collection represented rent, judgment interest, or other charges.

The mosque’s board put the broader financial impact at NT9.4 million dollars, including NT6.5 million that it said was frozen. Cheng explained that although the bank note does not reflect the freeze, they still cannot use it nor do they know how much more the CMA will take from the amount.

Records also list NT$7.5 million in remaining fixed deposits as of Oct. 1, but do not establish whether all those funds were accessible.

Cheng said financial pressure had curtailed assistance for poor people and plans to purchase cemetery land. However, he said the foundation would retain its employees despite the strain, describing its staffing resources as already limited.

He also accused the opposing institution of using financial pressure to force the board out. The documents establish that funds were collected through court enforcement but do not independently establish that motive or wrongdoing by either institution.

The documents include a September 2023 order requiring the foundation to vacate and return the mosque building. They do not establish that an eviction occurred or clarify the present status of proceedings concerning possession.

The property dispute stems partly from arrangements involving former landowner Chia Hsin Cement and the city’s efforts to preserve the mosque.

Cheng alleges that former mosque chairman Ma Chao-yen arranged for property rights to benefit the opposing foundation without proper board authorization.

But TaiSounds reported in January that prosecutors declined to indict Ma for breach of trust, finding insufficient grounds for prosecution over the arrangements. That decision did not resolve every separate civil or governance issue.

In earlier reporting by Taiwan’s Central News Agency’s Indonesian service, an unnamed representative of the opposing foundation said worship would continue and characterized disputed payments as tax-related.

For worshippers, uncertainty extends beyond the courtroom.

Raja Ramadhana, an Indonesian doctoral student at National Taiwan University of Science and Technology, said the dispute complicated his understanding of whom to approach when organizing community activities.

He said he usually worked with the mosque foundation but wanted the association to explain its position before drawing conclusions.

“For now, the information is so imbalanced,” Ramadhana said.

title: De la porte de Maricarmen à la Puerta del Sol
content:
Le 23 septembre dernier à Madrid, Maria del Carmen Abascal, 87 ans, était expulsée de son logement. Le 7 octobre, elle mourait sans avoir pu regagner l'appartement où elle avait vécu pendant près de soixante-dix ans. Son décès a déclenché une vague de manifestations autour du logement dans toute l'Espagne.


Le 23 septembre, l'huissier de justice et la Policía Nacional étaient convoqués pour procéder à l'expulsion de Maricarmen de son logement, dans le quartier madrilène d'El Retiro. C'était la quatrième tentative ; les trois précédentes avaient échoué grâce à la pression et au travail du Sindicato de Inquilinas de Madrid

 [

1

]

, qui avait organisé la défense du logement contre Urbagesa, un groupe d'investissement immobilier spécialisé dans les achats dits « con bicho dentro »

 [

2

]

. En clair : acheter à bas prix un bien avec son locataire à l'intérieur, destiné à être expulsé sur ordre d'un juge qui fera respecter le sacro-saint droit de propriété privée et l'Empire de la Loi.


À première vue, rien d'extraordinaire : une expulsion de plus parmi celles qui ont constitué le visage le plus visible du cycle ouvert par la crise de 2008. Selon le CGPJ

 [

3

]

, entre 2013 et 2025, 627 421 expulsions ont été exécutées dans l'ensemble de l'État espagnol, avec une part toujours plus importante des impayés de loyer par rapport aux défauts de remboursement des prêts immobiliers, dans un pays où l'accession à la propriété a été une affaire d'État — rappelons la formule du ministre phalangiste José Luis Arrese, qui voulait « un pays de propriétaires, pas de prolétaires »

 [

4

]

 — et presque une norme sociale.


Pourtant, l'expulsion de Maricarmen avait quelque chose de particulier : elle a réussi à canaliser l'exaspération latente d'une partie de la société espagnole face à l'inertie du « gouvernement le plus progressiste de l'histoire »

 [

5

]

 en matière de régulation du marché du logement.


Cette exaspération a des racines structurelles. Les loyers ont atteint des niveaux exorbitants dans les grands centres urbains, sous l'effet, notamment, du tourisme et de la dépendance des générations les plus âgées aux revenus locatifs pour maintenir leur niveau de vie, dans un contexte de bas salaires et de pensions insuffisantes. La loi adoptée en 2023

 [

6

]

 s'est révélée clairement insuffisante pour freiner cette escalade et les expulsions. L'étau se resserre même autour des jeunes qui aspirent à rejoindre les classes moyennes et occupent un emploi public dans les grandes villes, en entravant leur reproduction sociale, sans parler de la quasi-impossibilité, pour le prolétariat migrant, d'accéder à la propriété.


La veille au soir, en prévision de l'arrivée de la police, convoquée pour le lendemain matin, de nombreuses personnes ont passé la nuit sous tente devant la porte de Maricarmen. Parmi elles, on a vu une bonne partie de la crème de la crème de la gauche espagnole : musiciens d'hier et d'aujourd'hui, humoristes, animateurices de podcasts… La stratégie d'organisation et de communication du Sindicato de Inquilinas a poussé beaucoup de personnes à se sentir appelées à engager leur corps, ce jour-là, pour empêcher l'expulsion. Elle a obtenu davantage encore : déplacer le récit politique et médiatique du cadrage droitier de l'« invasion » marocaine de Ceuta

 [

7

]

 et de la crise migratoire, qui avait dominé l'été, vers la question du logement.


Après une manifestation en soirée qui s'est achevée devant un appartement de luxe au dernier étage, acheté par la Communauté de Madrid pour la modique somme de 6,3 millions d'euros et qui, selon des indices de plus en plus nombreux, serait le domicile de la présidente de la région, des militants du Sindicato de Inquilinas, avec des membres d'autres collectifs de la ville, ont annoncé qu'ils planteraient leurs tentes à la Puerta del Sol. La Communauté de Madrid, c'est-à-dire le gouvernement régional présidé par Isabel Díaz Ayuso, est le bastion du Partido Popular, principal parti d'opposition au gouvernement central de gauche. Le choix du lieu n'était pas non plus anodin : le gouvernement régional siège à la Puerta del Sol, et c'est là qu'est née, en mai 2011, l'acampada du 15M

 [

8

]

.


En un peu moins d'une semaine, l'acampada de Madrid est passée de quelques dizaines de personnes à plus de 1 200 tentes, devenant un véritable espace d'expérimentation politique. Un microcosme singulier s'y est constitué : chaque jour, des assemblées du mouvement pour …

author: Dionne Phillips, Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Family moves into Nuxalk village site Nusq’lst for the first time in 164 years
content:
The cabin in the ancestral village of Nusq’lst.

Submitted photo


Nestled in the lush coastal temperate rainforest of the Bella Coola Valley sits the ancestral village of Nusq’lst.


The last time someone lived at the historic Nuxalk townsite was in

1862

, as people’s forced removal from their homelands and the devastating smallpox epidemic emptied many traditional villages.


Now, 164 years later, three generations of a family are calling Nusq’lst home again. 


Kmalsuuncw (Orden Mack) and his mother Nuskmata turned what was originally planned as a hand-built hunting cabin into a permanent family home when Kmalsuuncw became a new father.


Building the cabin quickly became a family project, with Kmalsuuncw receiving advice on its construction from cousins, uncles and other supporters.


“We’ve received a lot of community support, and honestly, that’s been a really driving feature as to why we kept on going for as long as we did,” he said in an interview with IndigiNews. 


Kmalsuuncw notes the site holds much of his family’s origin story. The village site’s name Nusq’lst was his grandfather — Nuskmata’s late father’s — name. 


In 2020, construction originally began with the intention of becoming a hunting cabin — but that goal soon changed as Kmalsuuncw found out he was going to be a father. He felt called to provide for his growing family with the food, safety and shelter found in and around their ancestral home. 


“Right when I found out that my wife Jessica was pregnant,” he recalled, “we had to turn it from a cabin to more of a home.”


They call their cabin “Qiqti’s House” (baby’s house), a reminder that they’re the first in generations to raise children there.


“We’re not building this place for us,” he said. “We’re building it for them.”


A sustainable home during a housing crisis


Kmalsuuncw — a member of the Xats̓úll First Natiion who also has ties to Nuxalk and Tŝilhqot’in communities — has made Q’umk’uts (Bella Coola) his home for the past seven years.


He traces the cabin’s impromptu beginnings to a family gathering in Nusq’lst around 2019.


In the midst of a local housing crisis, with few housing options available to community members, building a sustainable home on the Nusq’lst village site became increasingly important to Kmalsuuncw — which he began to see as his “responsibility” to build on Nuxalk territories.


Kmalsuuncw’s mother Nuskmata

told Coastal First Nations

 that some of the last ancestors to live at Nusq’lst were her great grandmother Mary Sampson and her sister, and “so it’s really about returning home and reclaiming that place.” 


While building the cabin his mom handled the logistics while he did the construction and carpentry. Without carpentry training, he learned quickly as he was “thrown in” to the experience throughout the process.


“That was something I kind of had to learn along the way,” he said.


He credits a family friend, Dean Mecham, as the one who taught him about the process of logging and using the wood for the cabin build process.


Kmalsuuncw noted how around 85 per cent of work on the house was done by hand, with help from an Alaskan mill — an attachment for chainsaws that helps cut logs into long boards from trees they felled for the cabin’s foundation.


Out of care for the land, Kmalsuuncw said they only cut the trees needed for the cabin site, leaving it surrounded by the forest.


“I feel so connected to this place,” he said, “because of the way that we made sure to leave it.”


Nusq’lst memorial pole.

Photo by Dionne Phillips


Nusq’lst memorial pole.

Photo by Dionne Phillips


A communal effort to build


The mother-and-son team didn’t build their home alone, however. 


More than 200 community members helped out on the project, becoming a sort of communal event, Kmalsuuncw said proudly.


Even at the beginning of the seven year process he was surprised at the support that quickly emerged from the hereditary leadership.


“Once they heard what we were doing after community events, we had full … unanimous support,” he said.


He also commented on the openness his family has had with the community on their plans which has created support for the cabin’s construction. 


“Everybody knows what we’re doing,” he said, “and they’ve all been really supportive.”


Even a trip to the store would turn into a community update session, as many locals have been interested in the progress from the start.


The cabin’s location has now become a gathering …

content:
Dossier


„

Seit Jahren werden wir durch steigende Immobilienpreise und Lebenshaltungskosten ausgebeutet. Wir arbeiten uns zu Tode und rackern uns ab, um mit unserem Gehalt bis zum Monatsende durchzukommen, die steigenden Kraftstoffpreise und die Grundausgaben zu bewältigen und unsere Wohnung nicht zu verlieren. Uns bleiben nur Schulden und Sorgen, während die Aussicht auf eine bessere Zukunft schwindet.

Coimbra bleibt nicht außen vor! Wir rufen alle dazu auf, sich am kommenden *Mittwoch (14.) ab 17:30 Uhr auf der Praça da República* zu einer Malaktion sowie zum Anbringen eines Transparents und anderer Materialien zu versammeln

author: Cecília Melo
title: Aluno da UFRN espancado em protesto envolvendo Girão: “Não tem alternativa senão a luta”
content:
Quando chegou na Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte (UFRN) no fim da tarde da segunda-feira (19), Henrique Neiva não sabia que terminaria o dia em um exame de corpo e delito, com hematomas pelo corpo e um dente fraturado. O estudante de 28 anos fez parte do grupo que tentou resistir ao avanço de um protesto organizado pelo perfil “Endireita RN” no grupo de WhatsApp “UFRN Anti Lula”, administrado pelo secretário do gabinete do deputado federal

General Girão

 (PL-RN), Allison Lobato. O parlamentar Girão esteve envolvido na ação junto à vereadora de Natal recentemente eleita deputada estadual Camila Araújo (PL-RN).


“Era pra ter quebrado mais uns três”, dizia uma mensagem no grupo, após o fim do protesto. “Apanhou pouco”, completava outro integrante, após as notícias de

agressões

 começarem a se popularizar na Grande Natal. A

Agência Pública

 teve acesso a mensagens trocadas no grupo administrado pelo secretário de gabinete do deputado da extrema direita. O caso foi registrado na 1ª Delegacia de Plantão da Polícia Civil.


A noite que não terminou


Henrique Neiva ainda estava em casa quando começou a ouvir um paredão automotivo reproduzindo: “Um caminho novo pra gente seguir. Agora é Flávio presidente”, parte da letra de um dos jingles do candidato à presidência pelo PL. Por volta das 17h, o universitário chegou à unidade de ensino, onde foi avisado que as aulas estavam sendo interrompidas e os estudantes, liberados, devido à aglomeração que se formava em frente à UFRN.


“Quando eu cheguei, já estava tendo violência, né? Eles já estavam xingando e instigando as pessoas a irem pra cima”, conta o estudante que disse ter acompanhado quando as ofensas passaram de verbais à físicas. “O que a gente tava fazendo era uma corrente humana, dizendo que daquele lado eles não passavam”, disse o estudante.


“Recua, fascista, recua”, gritavam alunos, como pode ser visto em vídeos divulgados nas redes sociais. Em outros registros, o deputado General Girão (PL), cercado por seguranças privados, aparece dizendo: “Avança, avança. Esse ambiente é meu também” e “muitos de vocês ficam na vadiagem vendendo drogas aqui dentro”, acusava.


Henrique conta que o portão do campus estava sendo fechado quando as agressões tiveram início. “Fui segurar o portão. E aí do outro lado a galera estava gritando, xingando e chamando para a violência. Quando eu saio com o meu celular para gravar quem é que estava fazendo isso eu levo um chute na perna. É nesse momento que eu vou atrás de quem me chutou e quando eu vou para cima sou agredido”, narrou o estudante que recebeu chutes e pontapés ao cair no chão, momento registrado em vídeos por colegas.


Após ser submetido por um exame de corpo de delito, Neiva foi para casa, mas não conseguiu dormir direito. “Eu estava sentindo dores e fiquei com uma angústia muito grande do que tinha acontecido, que eu tinha ido pra lá para ser agredido. Fiquei pensando que não vale de nada, né? Nada vai tirar as agressões que eu sofri”, conta. “É necessário ter responsabilização para que isso não volte a acontecer”, opina.


Estou me recuperando física e mentalmente, também temendo pela segurança, mas não tenho deixado esse medo me paralisar. Mesmo eu recebendo esses comentários de ódio nas minhas redes sociais, eu continuo seguindo a minha vida. […] Não acho que é o momento de parar. Eu acho que é na verdade um momento de intensificar, de a gente ocupar mais as ruas, de a gente disputar a consciência das pessoas, de a gente mostrar que não tem outra alternativa senão a luta política”


Henrique Neiva


estudante universitário.


Os lados da moeda


Em sua curta jornada política, Henrique Neiva já vivenciou lados opostos do espectro político e disse ter votado em Jair Bolsonaro em 2018, motivado pelo sentimento antipetista. Foi com a efervescência política de junho de 2013 que Neiva começou a se interessar por política. O jovem contou que começou a buscar na internet informações sobre o cenário político brasileiro, e foi quando teve contato com o pensamento liberal. Foi no MBL que Henrique começou sua trajetória na militância, e chegou a se candidatar a vereador de Natal pelo Novo, mas diz que o sentimento mudou durante o mandato de Bolsonaro.


“Eu vi que não era um governo que tava sendo feito para governar para todas as pessoas, era um governo feito de atacar as instituições públicas e aí essa desesperança começa e se amplifica em 2020”, avalia o jovem, que disse ter sentido na pandemia o divisor de …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "A Spark from the Cockroaches": Arundhati Roy on India's Youth Protests & Modi's Crackdown
content:
A court in India on Wednesday ordered the release of two leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party, the youth-led movement that has led historic waves of protests in India since the summer. Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were detained amid massive protests last week after they scaled a barricade to enter a site popular for protest, unfurled the national flag and called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Kumar oversaw the deletion of 130 million names from the voter rolls in India since June of last year. Opposition parties say those impacted are primarily Muslims and other minorities less likely to support the

BJP

, the Hindu nationalist ruling party of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.


“You have a deep and wide — an ideologically wide — historical culture of resistance in India,” says acclaimed writer and activist Arundhati Roy. At the same time, the Modi government “has three things in its playbook: One is false-flag attacks, two is engineering communal riots, and the third is massive repression. And I don’t think we’ve seen its hand yet.”

title: The Student Revolt in France Spreads
content:
from the

CrimethInc.

collective, 21/10/2026


Moving Forward with Rage and Solidarity


October 17 marked one of the fiercest days of mass protest in recent French history. Scenes of ferocious resistance unfolded throughout the day, not only in Paris but in

Bordeaux

,

Dijon

,

How did we get here? Courageous high school students

In this article, our correspondent from Paris explains the context behind the youth rebellion, tracks the movement’s growth over the two weeks leading up to October 17 and the government’s failed attempts to repress or to pacify it, and clarifies the stakes moving forward.

The stakes were high on this crucial day of action. It was critical to show massive solidarity with the high school students fighting like hell against the empty future looming on their horizon. The day presented an ideal opportunity to expand the scope of the current movement by joining forces to resist the authoritarian state power that has been growing stronger every day.


The following article provides further context and analysis to understand the current situation in France, along with reports on what went down in the streets over these last rebellious weeks.


Background: The

Banlieues

 and the Enemy Within


When governments or powerful institutions feel threatened, they often strive to reaffirm their authority by inventing scapegoats to hold responsible for all supposed misfortunes. By invoking the menace of an “enemy within,” politicians can shift blame for systemic problems that have resulted from their own actions onto a specific category of individuals. In France, the most common targets are the residents of the

banlieues

, the impoverished suburbs on the outskirts of Paris and other cities.


At the beginning of the student blockades, the movement remained limited to a handful of high schools in these Parisian suburbs. In response, President Emmanuel Macron and his ministers decided to react quickly and do everything in their power to silence this emerging wave of youth protest. Due to the location of the first blockades, authorities believed that they could act more freely and repress the unrest with impunity, since these specific territories have been targeted for generations by all government administrations across political lines.


The condition of the

neocolonial power

 that continues to exploit African territories. Consider the disastrous

oil project

corruption case

French governments and corporations have no scruples about extracting enormous wealth from African countries. This neocolonial pillaging fuels France’s position as the

seventh richest country

 in the world today, according to the IMF. Yet despite these astronomical profits, the nation refuses to address the problems facing its post-colonial population and their descendants within its national territory.

author: Amy Goodman
title: Albania Protests Escalate Over Corruption, Planned Kushner/Trump Luxury Resort
content:
Student-led anti-corruption and cost-of-living protests call for the prime minister’s resignation, among other demands.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Student-led anti-corruption and cost-of-living protests in Albania are calling for the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama, among other demands. Hundreds of injuries and arrests have been reported amid a violent police crackdown, along with widespread damage to public and private property. The student demands are an outgrowth of the “Flamingo Revolution,” which erupted earlier this year in opposition to a luxury resort being developed on the ecologically sensitive Sazan Island. The planned resort is backed by Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump, President Trump’s son-in-law and daughter, and has been fast-tracked by the Rama government.

“Students find no future in Albania,” says Bora Mema, a founding member of the left-wing political party Lëvizja Bashkë, about the motivations behind the burgeoning pro-democracy movement. “Many of us have to migrate because the only development model that the government proposes is to clean the toilets of the rich and the mafia in luxurious resorts, like the one that Trump and Kushner and the national oligarchs and mafia in Albania are constructing.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: In Albania, student-led anti-government protests have rocked the capital Tirana for more than a week, as thousands have taken to the streets to call for the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama. Last week, the Albanian Student Union called for strikes and demonstrations at the Ministry of Education to protest high tuition costs, poor university conditions, a lack of jobs, and corruption. At least half a million young Albanians have left the country over the last decade in search of better economic opportunities.

Initial protests have escalated into ongoing clashes with police, leading to hundreds of injuries and arrests, widespread damage to government buildings, street lights and private property. Riot police have deployed tear gas, water cannons, sound grenades and rubber bullets against the protesters. These are some of those protesters in their own words.

LULJETA KOLA: [translated] What does Albania want? It wants a revolution, a change, a complete overthrow of the system, because it can’t go on like this, because these people have become billionaires, superbillionaires, and there are very poor people here.

ULIKS SKENDERAJ: The economy, like education, healthcare, everything, has gone downhill since many years. Yeah, basically. But all of the — all of the politicians from both parties, the main parties, should be gone, basically. This is what the new generation wants.

NDERIME VLADI: For us to stop the protests, first of all, Edi Rama should resign, immediately. Like, at the second that he resigns, his whole Cabinet should resign. … They deserve prison for every corruption that they have done. They have done so many. I mean, I cannot begin to, like, count with my fingers what they have done with this country. The corruption is on levels unseen, unseen in any other state of the world.

ANJALI KAMAT: Albania’s protests first began in May, when environmentalists rallied against a luxury resort development on the ecologically sensitive Sazan Island. The project is backed by President Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and has been fast-tracked by the Albanian government. Protests against the development grew into what is known as the Flamingo movement, which has rallied against government corruption for months and has now been joined by students in this latest wave of unrest.

On Sunday, Prime Minister Edi Rama set up chairs outside Parliament in a symbolic gesture for dialogue. Protesters calling for his resignation later smashed the chairs. Rama is leader of the Socialist Party and has a majority in Parliament. He’s been in power for 13 years and has so far refused to resign. The next elections are scheduled for 2029. During a live stream on Sunday, Rama said protests could hurt Albania’s bid to join the European Union by 2030, and claimed protesters were linked to antifa.

author: Isaac Nellist
title: Residents rally against Inner West Council’s pro-developer plan
content:
About 300 people rallied outside the Inner West Council meeting at Ashfield Town Hall on October 20 to demand real consultation time and more information about its so-called Fairer Future Plan 2 (FFP2).

The Fairer Future Part 1’s rezoned large sections of the inner west for luxury high-rise apartments.

The rally was organised by No High Rise Lilyfield and supported by a range of community groups, including the Better Future Coalition, Leichhardt Matters, Save Marrickville, Save Dulwich Hill and Action for Public Housing.

Lucy Wynter from No High Rise Lilyfield said the Fairer Future plan is “ill-conceived, underdone, under-prepared, not explained to the public and the time we’ve had to digest it has been paltry”.

Wynter said that when FFP2 was announced, she started a WhatsApp group chat with neighbours and friends in Lilyfield. A few weeks later, there are 700 members of the group chat, “about 10% of the population of Lilyfield. That shows how much this matters to people.”

Lilyfield residents did not receive a notice about FFP2 until two weeks into the six-week consultation period and many have still not received any information at all.

“That means we can’t provide informed consent; we cannot provide feedback to a plan we don’t understand or have not seen,” Wynter said.

“We are ordinary mums and dads, and we think it's unfair to implement the biggest change in the history of the Inner West, on such a broad scale, without actually asking us.”

John Stamolis, a former independent councillor on Inner West Council, and a member of the Better Future Coalition, which includes resident action groups opposed to Fairer Future, told the protest that the Inner West is already one of the most-densely populated local government areas in the state.

He said it is wrong that there had been so little information, consultation or debate about the plan.

Kobi Shetty, Greens MP for Balmain, also spoke. “We are a closely connected community; we care about each other. They are proposing to remove heritage restrictions, to massively rezone our entire neighbourhood, including public housing estates that are only 15-years old.

“We know that it is not fair; it is not going to fix the housing crisis.

“We’ve seen what happens when developers get their hands on the most affordable places in our communities … they demolish those and create luxury housing.”

The crowd then entered the chambers to address and observe the meeting.

Under pressure, Labor Mayor Darcy Byrne had attempted to neutralise residents’ anger about the proposal by offering an extra week of consultation — but only for the suburb of Lilyfield. He promised a number of concessions to reduce the increased density in the area.

Speakers at the council forum questioned why only Lilyfield had been granted an extension, arguing that the consultation period should be extended to all of the Inner West.

A motion to extend consultation to February to allow residents to better understand the plans and make submissions was put by Greens Councillor Liz Atkins and seconded by independent Councillor Victor Macri. It was voted down by the Labor majority, 8–7.

Byrne was noticeably absent from the meeting while residents outlined their concerns. He later suggested that only “activists and socialists” opposed the plan, disregarding the concerns of many community groups.

[The deadline for submissions is October 28. Isaac Nellist is the Socialist Alliance candidate for Balmain in the NSW elections.]

author: Olly Haynes
title: Why France’s Student Protesters Won’t Back Down
content:
On Sunday in Paris, crowds filled the major squares and thoroughfares of Place de La Republique, Boulevard de Magenta and beyond. Flares were lit and the flags of France, Palestine, political parties and unions adorned the crowd. In one placard, a hand drawn Homer Simpson told President Macron that disturbances in 2019 and 2023 were just the worst protests of his life “so far”, indicating that the movement does not intend to lie down easily.


Students have been on the march or blockading their schools since 17 September, but this time they were joined by trade unionists and yellow vest protesters supporting student demands, protesting against the rising cost of living and rejecting the upcoming austerity budget. Anything between 550,000 (according to the interior ministry) and 800,000 people (according to the unions) took to the streets across the country.


The convergence of different movements that have erupted under the Macron presidency could be heard in the songs and chants of the crowd. There was “on est la” (“we are here”) the defiant song of the “yellow vest” movement, chants of free Palestine, as well as adapted versions of songs against Macron’s pension reform which were recycled to apply to education.


While the majority of the protests have occurred peacefully since the movement began, there have also been dramatic clashes with police. Violence has largely characterised the police response so far. A rubber bullet and tear gas left two students blinded. A grenade left one with a severed hand and a tear gas canister fired directly into a 15-year-old’s face left him with a broken jaw. Thousands of people have been arrested, the majority of whom are minors.


Many have questioned the police tactics and their role in escalating the disorder. On Sunday in Paris, a youth orchestra formed to promote climate justice was tear-gassed in the middle of a rehearsal at Place de La République, setting the stage for the square to become the site of pitched battles between police, protesters and rioters for the rest of the day. Shops on the square had their windows smashed in and cars were burned by “casseurs” (vandals) who used the protests as an event to fight the police.


Instances of violence and looting have accompanied the protests, though often not from students – according to figures released by the Justice Ministry,

the majority of those arrested following the looting on 17 October

 were adults, in contrast to the arrests at previous protests. There have also been sporadic arson attempts at certain schools, and instances of violence. Generally – but with some exceptions – these have not come from the students at the schools in question, but young people who had come from outside.


‘Bismillah, c’est les tenebres.’


On Boulevard de Magenta, just off Place de la Republique, placards and slogans drew attention to a variety of demands and grievances ranging from the lack of teachers in schools, the suffocating heat of classrooms during the June heatwaves and the police violence.


A placard with a drawing of a chicken read “plus de masters, moin du poulet” (“more masters, less chicken”) – referring to the moral panic that occurred earlier this year about youth from the banlieue eating at fastfood chicken joints like Master Poulet.


“Watch your hands” read another, depicting a police grenade.


A recurring theme was the phrase “bismillah, c’est les tenebres” (“In the name of God, it’s the darkness”). The phrase doesn’t really mean anything, but it has become a ubiquitous meme. The phrase was mockingly reclaimed by protesters after it was allegedly used by police in a cack-handed attempt to mimic North African youth slang during an infiltration of protest groups on Snapchat. (One placard translated as: “bismillah, we want the name of the author of the punchline of the century”, referring to how widespread the meme has become.)


A placard at a student protest in Paris on Sunday. Photo: Olly Haynes


Novara Media spoke to several student protesters about why they were protesting and where the movement goes next. In France, the media usually does not print the surnames of minors, so accordingly all the students only gave their first names.


Camille and Nathan, both 17, from the Lycée Gabriel Fauré in Paris’s 13th arrondissement, have been blockading their high school for two weeks.


Camille described their school as “your average high school, not the least well off, but not rich either”.


Nathan said he wanted …

author: LCM-Redaktion
title: Die Menschen scheinen jeden Tag mehr zu erwachen – Interview zu den Protesten in Albanien
content:
„I’m busy at the moment will write in the evening”

schreibt mir mein Genosse aus Tirana als ich ihn nach einem Lagebericht frage. Dazu schickt er ein Foto von brennenden Barrikaden und einer Straße, in der mehr Pflastersteine herumfliegen als Merz Haare auf dem Kopf hat. Ich schaue aufs Foto und denke mir, das könnte genauso gut Lyon, Marseille, Brüssel oder Madrid sein. In Europa brennt es also wieder an verschiedenen Stellen. Doch was ist da in Albanien los?


Um mehr Einblicke zu bekommen, frage ich Sokol aus Tirana. Sokol Hazizi ist 43 Jahre alt und arbeitet seit über 20 Jahren als Architekt. Der Genozid in Gaza brachte ihn dazu, sich den Protesten anzuschließen und sich zu organisieren. Erst für ein Ende des Krieges in Gaza und die Befreiung Palästinas und nach und nach auch darüber hinaus:

„Ich hab angefangen mich auch stärker für unsere Innenpolitik zu interessieren, denn durch diesen Konflikt bekam ich irgendwie einen umfassenderen Blick auf die Welt und darauf, wie alles miteinander verbunden ist.“


Nun ist er seit Tag Eins Teil der aktuellen Proteste.


Danke Sokol, für die Möglichkeit für das Interview. Hier in Deutschland berichten die Medien fast ausschließlich von „brutaler Gewalt auf den Straßen Albaniens“. Kannst du uns einen kurzen Überblick darüber geben, was dort derzeit tatsächlich vor sich geht?


Es ist brutal, es ist sehr schlimm. Es ist beängstigend, das mit anzusehen. Jetzt begann es so richtig am 13. Oktober. Ich sah, wie die Steine vor mir durch die Luft flogen. Und sofort setzte die Polizei Wasserwerfer, Tränengas und Pfefferspray ein.


Und dann diese schiere Gewalt – mit Schlagstöcken und Tritten gegen die Jugendlichen, bis sie auf den Boden liegen. Es ist Gewalt in jeder Form. Und was mir im Vergleich zu anderen Ausschreitungen, die ich in Europa gesehen habe, am meisten auffällt, ist, wie unprofessionell das Ganze ablief. Es war chaotisch, die Polizei war sehr unorganisiert und ging sehr brutal gegen die Jugendlichen vor. Und dann, nach dem Ende der ersten Zusammenstöße war die Polizei dann überall auf den Straßen präsent.


Ein Problem ist auch die Zivilpolizei, da ihre Handlungen nicht nachvollziehbar sind. Sie tragen keine Dienstmarken. Sie geben nicht bekannt, zu welcher Einheit sie gehören.


Sie greifen einfach zu, oder fordern die Menschen auf, sich zu zerstreuen, und fangen dann an, sie zu schlagen.


Und es geht nicht nur um Gewalt, sondern auch um Einschüchterung, Was sie jetzt schon tun, ist im Grunde eine Ausgangssperre, es ist keine offizielle Ausgangssperre, aber man weiß: Wenn man nachts rausgeht, werden Polizisten oder Beamte in Zivil einen aufspüren, verprügeln, wahrscheinlich zur Polizeiwache bringen, und dort bleibt man dann mindestens über Nacht. Das sind keine Dinge, die ich mir ausdenke. Das sind Berichte, vor allem von Jugendlichen.


Und auch im vermeintlich kleinem: Als ich mein Kind in den Kindergarten brachte und auf dem Rückweg nach Hause war, sah ich vor dem Partizani-Gymnasium dutzende Polizisten, die dafür sorgen sollten, dass die Schüler das Gebäude nicht verlassen konnten, um sich den Protesten anzuschließen. Und das war so gegen neun Uhr morgens. Aber ich glaube, das kam den Jugendlichen zugute, denn sie sahen die dort postierten Polizisten und gingen daraufhin direkt zur Demonstration auf den Hauptplatz.


Wer ist da denn eigentlich auf der Straẞe? Wer steht hinter den Flamingo Protesten?


Ja das ist eine ganz schön gute Frage, denn das Flamingo als Symbol ist hier nicht bewusst entstanden. Der Flamingo war zwar ein Symbol, das schon in der Anfangszeit aufkam – ein Symbol, das den Kampf für die Natur und den Kampf für den Erhalt von Schutzgebieten verkörpert, nämlich das

Gebiet


Vjosa-Narta, in dem das Kushner-Resort

 gebaut werden soll. Dort sind ja unter anderem die Flamingos akut bedroht. Nach und nach hielt jemand in der Menge ein Schild hoch, auf dem „Flamingo-Revolution“ stand und es scheint, als hätten alle diesen Gedanken aufgegriffen. Seitdem dreht sich alles immer wieder um Flamingos, und ein Teil von uns ist dabei geblieben, weil es so schön war, was der Flamingo repräsentiert: die Farben, die Verletzlichkeit des Vogels, aber gleichzeitig auch die Eleganz und die Hartnäckigkeit eben dieses Vogels. Und ja, wir sind bei diesem Symbol geblieben.


Ich würde auch sagen, dass ich Teil der Bewegung bin. Aber es ist nicht so, dass „Die Flamingos“ eine feste Gruppe ist.


Unsere einzige Überzeugung war, dass diese Regierung weg muss. Sie …

author: A Melanie Lübbert
title: Baden-Württemberg: Kettensäge gegen Datenschutz
content:
Bild: Michael Fenton Unsplash-Lizenz; Bearbeitung: Digitalcourage

Wer in Baden-Württemberg wissen will, ob ein Unternehmen oder eine Behörde rechtmäßig mit personenbezogenen Daten umgeht, kann sich an den Landesbeauftragten für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit, Tobias Keber, wenden. Doch ausgerechnet seine Behörde soll massiv Personal verlieren.

Der Entwurf des Staatshaushaltsgesetzes 2027 sieht vor, bis zum Ende der Legislaturperiode (2029) 40 Prozent der Stellen abzubauen. Von derzeit 67,5 Stellen sollen 27 wegfallen. Übrig blieben gerade einmal 42 Planstellen. Für 2027 sind zunächst 5,5 Stellen zur Streichung vorgesehen; weitere Kürzungen sollen 2028 und 2029 folgen.

Eine inhaltliche Begründung für diesen drastischen Einschnitt liefert die grün-schwarze Landesregierung unter Ministerpräsident Cem Özdemir nicht. Auffällig ist zudem: Während für die übrige zentrale Verwaltung fünf Prozent Stellenabbau vorgesehen sind, soll die Datenschutzaufsicht 40 Prozent einsparen – eine achtmal so hohe Kürzungsquote.

Der geplante Kahlschlag steht in krassem Widerspruch zur Entwicklung der vergangenen Jahre. Seit die Datenschutz-Grundverordnung (DSGVO) 2018 wirksam wurde, hat sich die Arbeitsbelastung der Datenschutzaufsicht erheblich erhöht. Die Zahl der Beschwerden und gemeldeten Datenpannen ist massiv gestiegen. Zugleich werden Datenverarbeitungen immer komplexer und stellen die Behörde vor neue Herausforderungen.

Quelle: Tätigkeitsberichte des Landesbeauftragten für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit Baden-Württemberg. Auswertung: Redaktion Digitalcourage. [Grafik: padeluun, mit Hilfe von KI erstellt]

Die Zahlen verdeutlichen, wie stark sich die Aufgaben der Behörde verändert haben:

Beschwerden: Seit Einführung der DSGVO wenden sich deutlich mehr Menschen an die Datenschutzaufsicht. Neue Technologien und der zunehmende Einsatz Künstlicher Intelligenz schaffen zusätzliche Konfliktfelder. Im Jahr 2025 erreichte die Zahl der Beschwerden mit 7.673 einen neuen Höchststand – ein Anstieg um rund 90 Prozent gegenüber dem Vorjahr.

Datenpannen: Mit der DSGVO wurden die Meldepflichten bei Verletzungen des Schutzes personenbezogener Daten erheblich ausgeweitet. Für die Aufsichtsbehörde entstand dadurch ein umfangreiches zusätzliches Aufgabenfeld. Die Zahl der Meldungen stieg deutlich an und erreichte 2025 mit 4.059 einen neuen Höchstwert.

Beratungen: Die Einführung der DSGVO löste zunächst einen enormen Beratungsbedarf aus. Durch standardisierte Leitfäden, Orientierungshilfen und Online-Angebote der Datenschutzkonferenz sowie eigene Praxishilfen und Veranstaltungen konnte die Behörde viele wiederkehrende Fragen beantworten. Auch das Bildungszentrum des Landesbeauftragten übernimmt einen wichtigen Teil der Beratung. Inzwischen entstehen neue Aufgaben, insbesondere durch Künstliche Intelligenz und europäische Regelungen wie den Europäischen Gesundheitsdatenraum. Unternehmen, Behörden und Bürger.innen sind weiterhin auf die fachliche Unterstützung der Datenschutzaufsicht angewiesen.

Kontrollen: Die anlassunabhängigen Vor-Ort-Prüfungen wurden nach 2018 aufgrund begrenzter personeller Kapazitäten deutlich reduziert. Während der Corona-Pandemie waren zusätzliche Einschränkungen notwendig. Nach 2022 konnten die Kontrollen mit einer besseren Personalausstattung wieder intensiviert werden. Die geplanten Kürzungen drohen diese Entwicklung umzukehren.

Personalstellen: Seit Einführung der DSGVO verdoppelte der Landtag die Zahl der Personalstellen bis 2025 schrittweise auf den Höchststand von 67,5 Stellen. Zwischenzeitlich waren es mit befristet zugewiesenen Personalstellen 70,5 Stellen. Bis 2029 ist nun eine Reduzierung um rund 40 Prozent vorgesehen. Am Ende sollen nur noch 42 Planstellen verbleiben, während andere Landesbehörden fünf Prozent einsparen sollen.

Hinweis: In der linken primären Y-Achse finden sich aufsummiert die Ereignisse „Beschwerden, Datenpannen, Beratungen und Kontrollen“; in der rechten sekundären Y-Achse finden sich die Werte für Kontrollen und LfDI-Personalstellen.

Quelle: Tätigkeitsberichte des Landesbeauftragten für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit Baden-Württemberg. Auswertung: Redaktion Digitalcourage. [Grafik: padeluun, mit Hilfe von KI erstellt]

Dabei benötigt die Behörde nicht weniger, sondern mehr Personal. Landesdatenschutzbeauftragter Tobias Keber hat dem Landtag in seiner Stellungnahme zum Haushaltsentwurf dargelegt, dass für eine ordnungsgemäße Aufgabenerfüllung …

author: Τάσος Θεοφίλου
title: Υπερπληθυσμός στις φυλακές: παρακαλώ, σταματήστε να μιλάτε για τετραγωνικά μέτρα
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Υπερπληθυσμός στις φυλακές: παρακαλώ, σταματήστε να μιλάτε για τετραγωνικά μέτρα


Ο Elton Kalica, διδάκτορας στο Πανεπιστήμιο της Πάδοβα, με προσωπική εμπειρία πολύχρονης κράτησης στις ιταλικές φυλακές, είναι μεταξύ άλλων και ιδρυτής της «Ιταλικής Εγκληματολογίας των Κρατουμένων». Ανάμεσα στα ερευνητικά του πεδία είναι η Κριτική Εγκληματολογία, η Εθνογραφία των Φυλακών, η Εγκληματολογία των Κρατουμένων και ο Καταργητισμός. Από το 2002, είναι μέλος της συντακτικής επιτροπής του περιοδικού

Ristretti Orizzonti

.


Στο πλαίσιο της πλούσιας αρθρογραφίας του υπάρχει

και ένα άρθρο με τίτλο «Υπερπληθυσμός στις φυλακές: παρακαλώ, σταματήστε να μιλάτε για τετραγωνικά μέτρα»

 το οποίο αναφέρεται την κατάσταση των φυλακών στην γειτονική Ιταλία το όχι και τόσο μακρινό 2011. Καθώς είναι επίκαιρο λόγω της διαχρονικότητας του, τα κύρια σημεία του μπορούν τεθούν και στον δημόσιο λόγο για τις ελληνικές φυλακές.


Ο υπερπληθυσμός δεν είναι ένας απλός μαθηματικός υπολογισμός


Το κύριο επιχείρημα του Έλτον Καλίκα είναι, ότι η αναγωγή του προβλήματος του υπερπληθυσμού σε έναν απλό μαθηματικό υπολογισμό της ελάχιστης διαθέσιμης επιφάνειας για κάθε κρατούμενο θα μπορούσε να καταλήξει σε μια άκαρπη διακήρυξη δικαιωμάτων, αντί για μια πρακτική προσπάθεια εξεύρεσης κατάλληλων μέτρων για τη μείωση του κινδύνου υποτροπής.


Ως αφορμή για την ανάπτυξη του επιχειρήματος του, ο Καλίκα παίρνει τον θάνατο ενός κρατουμένου, ο οποίος πέθανε αφού προσπάθησε μάταια να πείσει τον γιατρό ότι είχε συμπτώματα καρδιακής προσβολής, η οποία τελικά τον σκότωσε στον ύπνο του.


«Όταν μιλάμε για υπερπληθυσμό, συζητάμε για τη σχέση μεταξύ του αριθμού των κρατουμένων και της επιφάνειας του κελιού που καταλαμβάνουν, ενώ αυτή η οπτική του υπερπληθυσμού κινδυνεύει να δώσει μια λανθασμένη εικόνα για το τι αποτελεί την πραγματική καταστροφή των σημερινών φυλακών. Ειδικά όταν μιλάμε για θανάτους…»


Ο κρατούμενος που πέθανε εκείνες τις ημέρες δεν ήταν θύμα της ελάχιστης επιφάνειας του κελιού που αναλογεί σε κάθε άτομο. Το ζήτημα είναι πιο περίπλοκο καθώς «το πραγματικό πρόβλημα δεν είναι τα τετραγωνικά μέτρα του κελιού που μειώνονται, αλλά το καθεστώς διαβίωσης που κρατά τους ανθρώπους ξαπλωμένους στα ράντζα τους για περισσότερες από είκοσι ώρες την ημέρα, η μονοτονία της καθημερινότητας που αποβλακώνει τους ανθρώπους και η έλλειψη δραστηριοτήτων».


Κάτι που επισημαίνει ο Καλικά στο άρθρο του είναι ότι η αύξηση του αριθμού των κρατουμένων ακολουθούν, κάθε χρόνο, επαναλαμβανόμενες περικοπές στα κονδύλια που προορίζονται για τις φυλακές. Και δεν ήταν δύσκολο να διαπιστώσει κανείς τις επιπτώσεις αυτού του δραματικού συνδυασμού σε θέματα υγιεινής, διατροφής, καθημερινής διαβίωσης, εκπαίδευσης και προγραμμάτων απεξάρτησης και κοινωνικής επανένταξης…


«Το πραγματικό πρόβλημα της φυλακής είναι τα άτομα με λιγότερα εφόδια, εκείνα που μένουν ξαπλωμένα στα κρεβάτια τους, συχνά γεμάτα ψυχοφάρμακα, απογοητευμένα να περιμένουν το χρόνο να περάσει, σε πραγματικά επισφαλείς σωματικές και ψυχικές συνθήκες. Και η φυλακή κάνει πραγματικά ελάχιστα γι’ αυτό, καθώς δεν υπάρχει κανείς που να αναζητά αυτούς τους ανθρώπους, να τους παρακολουθεί και να τους παρακινεί να βγουν από το κελί τους και να κάνουν κάτι χρήσιμο. Ως εκ τούτου, δημιουργείται σχεδόν φυσιολογικά ένας διαχωρισμός μεταξύ των λίγων που κάνουν πολλά -εργασία, σχολείο, μαθήματα- και των πολλών που δεν κάνουν τίποτα. Αυτό είναι και το πρόβλημα του υπερπληθυσμού».


Λίγα μέτρα από τις φυλακές της Πάδοβας στις οποίες αναφέρεται ο Καλίκα βρίσκεται το προανακριτικό κέντρο, όπου κρατούνται τα άτομα που περιμένουν τη δίκη τους. (Καθώς στη Ελλάδα δεν υπάρχει τέτοια διάκριση μπορούμε να φανταστούμε ότι πρόκειται για έναν τύπο φυλακής μεταξύ των φυλακών Κορυδαλλού και του Τμήματος Μεταγωγών).


Σύμφωνα με την μαρτυρία ενός συμπατριώτη του Καλικά, «οι μέρες περνούσαν ανάμεσα σε μακρές αναμονές για να πάμε στο ντους και αμήχανες σειρές για να μπορέσεις να χρησιμοποιήσεις το μπάνιο. Μέσα σε όλη αυτή την κίνηση ανθρώπων, μέσα σε εκείνο το ποτάμι αγωνίας, δεν υπήρχε χρόνος να σκεφτείς τίποτα. Δεν μπορούσες να επιτρέψεις στον εαυτό σου αδυναμίες και περισπασμούς, έπρεπε να είσαι δυνατός, ακόμα και όταν ένιωθες αδύναμος, έπρεπε να επιβιώσεις.


»Οι μήνες περνούσαν και κάθε μέρα έβλεπα ανθρώπους να τσακώνονται για το ντους, για τη σειρά στο μπάνιο, για το φαγητό, για το τηλεχειριστήριο ή για πολλά άλλα πράγματα που μπορεί να φαίνονται παράλογα σε πολλούς έξω από εκεί. Ήταν μια συνεχής σύγκρουση διαφορετικών …

author: Perseus
title: Αυτό το ζωντανό τίποτα που πετά στα τυφλά δακρυγόνο στο μετρό στην Ομόνοια ενσαρκώνει τη φράση του Χρυσοχοΐδη (Βίντεο)
content:
Αυτό το ζωντανό τίποτα που πετά στα τυφλά δακρυγόνο στο μετρό στην Ομόνοια ενσαρκώνει τη φράση του Χρυσοχοΐδη (Βίντεο)


Με βίαιη καταστολή ολοκληρώθηκε το πανεκπαιδευτικό συλλαλητήριο την Τετάρτη 21 Οκτώβρη 2026 στην Αθήνα, με τις αστυνομικές δυνάμεις καταστολής να εξαπολύουν επιθέσεις με χρήση χημικών και χειροβομβίδων κρότου-λάμψης κατά των διαδηλωτών.


Μάλιστα στα πλάνα που αναρτήθηκαν στο instagram από τον χρήστη pi_kappaa, αστυνομικός των ΜΑΤ πετά στα τυφλά δακρυγόνο μέσα στην είσοδο του σταθμού του μετρό στην Ομόνοια, εν ώρα λειτουργίας, με προφανή σκοπό να τραυματίσει όποιον ή όποια εισερχόταν ή εξερχόταν του σταθμού εκείνη τη στιγμή.


Σε μια επίδειξη προκλητικής αδιαφορίας, ο αστυνομικός εμφανίζεται στη συνέχεια να προβαίνει σε έναν ειρωνικό χαιρετισμό, περήφανος για την εγκληματική του πράξη μπροστά στις κάμερες των φωτορεπόρτερ και των δημοσιογράφων.


Το γεγονός ότι ο αστυνομικός ένιωσε ασφαλής να επιτεθεί έτσι, εν γνώσει του ότι καταγράφεται, αποκαλύπτει και κάτι χειρότερο: ότι δε φοβάται. Δε φοβάται οποιαδήποτε τιμωρία, αλλά υποδηλώνει μια βαθύτερη πεποίθηση ότι μπορεί να ενεργήσει, χωρίς συνέπειες. Αυτή η αίσθηση της ασυλίας είναι το πιο επικίνδυνο στοιχείο της συμπεριφοράς του, γιατί γνωρίζει πως το σύστημα σπάνια αγγίζει τους «δικούς του». Ίσα, ίσα κιόλας που κάθε τρεις και λίγο τον ανταμείβει με νέα επιδόματα. Αυτή η αίσθηση ατιμωρησίας και επιβράβευσης της

βίας

 αποτελεί το υπόβαθρο για την κλιμάκωση της αστυνομικής αγριότητας. Το συγκεκριμένο παράδειγμα ενός ακόμα περιστατικού αστυνομικής βίας, δεν είναι επιβολή της τάξης, αλλά εγκληματική βία στην πιο ξεκάθαρη μορφή της.


 


Το άλλο κρίσιμο ερώτημα όπως και κάθε φορά είναι: αφού δεν είναι όλοι οι αστυνομικοί ίδιοι, τι έκαναν οι συνάδελφοι του όταν είδαν να συμβαίνει αυτό;


 


Και τέλος, το πραγματικό ερώτημα, δεν είναι «ποιος και αν θα τιμωρηθεί», αλλά εμείς τι ανεχόμαστε. Γιατί όσο μένουμε σιωπηλοί, όσο μένουμε σιωπηλές, όσο το βίντεο παίζει για λίγα λεπτά στα social media κι έπειτα χάνεται μέσα στη ροή των ειδήσεων, τόσο θα βαθαίνει το ρήγμα στην αξιοπρέπεια μιας κοινωνίας που έχει πάψει να εξοργίζεται με αυτά που βλέπει, με αυτά που ζει, με την πραγματική απεικόνιση της φράσης Χρυσοχοϊδή “περνούν οι αστυνομικοί και ο κόσμος τους χειροκροτεί”.

author: Chris Walker
title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump Bid to Halt Care for Incarcerated Trans People
content:
The decision is a rare win for transgender rights at the conservative-leaning Supreme Court.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The U.S. Supreme Court has denied an emergency petition from the Trump administration, which sought a stay on a lower court’s injunction on a policy that would have denied gender-affirming care to federally incarcerated transgender people.

That policy was implemented by the Bureau of Prisons (BOP) after President Donald Trump signed an executive order in January 2025 that denied the existence of transgender people. The order also directed federal agencies to take steps that would be consistent with that view, and included specific instructions for the BOP.

“The Attorney General shall ensure that the Bureau of Prisons revises its policies concerning medical care to be consistent with this order, and shall ensure that no Federal funds are expended for any medical procedure, treatment, or drug for the purpose of conforming an inmate’s appearance to that of the opposite sex,” the order reads.

After the BOP conformed to the order, a group of incarcerated trans people who had been receiving gender-affirming care sued the administration. The group is being represented by the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), which argued that their Eighth Amendment protections against cruel and unusual punishment were being infringed upon.

A federal judge agreed, and, in August, ordered the policy to be blocked. The Trump administration challenged that finding, but the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit upheld it, prompting Solicitor General John Sauer to submit an emergency appeal to the Supreme Court.

The court has regularly ruled against transgender people, allowing state bans on trans athletes’ participation in sports, ruling in favor of a ban on transgender people in the military, and upholding state laws that bar gender-affirming care for trans children and teens. Yet on Wednesday, the court denied the Trump administration’s request.

“The application for stay presented to The Chief Justice and by him referred to the Court is denied,” the order read, giving no further explanation. Two justices for the court — Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas — would have granted the Trump administration’s request for a stay, the document said.

The ACLU heralded the high court’s denial of the emergency petition, stating, “This ruling affirms that federal prison officials can’t deny transgender people essential health care.”

Around 1,000 federally incarcerated trans people have also been diagnosed with gender dysphoria. The ruling means these individuals can continue receiving gender-affirming care while they remain in federal prisons or jails and the case moves forward in the lower courts.

This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

author: labor4pal
title: As More Unions Oppose ICE and Israel, the Right Is Cracking Down (Truthout)
content:
The right is trying to gain access to labor unions’ minutes, membership lists, and Zoom chats.By Blanca Missé , Truthout Published October 21, 2026

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

On September 22, The Free Press attacked the California Faculty Association (CFA), which represents about 29,000 faculty, librarians, counselors, and coaches across the California State University (CSU) system. Drawing on private discussions about a proposed Jewish caucus, including communications from a union Zoom meeting, the article accused CFA of antisemitism. How those communications reached the publication remains unclear. Two days later, the Jewish Journal amplified those allegations, urging Gov. Gavin Newsom to consider them as he weighed California Assembly Bill (AB) 2551, CFA-sponsored legislation challenging campus protest restrictions imposed after the 2024 Palestine solidarity encampments. Less than a week after The Free Press story was published, Newsom vetoed the bill.

Pro-Israel and Jewish advocacy organizations had already campaigned against AB 2551 before the union’s internal deliberations were targeted, arguing that greater scrutiny would weaken rules needed to protect Jewish students from harassment and intimidation. Newsom’s veto does not prove coordination, but the campaign portraying CFA as hostile to Jewish students had become entangled with the union’s fight against campus protest restrictions.

The CSU’s systemwide policy prohibits encampments, overnight demonstrations, and unauthorized structures. The CSU Academic Senate immediately condemned the restrictions as undermining academic freedom when it was instituted in 2024, while CFA warned that vague definitions of disruption threatened constitutionally protected speech, assembly, protest, and future strike activity. A major 2026 ACLU-Amnesty study, investigating 80 campuses over two years, documented sweeping repression of Palestine solidarity protests. As the report found, universities “have imposed sweeping restrictions on student speech, initiated disciplinary actions against students, and imposed severe punishments, including expulsions and suspensions.” The ACLU has insisted that even legitimate time, place, and manner restrictions “must leave ample room for students to express themselves.”

The controversy reaches beyond CFA and CSU. Unions and rank-and-file organizations committed to Palestine solidarity have been forced to relitigate, again and again, whether anti-Zionism and solidarity with Palestinians constitute antisemitism — and whether such organizing should be systematically policed, investigated, or surveilled. At stake is a more fundamental right of the exploited: Can workers democratically connect economic struggles with Palestine solidarity, resistance to anti-immigrant and anti-Black racism, and the defense of civil liberties without exposing their organizing and deliberations to external pressure or repression?

We already have a word for the use of legal process as a political weapon: lawfare. You do not necessarily have to win. Investigation, expense, compelled disclosure, and possible sanctions can exact their own price.

Call its media counterpart pressfare: leaked material, selective or doctored quotations, and public identification can turn people into political targets and invite pressure on employers, universities, or government agencies.

The leaked CFA meeting should not be adjudicated through fragments selected for publication, especially when CFA’s statewide record contradicts the portrayal of a union indifferent to antisemitism. During the 2024 encampments, CFA opposed antisemitism and Islamophobia “in all forms” while supporting the encampments. Amid a 2025 federal antisemitism investigation, it stated that “as CFA members, we are united against antisemitism; it has no place in our communities,” while defending members’ academic freedom. CFA’s Palestine, Arab, and Muslim Caucus likewise defines its mission as confronting racism “in all its manifestations,” explicitly including antisemitism. The Free Press story — a clear example of pressfare — sought to overwrite this legacy with weaponized accusations, undermining the trust that workers place in the sanctity of their union spaces and processes.

Antisemitism demands to be taken seriously — which is why accusations of anti-Jewish discrimination should not be …

author: admin
title: Latest Essay by Maksym Kryvosh (Plokhoi), Liberation Prisoner in Ukraine
content:
I was taken from my cell to a room to participate in a court hearing remotely, via video conference. The court was considering a petition from the prison guards to place me in solitary confinement for two months. (For the kleptocracy known as Ukraine, it wasn’t enough that I’ve been in solitary for seven years, or the 13-year sentence I was awarded for fighting for Justice; they also had to throw me into the punishment cell for periods ranging from 14 days to three months—bringing my total to 18 stints in the punishment cell over three years).

The judge was reading out the ruling, but I wasn’t listening anymore, nor was I looking at the monitor. I was looking at the window—a large moth was beating its wings against the glass. It was unclear how it had gotten there; the windows were sealed shut. I told the guards: I won’t go back to the cell until I set it free… It worked! Outside, I opened my palms; it was a Peacock butterfly—the most beautiful butterfly I had ever seen—its colors shimmering and mesmerizing in the sunlight. It felt at ease on my palm and didn’t want to fly away. For a whole minute, we were happy.

*** July 21, 2020, Lutsk, Ukraine: the “Anti-System Day” protest action; the president of a nation of forty million people fulfills my main demand—recording and publishing a video message titled “EVERYONE MUST WATCH THE FILM ‘EARTHLINGS’.” No one was hurt. (I don’t count). The result?! What did I achieve?

Let me quote two online publications; let facts and figures answer my question. “27,000 views in a single day—in the Ukrainian language alone.” This refers to the Wikipedia page for the film *Earthlings*. This means that millions of people across all languages viewed the page over the course of a few days. It means that some of them watched the film itself.

This is discussed in a second report titled “The Plokhoi Got His Way”: The film *Earthlings* saw a surge in global popularity thanks to the Lutsk “terrorist”… in a single day, search queries for the film within the Ukrainian segment of Google hit peak popularity—a score of 100… the movie became the most popular title on the KinoPoisk service. It climbed 4,265 places in the rankings in just 24 hours, achieving a rating of 8.7 based on 12,700 votes…

According to Google Trends data from the last day, interest in the film spiked in the USA, Canada, Brazil, most of Asia, and across the entire European Union (July 22, 2020, “Kommentarii COMMENTS.UA”). “Following the events involving the Lutsk terrorist, the film *Earthlings* saw record-breaking popularity on Wikipedia… The article, published in 2015, received three times fewer views over five years than it did in a single day—July 21…” (July 27, 2020, “Korotko Pro”)

Unfortunately, it is impossible to track statistics on how many people had their conscience regarding animals awakened by the “Lutsk terrorist”—people around the world who, after watching *Earthlings*, paused—even for a moment—to reflect on the Meaning of Life.

*** The “Anti-System Day” performance took place in Lutsk’s central square—Teatralna Square—near the monument to Lesya Ukrainka. She authored a philosophical parable-novella titled *The Butterfly*. It is a parable about the yearning for the light of true life, and the choice between a “safe” existence in the darkness of insignificance versus a dangerous life—a striving toward the light of Truth. “He sought the light”—that is how the novella ends. …about the life of a moth. Fitting words for an obituary, for an epitaph… A butterfly would not be a butterfly if it did not fly toward the flame that kills it. It flies to prove that DEATH DOES NOT EXIST. It flies to be resurrected as Truth.

So it is with man: he is not truly Human if perishing—being crucified—for the sake of Truth is not a source of happiness for him. By surrendering our mortal shell, we attain our immortal essence. The moth teaches us the wisdom of living each day—this very day—to the fullest. Of fearlessly celebrating Life in the here and now. The butterfly is a living Philosophy!

*** Anton Chekhov wrote: “With insects, a butterfly is born from a caterpillar, but with humans, it is the opposite: a caterpillar emerges from a butterfly.” We, “political animals,” arrive on this beautiful planet to be human—that is, beings possessing both the capacity and the duty to realize and give meaning to Life through All-Encompassing Love-and-Justice; yet, while we come here to be human, we exist and depart as something less than …

author: Blanca Missé
title: As More Unions Oppose ICE and Israel, the Right Is Cracking Down
content:
The right is trying to gain access to labor unions’ minutes, membership lists, and Zoom chats.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

On September 22, The Free Press attacked the California Faculty Association (CFA), which represents about 29,000 faculty, librarians, counselors, and coaches across the California State University (CSU) system. Drawing on private discussions about a proposed Jewish caucus, including communications from a union Zoom meeting, the article accused CFA of antisemitism. How those communications reached the publication remains unclear. Two days later, the Jewish Journal amplified those allegations, urging Gov. Gavin Newsom to consider them as he weighed California Assembly Bill (AB) 2551, CFA-sponsored legislation challenging campus protest restrictions imposed after the 2024 Palestine solidarity encampments. Less than a week after The Free Press story was published, Newsom vetoed the bill.

Pro-Israel and Jewish advocacy organizations had already campaigned against AB 2551 before the union’s internal deliberations were targeted, arguing that greater scrutiny would weaken rules needed to protect Jewish students from harassment and intimidation. Newsom’s veto does not prove coordination, but the campaign portraying CFA as hostile to Jewish students had become entangled with the union’s fight against campus protest restrictions.

The CSU’s systemwide policy prohibits encampments, overnight demonstrations, and unauthorized structures. The CSU Academic Senate immediately condemned the restrictions as undermining academic freedom when it was instituted in 2024, while CFA warned that vague definitions of disruption threatened constitutionally protected speech, assembly, protest, and future strike activity. A major 2026 ACLU-Amnesty study, investigating 80 campuses over two years, documented sweeping repression of Palestine solidarity protests. As the report found, universities “have imposed sweeping restrictions on student speech, initiated disciplinary actions against students, and imposed severe punishments, including expulsions and suspensions.” The ACLU has insisted that even legitimate time, place, and manner restrictions “must leave ample room for students to express themselves.”

The controversy reaches beyond CFA and CSU. Unions and rank-and-file organizations committed to Palestine solidarity have been forced to relitigate, again and again, whether anti-Zionism and solidarity with Palestinians constitute antisemitism — and whether such organizing should be systematically policed, investigated, or surveilled. At stake is a more fundamental right of the exploited: Can workers democratically connect economic struggles with Palestine solidarity, resistance to anti-immigrant and anti-Black racism, and the defense of civil liberties without exposing their organizing and deliberations to external pressure or repression?

We already have a word for the use of legal process as a political weapon: lawfare. You do not necessarily have to win. Investigation, expense, compelled disclosure, and possible sanctions can exact their own price.

Call its media counterpart pressfare: leaked material, selective or doctored quotations, and public identification can turn people into political targets and invite pressure on employers, universities, or government agencies.

The leaked CFA meeting should not be adjudicated through fragments selected for publication, especially when CFA’s statewide record contradicts the portrayal of a union indifferent to antisemitism. During the 2024 encampments, CFA opposed antisemitism and Islamophobia “in all forms” while supporting the encampments. Amid a 2025 federal antisemitism investigation, it stated that “as CFA members, we are united against antisemitism; it has no place in our communities,” while defending members’ academic freedom. CFA’s Palestine, Arab, and Muslim Caucus likewise defines its mission as confronting racism “in all its manifestations,” explicitly including antisemitism. The Free Press story — a clear example of pressfare — sought to overwrite this legacy with weaponized accusations, undermining the trust that workers place in the sanctity of their union spaces and processes.

Antisemitism demands to be taken seriously — which is why accusations of anti-Jewish discrimination should not be instrumentalized. Kenneth Stern, director of the Bard Center for the Study of Hate, has …

author: Franco Giandana Gigena
title: Openness in AI development: a path to long-term independence
content:
As concerns grow over

deepening dependencies

 on a handful of Big Tech companies and the

outsized influence

 of the U.S. and China, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk used his speech during July’s inaugural

Global Dialogue on AI Governance

 to call on humans to

“take back our agency”

 over AI. But what does agency over AI really mean? What policies and practices can allow people to shape AI in ways that respect, rather than undermine,

human rights

? 


This blog post unpacks concrete initiatives that show how openness in AI development can increase people’s agency over AI and advance the development of public interest technology. At the same time, we reflect on how openness is not the same thing as mere access, and how short-term pragmatism can pave the way toward long-term independence.


Why is AI development so concentrated? 


Last year, the UN formally established an

Independent International Scientific Panel on AI

, intended to “advance scientific understanding and ensure that international deliberations are informed by the best available evidence.” The panel’s

preliminary report

, published this past July, contained a stark warning about the concentration of AI capabilities in a small number of firms and countries, which it says “could enable authoritarian capture and undermine democratic accountability.” But how has this concentration of power come about? 


One of the main reasons is that

building

 a complete, multilayered “

AI stack

” is both an astronomical investment and a complex technical challenge. This technological stack comprises:


The hardware layer, which provides the computing power that AI demands, mainly via advanced chips known as graphics processing units, or GPUs; 


The data layer, used for training and post-training; 


The model layer, which consists of the models themselves, such as GPT-4 or Claude, and the tools to service them; 


And finally, the application layer, which is the interface that users interact with. 


Currently, the U.S. and China are the only two countries realistically capable of building a fully national version of the entire stack, where they build and control all necessary infrastructure within their borders. However, even then, they would continue to depend on other countries for some elements, whether that’s for sourcing the chips or the critical minerals used in the hardware layer. Meanwhile, most other countries’ reliance on U.S. or Chinese companies creates critical safety and accessibility vulnerabilities. 


However, all is not lost for other countries and regions that want to build agency across the stack. There are several parts in the AI stack — notably

the data, model, and application layers

 — where greater openness and geopolitical collaboration could help foster collective agency. In this way, we can work towards what Martin Tisné, founder and CEO of the Collaborative for AI in the Public Interest, calls a “

global, open, resilient, non-aligned stack

” adaptable to local needs. 


How does openness support greater agency over AI? 


When considering how to gain more agency over AI, it’s worth looking at the free and open source software (FOSS) movement; a longstanding and major driver pushing for increased agency over technology, from the software running the internet, to the tools millions of people rely on every day, such as the Firefox internet browser. Although definitions of FOSS vary from

source

 to

source

, the essential principle means ensuring that anyone can access a given technology’s source code, study how it works, modify it, and share modified or unmodified copies with others.


The Open Source Initiative (

OSI

) has already applied this in the context of AI, with their

open source AI definition (OSAID)

 according to which an open source AI system is one that enables four key freedoms:


Use

 the system for any purpose and without having to ask for permission.


Study

 how the system works and understand how its results were created.


Modify

 the system for any purpose, including to change its output.


Share

 the system for others to use with or without modifications, for any purpose.


None of the offerings from major AI tool providers, such as OpenAI or Anthropic, currently enable any of these freedoms. Until now, the overwhelming preference in AI development has been for closed systems, accessible only through online interfaces or

application programming interfaces (APIs)

. This …

author: EDRi
title: EDRi celebrates Global Encryption Day 2026
content:
On 21 October 2026, we celebrate the Global Encryption Day! Part of EDRi’s KISS campaign, we celebrate this day with our partners, online, in Brussels and in different European capitals.

On 21 October 2026, we celebrate the Global Encryption Day! Part of EDRi’s KISS campaign, we celebrate this day with our partners, online, in Brussels and in different European capitals.

A recent survey conducted by CDT Europe shows that across several European countries (France, Sweden, Poland, and Ireland), people consistently oppose measures that would compromise encrypted communication platforms. In France, 92% of respondents agree they have the right to have private conversations online, while the figure goes to 94% in Poland, 88% in Sweden and 93% in Ireland.

Encryption is great for protecting the way our messages travel on the internet. Through “end to end encryption”, anyone can make sure that the content of an online conversation can not be intruded upon, not even the server that facilitates the transmission.

This year, we have coordinated several campaign actions to celebrate encryption.

1. Raising awareness in European Capitals through LED “Encryption trucks” driving around Paris, Berlin and Dublin and a metro poster campaign in Prague.

To visibilise people’s support for encryption, we partnered with the Irish Council for Civil Liberties, Féministes contre le cyberharcèlement and Digitale Gesellschaft who are in the streets today, talking to people and press about the “Encryption trucks” and the importance of encryption. In Prague, our partner Iure has been supporting the Metro Posters campaign for the past weeks.

2. Working across silos with groups promoting gender justice, and sex workers rights in the digitalised society.

In the case of women defenders, land defenders from indigenous groups, racial justice activists, sex workers defenders and defenders of migrants, unsafe communications can have life or death consequences. For human rights defenders, secure and trusted communication is often a matter of physical safety and democratic organising.

For 21 October 2026, we have partnered with European Sex Workers Alliance and Féministes contre le cyberharcèlement (France) to raise awareness on the importance of safe and secure communications for sex workers as well as womens’ rights. Check ESWA’s Instagram video and

3. Visibilising the testimonials of activists from Privacy Camp and across Europe

During 14th edition of Privacy Camp gathering that happened recently in Brussels, EDRi asked a few participants why encryption mattered for them. The people we interviewed came from a variety of causes: those fighting for a healthy European civic space, and for digital rights in Netherlands, Portugal and Germany. More, we asked EDRi’s over 35.000 supporters why encryption mattered to them too. Their answers inspired us to post some of them, and we will post them during the next couple of weeks. Check the content on EDRi’s social media channels – on Instagram , Mastodon or LinkedIn.

4. Connecting with global experts to advocate for encryption

During the Global Encryption Summit taking place at 4pm CET, EDRi’s expert Chloé Berthélémy will join a panel in an event organised by Internet Society, the Center for Democracy and Technology, Mozilla, and Global Partners Digital.

Europol and law enforcement are pushing to legalise hacking methods that weaken encryption. These methods rely on ordering a service provider (those who develop or maintain the software, computer system, network, or electronic device) to build vulnerabilities in their systems. With this demand, state actors want to enable the police or intelligence agencies to have access to our data and break encryption. Client-side scanning (scanning of all content such as text,images, videos, etc. on a device or shared in a communication channel) is a method proposed under the EU CSA Regulation. Key escrows or “key recovery”, involves placing decryption keys in a “vault” managed by a trusted authority or group of trusted authorities, who can break them out when access to the encrypted data is needed. Finally, ghost proposals refer to the modification of the encryption system to enable a third-party listener to be silently added to encrypted conversations.

In democratic societies, communication systems are vital for our lives and connections with others. Safe and secure communications and devices allow us to work, socialise, organise, express ourselves, and connect …

Les écrans, explique-t-il, feraient des élèves des « zombies », que leur téléphone, « stupéfiant-image », arracherait au monde. Leur confiscation aurait ainsi fait l'effet d'un électrochoc. Privés d'écran, les porcelets auraient enfin levé les yeux au ciel pour y découvrir leur misérable existence, et avec elle, ce que les adultes font de leur monde.


L'hypothèse est sans doute bienveillante. Le professeur précise qu'il écrit « sans aucune agressivité ni mépris envers mes élèves, que j'aime et apprécie ». On le croit, et c'est bien le problème. Le berger peut parfaitement aimer son troupeau : il n'en reste pas moins un berger. Or en matière de pouvoir pastoral, la sollicitude est parfois pire que le mépris.

Car de porcherie, il est bien question, mais pas de celle du groin dans les réseaux. Ce sont les rats, les chiottes bouchés, les canicules dans les préfabriqués.
