author: Joshua Carroll
title: Burnham Approves New North Sea Gas Drilling in ‘Act of Climate Vandalism’
content:
Andy Burnham’s government has given fossil fuel giants Shell and Equinor permission to drill the undeveloped Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea.


Energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh, who publicly opposed new drilling before taking on the role, is set to make the announcement from Aberdeen on Wednesday morning alongside chancellor John Healey. 


In 2022 Fahnbulleh wrote on X: “To have a shot at staying within 1.5C global warming, we can’t have any new oil or gas fields. 


“Banks know this, but some are pumping billions into new projects. It’s irresponsible and shortsighted to be funding new fossil fuels when we need to be getting to net zero fast.”


Before becoming prime minister, Burnham endorsed calls for a fossil fuel non-proliferation treaty. “It’s not just a plan, it’s a lifeline,” he

said last year

. “It’s a call to end coal, oil, and gas, hold polluters accountable.” 


Fahnbulleh told BBC Radio Scotland on Wednesday that drilling Jackdaw “won’t lower energy bills this winter”. Numerous energy experts have said extracting the gas will not lower bills at all. “The UK is not an isolated energy island where new supply has the effect of decreasing prices,” professor Gavin Bridge, fellow of the Durham Energy Institute,

told the Independent

 in April. 


Advocacy group

Greenpeace argues

 that, based on calculations for climate harm used by the government, burning the gas from Jackdaw will cause £16.1bn in “global damage” and cause more than 8,000 heat-related deaths.


Ross Greer, co-leader of the Scottish Greens, said: “Labour’s decision to approve Jackdaw is climate vandalism. Andy Burnham’s government had the opportunity to reject the greed of oil and gas companies… Instead, this Labour prime minister has caved in to the fossil fuel lobby and continued to devastate our climate. It is a devastating betrayal of our children’s future.”


Zack Polanski, leader of the Green party of England and Wales, said: “Labour has abandoned all credibility in the fight against climate change. This is a victory for Shell over the people.”


US president Donald Trump said in July that Burnham had told him he would “open up North Sea oil”.


The government is yet to issue a decision about Rosebank, an oil field also in the North Sea owned by Shell, Equinor and a firm called Ithaca Energy, which is part-owned by Israeli holding company Delek Group.

author: Vivian La
title: In Michigan, 3 tribes are on a mission to bring back a fish that disappeared 100 years ago
content:
Even when they’re young, the characteristic iridescent hues of the Arctic grayling are noticeable at the right angle.


On a brisk morning in September, fish and wildlife biologist Sean Leask counted and measured hundreds of these fish, which were raised at the Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians’ streamside rearing facility, located just outside Traverse City in northern Michigan. 


“Some of these might be catchable by the end of next year,” Leask said. “I don’t know what their growth will look like in the wild.”


That’s because Arctic grayling haven’t been seen in Michigan waters for almost a century. By the 1930s, industrial activity like logging and overfishing, along with competition from non-native fish, had decimated their numbers. But three northern Michigan tribes and the state are trying to change that by reintroducing the fish to local waters. 


“Our taking care of them and helping them to reestablish their population helps us to reestablish ourselves, our culture, and our traditions,” said Tina Frankenberger, the Grand Traverse Band’s tribal environmental resiliency lead.


Their work joins broader efforts by tribes around the country to restore native species — from

salmon

 to

oysters

 to

condors

 — that are culturally and economically important, while also strengthening the ecosystems that these species depend on against threats like climate change.


One year into raising and releasing grayling to northern Michigan waterways, biologists with the Michigan tribes are grappling with questions about whether the fish are surviving and how to adapt their efforts to extreme weather. No released grayling have been seen in the wild. Flood conditions and the small number of fish they began with are complicating survey work.


But the tribes remain optimistic that their restoration efforts will improve as they collect more data in the coming years. Biologists think it will be around six to eight years before they can tell if grayling reintroduction has been successful.


“This is an experiment,” said Dan Mays, inland policy biologist for the Grand Traverse Band. “We’re trying our best.”


Young Arctic grayling swim in holding tanks at a Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians streamside rearing facility near Traverse City.


Vivian La / IPR News


In the summer and early fall, the Grand Traverse Band raised around 8,000 young grayling and released them into the Boardman-Ottaway River. They’re one of three northern Michigan tribes that

received grayling eggs from a state hatchery

 in 2025, along with the Little River Band of Ottawa Indians and the Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians. This was the culmination of years of planning plus millions of dollars in combined

state

,

federal

, and

private

 funding to restore ecosystems. The eggs for Michigan’s reintroduction efforts were sourced from the Chena River in Alaska, a state where Arctic grayling are plentiful and more genetically diverse than the only remaining population in the Lower 48, in

Montana’s Big Hole River

.


Mays is already feeling more optimistic about the number and the size of the grayling that the Grand Traverse Band raised compared to last year, when a power outage at the tribe’s rearing facility killed a majority of the grayling.


“Overall, four times as many grayling,” he said. “We’re also stocking a higher proportion of bigger grayling this year. Greater size, greater survival.”


Raising the grayling is one challenge. Tracking the fish to see whether they’ve survived is another. None of the three northern Michigan tribes have recaptured a grayling yet.


“It’s like looking for a needle in a haystack, and the haystack is the size of a river,” said Alex Ontkos, an inland fisheries biologist with the Little River Band of Ottawa Indians. Earlier this year, this tribe stocked 391,000 grayling eggs using in-stream incubators on the Manistee River near Kalkaska. Not all of those eggs hatched, with viability rates estimated around 50 to 60 percent, Ontkos said.


Unlike the Grand Traverse Band, the Little River Band let larvae hatch directly into the incubators, grow into tiny fry, then leave the incubator. While biologists observed tens of thousands of fry leaving the incubators, they have yet to see or recapture a grayling. 


“I don’t think that that’s because they’re not out there,” Ontkos said. “It’s just a matter of being in the right place at the right time.” The team with the Little River …

author: Publicación Abierta
title: E INICIO EL PROCESO DE CONSULTAS A COMUNIDADES INDIGENAS SOBRE EL PLAN DE MANEJO DEL HUMEDAL LAGUNA MELINCUE (Santa Fe)
content:
Melincué, 22 de octubre de 2026 (por Centro Mocovi)


 El 20/10/2026 desde las 9 a 17 horas se realizaron los Talleres para iniciar el Proceso de Consulta Previa del Plan de Manejo del Sitio Ramsar “Humedal Laguna Melincué”, junto con el Ministerio de Ambiente y Cambio Climático de Santa Fe (Luciana Manelli, Directora Prov. de Bosques Y Áreas Protegidas), la Dirección Provincial de Pueblos Originarios (Victor De Battista), y el IPAS (Ramón Vilafañe). Los Talleres se realizaron en las Comunidades indígenas del Pueblo Mocoví de Maicasari Iagpa (Carreras), Noagué Noa Nonot’i (Melincué) y Ñachishinaxanaxat (Carmen).


El Centro Mocoví “Ialek Lav’a”, organización indígena que representa a las Comunidades Indígenas del Pueblo Mocoví asentadas en el Sitio Ramsar “Humedal Laguna Melincué”, y como parte integrante del

Comité Intersectorial de Manejo del Sitio Ramsar Humedal Laguna de Melincué

; viene impulsando el Procedimiento de Consulta Previa, Libre e Informada de las Comunidades Indígenas asentadas en el Sitio Ramsar “Humedal Laguna Melincué” sobre el Plan de Manejo de esta Área Natural Protegida.


Debemos destacar, que de la consulta preliminar realizada a las autoridades tradicionales indígenas de las comunidades mencionadas, en relación a la zona geográfica de impacto del Proyecto, resulta que existen comunidades y familias indígenas de los Pueblos Mocovi, Mapuche, Ranquel y Querandí radicadas en la zona de influencia del mismo; por lo que resulta obligatorio la aplicación de la Ley Nacional 24.071 (Convenio 169 de la Organización Internacional del Trabajo -OIT-) respecto a la aplicación de los procedimientos del Consentimiento Previo, Libre e Informado (CPLI) de los Pueblos Indígenas, contenidos en la norma citada.


Al respecto, y dado que la propuesta y el Proyecto “Plan de Manejo del Sitio Ramsar Humedal Laguna Melincué” , realizado por el Ministerio de Ambiente y Cambio Climáticoi, no tuvo la participación y consentimiento de las Comunidades Originarias, se deberá iniciar los procesos de consultas, en el marco del Convenio 169 de la OIT (Ley Nac. 24071), la Constitución Nacional (Art. 75, inc. 15), las leyes provinciales 10.375 y 11.078; la Declaración de las Naciones Unidas sobre Derechos de los Pueblos Indígenas; y la Declaración Americana sobre Derechos de los Pueblos Indígenas (OEA), a las Comunidades Indígenas de los Pueblos Mocovi, Rankülche, Mapuche y Querandí, asentadas en el Sitio Ramsar Humedal Laguna Melincué; a fin de determinar los impactos de las acciones y actividades a ejecutar con el proyecto; o las que surjan y propongan las Comunidades y organizaciones Indígenas. La misma deberá realizarse en conjunto con las Comunidades Originarias, las Organizaciones de Pueblos Indígenas de Segundo Grado (Centro Mocoví “Ialek Lav’a”) en aplicación de las Salvaguardas Sociales y Ambientales para Pueblos Indígenas contempladas en la legislación vigente.


En este caso el procesos de Consultas debe incluir un Plan de Manejo del Sitio Ramsar Humedal Laguna Melincué con la visión de los Pueblos Indígenas (PPI), o un Capítulo de Pueblos Indígenas, que contenga lineas de acción y actividades a desarrollar por el CIM (Comité Intersectorial de Manejo del Sitio Ramsar Humedal Laguna Melincué), incluido un especialista indígena y la asistencia técnica de las propias Organizaciones de Pueblos Indígenas (OPI), en el marco determinado por la 

Convención Ramsar: “

facilitar la participación directa de las comunidades locales y pueblos indígenas en el proceso de adopción de decisiones en los planos local y nacional para el uso sostenible de los humedales, incluido el suministro de los recursos necesarios; (Art. 15); y que “los expertos técnicos y las comunidades locales y pueblos indígenas a que trabajen conjuntamente en la planificación y el manejo/gestión de los humedales a fin de asegurar que en la adopción de decisiones se tomen en consideración los mejores conocimientos científicos y conocimientos locales disponibles; (Art. 18).


En los Talleres realizados se habló sobre la Visión Indígena del Humedal y la relación de las Comunidades con el Area Protegida, incluido los usos tradicionales dado por las Comunidadesa la biodiversidad del Humedal, y los proyectos que tienen en dicha Area Protegida, Territorio Ancestral y Sagrado Indígena….


ARIEL ARAUJO- Coordinador Centro Mocovi “Ialek Lav’a”

author: Unknown
title: Where are the Zapatistas 30 years later?
content:
The Zapatista Army of National Liberation (EZLN – Ejército Zapatista de Liberación Nacional), which emerged in Chiapas in the first days of 1994, came to the world's attention through an armed uprising in a region of Mexico marked by widespread poverty and inequality, where Indigenous people make up a significant proportion of the population. However, it was not only the uprising that made the Zapatista experience distinctive.


In the years that followed, the movement moved away from the goal of seizing state power and developed a practice of autonomy centred on the right of Indigenous communities to govern themselves. In this direction, it established autonomous governance, education, healthcare and production structures based on local communities. Over more than thirty years, as demands for Indigenous rights and political autonomy were not sufficiently realised, the Zapatistas declared their own autonomous governance structures and reorganised them several times. Having established autonomous municipalities and regional administrative centres for a period, the movement dissolved these structures in 2023, shifting decision-making processes to a model based on smaller, local communities.


During this process, it developed its own mechanisms for education, healthcare, justice and community governance outside the official structures of the state, and prioritised the collective use of land and natural resources. We spoke with Professor Neil Harvey of New Mexico State University about the Zapatistas.


Who is Neil Harvey?


Dr Neil Harvey is Professor and Head of the Department of Government at New Mexico State University, specialising in Political Science, Public Law and Administration. Harvey, who studies social movements and struggles for democracy in Mexico and Latin America, has conducted field research in Chiapas. He is the author of The Chiapas Rebellion: The Struggle for Land and Democracy (Duke University Press, 1998) and has published numerous articles on the Zapatista movement and autonomy.


More than thirty years have passed since the 1994 Zapatista uprising. How would you describe the most significant transformation the movement has undergone in the process of moving from an armed uprising to the construction of autonomous political and social structures?


This transformation involved several important changes over time. First, there was a shift from armed uprising to a peaceful strategy based on effective communication, which gained broad support within Mexican society and internationally. Second, there was a transition from the highly centralised position of military commanders to a structure in which civilian Zapatista members in hundreds of local communities assumed stronger leadership. Finally, the language used by the movement changed. The more traditional revolutionary discourse of the Latin American left was replaced by an approach in which different goals and cultural elements, both specific to the Indigenous peoples of Chiapas and appealing to humanity as a whole in a broader sense, were continuously expressed.


Rather than seizing state power, the Zapatistas developed autonomous structures in areas such as local governance, education, healthcare and justice. Why did this path emerge, and what has enabled these structures to survive for so long?


Shortly after their uprising in 1994, the Zapatistas clearly stated that their aim was to "change the world without taking power". By this, they meant that they refused to engage in a struggle to seize state power in Mexico, preferring instead to create their own forms of self-government and autonomous decision-making mechanisms. This approach represents a different understanding of revolution, aimed at avoiding the pitfalls of centralised leadership, a single ideology and the associated pyramid-shaped organisational structure that can emerge when attempting to seize state power. It is a call to change the world by starting from the specific conditions of each place and period in which struggles for justice emerge, while doing so in alliance with one another.


The goal of autonomy initially emerged as an extremely urgent need in the rural Indigenous communities of Chiapas. In these areas, the presence of teachers, doctors and other services provided by central or local governments was very limited. In the 1970s and 1980s, while the EZLN was undergoing its own process of independent formation, community members were also working with the Catholic …

author: Kiara Green
title: Beyond Indigenous Peoples Day: The Fight to Protect Indigenous Communities
content:
The second Monday in October is federally recognized as Christopher Columbus Day, commemorating the arrival of colonizer Christopher Columbus to the Americas. It’s undeniable that Indigenous communities lived in America long before Columbus docked his ship. Why, then, is he celebrated as the man who “discovered” America?

For years, public debate has challenged this Eurocentric narrative. In response, several states have recognised the second Monday in October as Indigenous Peoples Day. The day celebrates the resilience and the vibrant cultures of Indigenous communities in America.

Despite the lack of federal recognition, Indigenous Peoples Day continues to be celebrated while bringing attention to issues that Indigenous communities face. The day has been used to advocate for the removal of Columbus memorials, the returning of Indigenous lands, and awareness about Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women (MMIW).

The Trump administration has rejected this broader recognition. In 2025, Trump declared he was “bringing Columbus Day back from the ashes,” reinforcing the federal emphasis on celebrating Columbus rather than recognizing Indigenous peoples.

Meanwhile, proposed federal funding cuts of $2.3 billion from the administration continue to impact Tribal programs especially violence related programs and services that support survivors. These reductions could undermine essential services, including programs that address violence and support survivors.

The consequences are especially serious given the rates of violence facing Indigenous communities. On September 15, the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Federal Government Surveillance held a hearing titled “Missing and Murdered Indigenous People: Strengthening Public Safety in Tribal Communities.” Lawmakers and witnesses discussed how the federal government can help ensure the safety of Indigenous communities as they face some of the highest homicide and missing persons rates in the country.

According to the CDC, homicide was the fourth leading cause of death for American Indian and Alaska Natives men and sixth-leading cause for women ages one to 44 in 2023. Tribal communities rely on violence prevention programs and other services to address these disparities. Funding cuts threaten their ability to sustain this work.

During the September hearing, witnesses urged members to increase the funding for tribal communities to sustain these instrumental programs. Trent Shores, former U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Oklahoma, stressed that “Resources need to reach the people and stay there.” Myron Lizer, Former Vice President of Navajo Nation, similarly warned that “we have built programs but not continuous systems,” highlighting the gap between establishing initiatives and providing the sustained resources communities need.

Legislation like Savanna’s Act and the Not Invisible Act have started to address missing and murdered Native Americans by strengthening relations between federal and tribal law enforcement. However, significant gaps remain in preventing violence, investigating cases and supporting survivors.

As Indigenous communities continue to face high levels of homicide and missing person rates, Congress must continue to act and pass the Trace Act for a concise database. Honoring Indigenous resilience goes beyond annual recognition but a continued effort to guarantee sustained resources and legislative action that protect these communities from ongoing violence and funding cuts.

author: Rachel Sherrington and Hazel Healy
title: How Big Pharma Tried to Weaken the Rules of the UN’s Nature Fund
content:
As the COP17 nature summit gets underway in Armenia, evidence has emerged of lobbying by a leading international pharmaceuticals group to weaken the terms of a flagship fund for nature.


Documents analysed by DeSmog show that the International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers and Associations (IFPMA)

called

 for a “radical rethink” of the rationale for the

landmark

 Cali Fund – the first mechanism built to take voluntary payments from large companies that profit from genetic sequence data.


The IFPMA states that the “modalities of the decision” to establish the Fund – which was ratified by 196 countries in 2024 at the COP16 summit of the UN Convention on Biological Diversity in Colombia – should be “significantly reviewed, revised and clarified”.


In the consultation submission, the trade group – which

represents

 the pharmaceutical sector at the UN – also challenged the indicative rates at which companies were invited to contribute to the Fund, agreed at COP16 as 0.1 percent of revenue or 1 percent of profit.

The IFPMA labelled these indicative rates as “premature”, set “without any rational analysis”, and “commercially unrealistic”, suggesting instead that companies be allowed to contribute to the voluntary fund at a level of their choosing. 


Other demands from the IFPMA included a guarantee that any contribution would explicitly substitute payments for digital sequence information required under national or international laws.

Despite contributions to the Cali Fund already being voluntary, following a fierce

lobbying push

 at the last summit, the IFPMA also seeks a guarantee they will remain so, stating that “there are elements in the decision that do not go far enough in creating a truly voluntary mechanism”.


Responses from other sectors, such as biotechnology and cosmetics – which are listed alongside pharma and artificial intelligence firms in the treaty text as industries that should contribute – echo some of the IFPMA’s objections, and appear to be reluctant to support the Fund as it is currently conceived. 


The UK Bioindustry Association (UK BIA), which

has

 600 biotech and life sciences companies among its members,

says

 the CBD’s expectations for what the Fund can raise are currently set “unrealistically high”, in its consultation response dated March 2025. 


UK BIA states that “for the Fund to succeed in the long term”, questions over its design and operationalisation must be addressed, and “clear incentives” created. 


The revelations come as negotiators gather for the UN biodiversity summit in Armenia this week, with just $10,000

pledged

 by companies to the Cali Fund. 


It falls far short of the $1 billion to $10 billion that the UN had

hoped

 the Fund could draw in every year, half of which is mandated to flow directly to the Indigenous and local communities that steward biodiversity.


“The tiny amounts contributed to the Cali Fund so far, combined with continued delays from industry, send a clear signal: voluntary contributions are simply not delivering,” An Lambrechts, a biodiversity politics expert at Greenpeace International, told DeSmog. 


The latest UN report shows that the world is

off track on

 all but one of 23 targets aimed at reversing catastrophic nature loss, with the total funds raised to date from both private and public bodies falling far short of what is needed to close a $200 billion “biodiversity finance gap”.

“Big multinational corporations are turning massive profits by exploiting nature,” Lambrechts says, “while leaving people all over the world to face the impacts of the biodiversity crisis.”

author: Sara Luterman
title: Nursing Home Residents Have a Right to Vote — Despite What Trump CMS Agency Says
content:
The Nursing Home Reform Act of 1987 requires facilities to support their residents in exercising their rights.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Cindy Napolitan and her daughter Melissa have multiple sclerosis, a degenerative condition in which the immune system attacks the brain, spinal cord and nerves. They have lived together at a nursing home in Mesquite, Texas, for nine years. In previous elections, Cindy and Melissa Napolitan voted by mail, but this year they took an unusual step: They voted in person. They worried their mail-in ballots — and even their in-person votes — may not be counted.

“I’ve never worried like this before. I’ve never worried that I don’t have the proper ID. I’ve never worried that somebody is going to intimidate me. Will I encounter somebody that’s going to threaten me or make me feel less than? So yeah, I’m very worried, and I shouldn’t be,” Cindy Napolitan said. “I shouldn’t have to be worried about stuff like that. This is the 19th Amendment. I’m allowed to vote.”

Nursing home residents are guaranteed the right to vote. Around two-thirds of all nursing home residents in the United States are women, making aging and long-term care gendered issues.

There is no data on how many nursing home residents exercise that right. Cindy, 70, and Melissa Napolitan, 48, at least, feel like they’ve had good experiences with voting at their facility. Cindy Napolitan, in particular, has worked with the activities coordinator to organize rides to the polls for her, her daughter and other interested residents.

“We are scheduled to go on the first day of early voting. So in case there are any issues that we come across, we still have time to rectify the situation and be allowed to vote,” Cindy Napolitan said.

Cindy and Melissa Napolitan are more concerned this year than in previous years about government interference and voter suppression. Their fears are not unfounded: Experts and advocates for the rights of nursing home residents, older adults and people with disabilities are worried too.

In July, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services rescinded previous guidance affirming that nursing home residents have the right to vote.

“The memo does not alter the underlying law. Nursing homes are governed by the Nursing Home Reform Act of 1987 and its implementing regulations,” said Nina Kohn, a professor at Syracuse University and expert on elder law. “That law still requires facilities to support their residents in exercising their rights as Americans.”

The memo also emphasized voter fraud in nursing homes, specifically around mail-in ballots. For years, President Trump has disparaged mail-in ballots, insisting without evidence that fraudulent votes by mail had a role in his loss during the 2020 presidential election. His comments have led to some states restricting who can use a mail-in ballot and in what contexts.

According to experts, including Kohn, there is no evidence that voter fraud is a serious or widespread problem in nursing homes. Instead, Kohn is concerned about the chilling effect that it may have on residents’ rights.

“The language in the memo itself is intimidating, and it may understandably make staff think that they could face criminal prosecution or be in some other form of legal trouble if they help residents vote,” Kohn said.

Cindy and Melissa Napolitan do everything together — and on Monday, they voted together. They are also roommates at the facility; most people living in nursing homes are assigned roommates who are strangers.

“Unlike other people that have roommates that don’t get along, I’m very lucky and fortunate that I have somebody that loves me and I love her,” Cindy Napolitan said.

This is the second time Cindy and Melissa Napolitan have voted in person since entering a nursing home. The first time was during the 2024 presidential election.

“I’ve been checking my status weekly to make sure that I haven’t been dropped off the voter rolls, making sure my daughter and I don’t have some sort of issue that says that we can’t vote,” Cindy Napolitan said.

People living in nursing homes and other long-term care facilities face specific barriers. Some residents may need assistance filling out their ballots because they lack the movement or dexterity to hold a pen or press buttons on a computer screen. People with dexterity or coordination issues may also be unable to produce the same signature twice …

author: Matthew McWade
title: The False Promise of Patient Rights in Psychiatric Units
content:
I

 have been aware of patient rights since I began working as a Certified Peer Specialist in 2006. I had the privilege of serving as emcee at an M-POWERed event at the statehouse in 2009, and participated in testimony related to Massachusetts’ Restraint and Seclusion Initiative around the same time. I worked for a year at The Transformation Center, a wing of M-POWER, the now-defunct grassroots political organization that secured Massachusetts mental health patients their six fundamental rights on psych units. I knew each of the six fundamental rights by heart (humane environment, daily private visitors, professional communications, uncensored mail, phone access, and outdoor access), but after becoming a peer specialist, I rarely experienced psychiatric hospitalization myself and had little opportunity to see how well those rights were upheld.


During a manic episode in late 2025, I felt little fear about voluntarily admitting myself to my local psych hospital because I assumed my rights would be respected. After a single weekend, I was astonished by the poor implementation of the six fundamental rights, and my mental state deteriorated as a direct result of the psych unit’s inability to uphold even the most basic of those rights.


Feeling sure that I could manage my mania and medication on my own, I asked for an immediate discharge, which was not granted (I signed a three-day but was told I would be taken before a judge — recalling my commitment in 2002 where the judge took one look at me and committed me without asking me a single question or providing me an opportunity for defense, I was hesitant to trust the local courts). Reviewing the rights board in the hallway, I vocally indicated to the staff where their policy deviated from state law, and I was met with disregard that devolved to disdain. Trapped and contemplating how to either exercise my rights or win my freedom to return to the community, I took comfort in the fact that at least the newest of the six fundamental rights, the right to fresh air, was being honored (though without access to cigarettes, which continually annoyed the other patients).


My first effort towards garnering assistance was to speak privately with my parents about my concerns, including the psych doctor’s stubborn refusal to discuss my discharge, but I was met with deprivation as my right to receive daily visitors of my own choosing, in private and at reasonable times, was immediately trampled. My elderly parents, who have vision problems and live over an hour away from the hospital, politely requested an earlier visiting time, in the early afternoon. The established visiting hours were 6pm-8pm (after the sun has set in late-autumn New England) which prevented my parents from ever having an extended visit with me during my entire psych ward stay considering they could not drive at night. They merely dropped off clothes, my phone, and a book and then left.


My next attempt was to have a private conversation with my mother about how I might secure a discharge, but I was met with another right denied when I was told I needed a “prescription” from the psych doctor for a private phone call (which she did not grant). I was told that even if I did get the “prescription phone call,” a staff member might be required to stand in the room (no one explained how the conversation could remain private with a staff member in the room). My mother insisted on having this phone conversation, being as upset as I was that they would not let me leave. I was left with two options: I could either call my mother from the crowded cafeteria during my allotted 30 minutes of daily cell phone access (with another staff member sitting five feet away with a sign-in sheet pretending not to listen as I whispered over the other 15 local phone conversations), or I could call my mother from one of the two “very private” payphones, each about seven feet from the staff office in the “secluded” hallway that everyone needed to walk through to arrive at the cafeteria or the TV room.


Reading the patients’ rights board, I noticed an unnumbered set of rights including the “right to know why you are being held on the psych unit and the stipulations for your discharge.” Waiting the entire evening, I knew I could question my assigned psych doctor the next day. Working with this doctor became a chore. She would devote barely two minutes to speaking with me regardless of my concerns, and refused to meet with me at all one day …

author: Unknown
title: Ulus: Healthcare must be free and accessible to all
content:
Structural problems in public hospitals and shortcomings in healthcare services are making it increasingly difficult for citizens to access medical care. People struggling to secure appointments through the Central Physician Appointment System (MHRS) sometimes have to wait at least 15 days just to submit an appointment request. Patients who eventually manage to obtain appointments after considerable effort must then try to explain their health problems within limited consultation times due to overcrowding in hospitals.


Difficulties in securing appointments and restrictions on consultation times are further deepening problems concerning the quality and accessibility of healthcare services.


Mehmet Nuri Ulus, Co-Chair of the Diyarbakır (Amed) Branch of the Health and Social Service Workers’ Union (SES), spoke to ANF about the problems facing public hospitals.


‘Healthcare is not being transformed, it is going backwards’


Ulus recalled that the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government has introduced healthcare reform and transformation programmes since 2002. He said that the policies implemented in recent years have caused serious problems in healthcare services and continued: “The AKP government has announced numerous programmes under the names of healthcare reform and healthcare transformation. However, particularly over the past 10 to 15 years, what has been called healthcare transformation has, from our perspective, meant collapse and regression. We have experienced both the COVID-19 pandemic and the earthquake during this period. These major crises showed us just how inadequate the healthcare system was in responding to the problems that arose.


The healthcare system should have been prepared for these crises and should have had the capacity to meet society's healthcare needs. Healthcare is a service that must be provided within the framework of the social welfare state. Everyone must be able to receive healthcare services equally, accessibly and in their mother tongue.


However, in recent years, we have seen healthcare services increasingly turn into a system in which those who have money can access care more easily. The proliferation of private hospitals is one aspect of this. Another is the emergence of an approach in which even public hospitals link faster access to certain tests, radiological examinations, medical reports and surgical procedures to payment. This undermines the principle that healthcare services should be equal for everyone.”


‘Physical queues have been replaced by virtual queues’


Ulus addressed the appointment crisis in the healthcare system, pointing out that the queues once seen outside hospitals now continue through the Central Physician Appointment System. He said appointment systems should make healthcare more accessible, but many citizens are currently unable to secure appointments.


Ulus said: “The AKP government used to say that people had to go to hospitals early in the morning and wait in queues to see a doctor. Today, physical queues have been replaced by virtual queues. Instead of waiting for hours outside hospitals, people now try to book appointments on their phones or online. However, when you access the system, you cannot find an available appointment. The queues have therefore not disappeared; they have simply changed form. Citizens now find themselves waiting in front of digital systems to access healthcare.


People face serious difficulties securing appointments, particularly in departments such as ear, nose and throat, ophthalmology and dermatology. Citizens who cannot obtain appointments are then forced to turn to private hospitals. However, considering the economic crisis, the struggle to make ends meet and the housing problems in Turkey, not everyone has the financial means to seek treatment at private hospitals.


As a result, the inability to access healthcare has become another dimension of economic hardship. Healthcare should be free and accessible, yet citizens are forced to stretch their financial resources to obtain the medical care they need.”


‘The budget is not allocated to preventive healthcare services’


Ulus said that the problems facing the healthcare system are not limited to difficulties in securing appointments. He drew attention to the following issues: “When we look at the Ministry of Health's budget and healthcare policies, we see that preventive healthcare services are consistently pushed into the background. title: Söke Ekmek ve Gül açıklaması: Her çocuğa okullarda bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı yemek istiyoruz
content:
Aydın - Söke'de Belediye Meydanı’nda Söke Ekmek ve Gül "Bir Öğün Ücretsiz Sağlıklı Yemek Güvenli Okul Güvenli Ulaşım İstiyoruz” diyerek basın açıklaması yaptı.

Söke Ekmek ve Gül’ün çağrısıyla yapılan açıklamaya veliler, Söke Kadın Dayanışma Derneği ve Söke Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri de destek verdi. "Bir öğün ücretsiz sağlıklı yemek güvenli okul güvenli ulaşım istiyoruz” pankartının açıldığı basın açıklamasıni Söke Ekmek ve Gül adına öğrenci velisi Huri Abrinç okudu.

Çocukların okullarda bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı ve dengeli yemek yiyebilmesi için yıllardır ülkenin dört bir yanında ve Söke’de aralıksız mücadele ettiklerini belirten Abrinç; “Söke Ekmek ve Gül olarak imza kampanyaları düzenledik, stantlar açtık, çocukların beslenme hakkını kararlılıkla savunduk. 2022 yılında Ekmek ve Gül tarafından başlatılan, 2023’te Kocaeli Ekmek ve Gül Kadın Dayanışma Derneği’nin çalışmalarıyla büyüyen, Esenyalı Kadın Dayanışma Derneği üyesi bir kadının hukuki mücadelesine kadar uzanan bu talep; bugün Türkiye’nin her köşesindeki kadınların, velilerin, öğretmenlerin ve eğitim emekçilerinin ortak talebidir. Toplanan binlerce imza, yapılan basın açıklamaları ve dayanışma ağları bu ihtiyacın ne kadar hayati, acil ve vazgeçilmez olduğunu defalarca kanıtlamıştır.

Çünkü biliyoruz ki derinleşen ekonomik kriz ortamında çocukların okula aç gittiği, ailelerin beslenme çantalarını doldurmakta zorlandığı, temel gıda ürünlerinin dahi lüks hâline geldiği bir ülkede; sağlıklı beslenme bir lütuf veya yardım değil, en temel insan hakkıdır. Çocuklar açken eğitimde fırsat eşitliğinden ya da nitelikli bir eğitimden söz edilemez” dedi.

Yürütülen bu haklı mücadeleler ve yükselen kamuoyu baskısı sonucunda Millî Eğitim Bakanlığının 5-19 Ekim tarihleri arasında ücretsiz okul yemeğine ilişkin velilerin görüşlerini almak amacıyla bir anket süreci yürüttüğünü hatırlatan Abrinç: “Yıllardır dile getirilen bu yakıcı ihtiyacı anlamak için çocukların açlığının bu kadar derinleşmesini bekleyen Bakanlığa soruyoruz: Velilerin ve kadınların sesi neden bugüne kadar duyulmadı” sorusunu sordu.

Bakanlığın adım atması önemli olsa da, yürütülen anketin kapsamı, erişilebilirliği ve yöntemi ciddi soru işaretleri doğurduğunu vurgulayan Abrinç anketle ilgili eksiklikleri sıraladı:

İnternet üzerinden yürütülen ankete pek çok veli eşit biçimde katılamamıştır. Veliler ankete ulaşmaya çalıştıklarında "yetkiniz yok" uyarılarıyla, sistemde yaşanan teknik sorunlarla karşılaşmış; internet ve telefon imkânı bulunmayan ya da dijital araçları kullanmakta zorlanan aileler süreçten tamamen izole edilmiştir. Ayrıca anket hakkında velilere yeterli bilgilendirme yapılmamıştır.

Edindiğimiz bilgilere göre ilkokul öğrencileri anket kapsamı dışında tutulmuş, süreç yalnızca ortaokul ve lise düzeyine sıkıştırılmıştır. Oysa en temel gelişim çağındaki ilkokul ve okul öncesi çocukların beslenme hakkı nasıl göz ardı edilebilir?

Servis imkânlarının kaldırılması veya kısıtlanmasıyla mağdur edilen taşımalı eğitim kapsamındaki aileler, bu anket hakkında da yeterince bilgilendirilmemiştir. Çocukların ulaşım ve beslenme ihtiyaçları birlikte değerlendirilmelidir.”

“İnternete erişemeyen, yetki engeline takılan ya da anket kapsamına alınmayan çocukların sağlıklı beslenmeye ihtiyacı yok mu? Çocukların en temel hakkı, teknik aksaklıklarla dolu bir anketin sonucuna ya da hangi eğitim kademesinde olduğuna indirgenebilir mi?” sorularını soran Abrinç, “Bir ankete katılamamış olmak, ücretsiz yemek ihtiyacının olmadığı anlamına gelmez! Çocukların açlığı anket sorularıyla giderilemez; beslenme sorumluluğu yalnızca ailelerin ve kadınların omuzlarına yıkılamaz” ifadelerini kullandı

Mıllî Eğitim Bakanlığına ve yetkililere çağrı yapan Abrinç şu talepleri sıraladı

Eşit ve Koşulsuz Hak: Okul öncesinden liseye kadar, kamu okullarındaki tüm öğrencilere ayrım yapılmaksızın her gün bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı ve dengeli yemek derhal sağlanmalıdır.

Anket Sonucu Beklenmemelidir: Ücretsiz okul yemeği bir anketin sonucuna bağlanmadan, bütçe bahanelerinin arkasına sığınmadan kalıcı bir kamu hizmeti olarak uygulamaya konulmalıdır.

Şeffaflık ve Hesap Verilebilirlik: Yapılan anketin kaç veliye ulaştığı, hangi kademeleri kapsadığı ve sonuçların nasıl değerlendirildiği kamuoyuyla açık ve şeffaf bir şekilde paylaşılmalıdır.

Erişilebilir Katılım Yöntemleri: Dijital araçları kullanamayan veya erişim sorunu yaşayan veliler için yüz yüze görüşmeler, basılı formlar ve okullar aracılığıyla katılım kanalları oluşturulmalıdır.

author: Kodao Productions
title: The Political Economy of Healthcare and the PhilHealth Dilemma: Social Insurance or Socialized Medicine?
content:
By

Prof. Sarah Raymundo


Angelo V. Suarez

’s sharp intervention in response to Cielo Magno’s senatorial campaign line brings a vital structural issue into the public sphere. Credit must be given to Magno: her platform draws directly from a concrete social issue plaguing the vast majority of Filipinos—a crisis of public health and economic vulnerability that demands urgent collective attention. Unlike the posture of mainstream politicians running on empty campaigns, abstract pledges of service, and hollow soundbites, Magno brings a substantive issue to the table that gives the citizenry something real to evaluate and debate.


It is precisely this substance that prompted Suarez—a poet, creative industry worker, and staunch peasant advocate for the Unyon ng mga Manggagawa sa Agrikultura (UMA)—to respond, participate, and rally his friends and comrades around this critical issue. While one might be tempted to label this response as a “new politics” brought forward by figures from late Generation X and early Millennial cohorts, its core is rooted in a fundamental class politics challenging mainstream governance in the Philippines. This intervention offers an opportunity to build on our collective arsenal of knowledge and critique regarding the current Philippine health system. It aims to foster a well-informed, critical citizenry whose stakes in national elections must be elevated to what the working people truly deserve. What is at stake in this counter-critique is the necessity of deepening public deliberation on genuine reforms—and examining how these immediate struggles can advance more systemic, transformative aspirations for society.


Dissecting the Policy Platform and the Critique


In her published academic research—such as her study on pharmaceutical competition for the Philippine Competition Commission—Magno approaches the issue of expensive medicines through neoclassical market regulation. She does not advocate for breaking away from foreign drug monopolies or building a state-owned pharmaceutical industry. Instead, she identifies high medicine prices as a symptom of insufficient market competition, brand bias, and distorted prescribing behaviors. Her proposed remedy relies on market regulation: using antitrust oversight to encourage generic competition, alongside using PhilHealth as a bulk purchaser to negotiate lower prices from private pharmaceutical suppliers and absorb outpatient drug costs.


Angelo Suarez’s critique dismantles this reformist premise at its structural foundation. Suarez’s actual text makes four direct arguments:


First, policy directions that prioritize a “stronger” PhilHealth obstruct the creation of a strong public health system. Second, PhilHealth fosters and entrenches an insurance system that welcomes and relies upon the private health sector. Third, the state must directly fund the supply side by hiring health workers with security of tenure and reasonable wages, building accessible facilities staffed by well-trained personnel, and establishing a nationalized pharmaceutical industry grounded in a program of national industrialization. Fourth, health services can and should be made entirely free, funded directly out of general state taxes without resorting to PhilHealth as an insurance middleman.


While Suarez articulates these core demands, this analysis extends his critique by placing it within the broader frameworks of international political economy, World Bank policy history, and Samir Amin’s theory of imperialist value transfer. Suarez identifies the political demands; this intervention maps the structural mechanisms behind them.


The core dispute between Magno’s platform and Suarez’s counter-position is not over whether Filipinos deserve access to medical care, but over the mechanism through which that care is delivered.


Magno advocates for demand-side financing, where the state acts as an insurer buying health services and imported medicines on behalf of citizens within a market economy. Suarez advocates for supply-side direct provision, where the state directly owns, operates, and funds the physical, human, and industrial infrastructure of health as an unmediated public good. #


 


The post

The Political Economy of Healthcare and the PhilHealth Dilemma: Social Insurance or Socialized Medicine?

 appeared first on

Kodao Productions

author: Mag
title: Immer nur Behindertenwerkstätten: Warum verdienen Menschen mit Behinderung so wenig? Und wo bleibt die Inklusion?
content:
Dossier


„

In der Pandemie sind beinahe unbemerkt Löhne in Behindertenwerkstätten gekürzt worden. Schon vorher ließ sich von den Geld kaum leben. (…) Der Lohn der Beschäftigten in Behinderten-Werkstätten setzt sich in Deutschland aus mehreren Teilen zusammen: Ein sogenanntes Arbeitsförderungsgeld von 52 Euro wird aus Töpfen des Landes gezahlt. Dazu kommt ein Grundlohn von 89 Euro und ein individuell festgelegter Steigerungsbetrag. Diese beiden Posten müssen die Werkstätten selbst erwirtschaften. Als die Corona-Pandemie Deutschland erreichte, schlossen die Betreiber ihre Werkstätten für Menschen mit Behinderung. In der Folge konnten viele Aufträge nicht mehr erfüllt werden. Der Steigerungslohn entfiel. (…) 19 Prozent der Werkstätten, die an der Umfrage teil nahmen, gaben an, Löhne gekürzt zu haben. Weitere 18 Prozent gaben an, dass Kürzungen absehbar sind. Insgesamt hat sich in der Umfrage gezeigt, dass die Auswirkungen der Krise verzögert in den Werkstätten ankommen

…“

Artikel von Fabian Hillebrand vom 14.11.2020 im ND online

 

 und auch dazu:


Gerechtigkeit statt Almosen: Die GFF geht mit Jürgen Linnemann gegen das diskriminierende Entgeltsystem in „Werkstätten für behinderte Menschen“ (WfbM) vor Gericht


Mindestlohn in Werkstätten: Der sitzende Leistungsträger


„

Jürgen Linnemann hat 40 Jahre in Werkstätten für Menschen mit Behinderung gearbeitet. Jetzt zieht er für den Mindestlohn vor Gericht. (…) Sie klagen vor dem Arbeitsgericht Münster darauf, dass die Werkstatt ihm die Differenz zwischen seinem bisherigen Arbeitsentgelt und dem Mindestlohn zahlt. Linnemann sei Arbeitnehmer und habe dementsprechend Anrecht auf den Mindestlohn, so die Begründung. Der gesetzliche Mindestlohn müsse zudem auch in Werkstätten gelten. Anfang September soll das Arbeitsgericht eine Entscheidung treffen. Falls es beides verneint, will die GFF das derzeitige Entgeltsystem auf Vereinbarkeit mit Verfassungs-, Unions- und Völkerrecht überprüfen lassen. Bislang fehlen entsprechende Gerichtsentscheidungen. Das könnte sieben bis zehn Jahre dauern, wie Linnemanns Anwältin schätzt. Bis dahin ist er bereits in Rente. (…)


Das Sondersystem der Werkstätten hat der Bundesrepublik bereits zwei Rügen durch den UN-Fachausschuss für die Rechte von Menschen mit Behinderungen beschert. Reformpläne gibt es zahlreiche. Erst 2023 kam eine Studie im Auftrag der damaligen Ampel-Regierung zu dem Ergebnis, dass ein steuersubventioniertes Mindestlohnmodell besser funktionieren und zu mehr Gerechtigkeit führen würde. Andere fordern für einen inklusiven Arbeitsmarkt die Abschaffung der Werkstätten

title: Sağlık Bakanlığı: Eşitsizlikleri devam ettirmekte kararlıyız!
content:
Sağlık Bakanlığı İstatistik Yıllığı (SBİY) 2025 Haber Bülteni, 30 Eylül 2025, çarşamba günü, saat 17:00’de 

(!)

 yayımlandı. İlki 12 yıl önce, 2014 yılında yine eylül ayının son günü SBİY 2013 Haber Bülteni olarak yayımlanmıştı. Bülten, istatistik yıllığından yaklaşık üç, dört ay önce daha az sayıdaki veri grubunu kapsayacak şekilde yayımlanıyor. Bununla birlikte, ölümlülük, aşılama ve hizmet kullanımıyla ilgili bir önceki yılın verilerine 9-10 ay sonra da olsa ulaşabilmiş oluyoruz. Ve Türkiye’nin dokuz ilinin bulunduğu coğrafyada yaşayanların, AKP’li yılların bundan önceki 16 yılında olduğu gibi, 17nci yılında da değişmeyen bir biçimde sağlık ve sosyoekonomik eşitsizlere mahkûm edilmiş olduğunu görüyoruz. Bu haftaki yazıda söz konusu durumu ve AKP’li Sağlık Bakanlığı’nın verileri kendine saklamak gibi bir özelliğini kendilerinin sunduğu kaynaklar üzerinden ele alacağım.


ERİŞ BİLALOĞLU YAZDI


Yeni Bir Sıfırlama Çabası mı: Türkiye’de Bebek Ölüm Hızı


29 Ocak 2015


AKP’li bakanlık verileri kendine saklıyor


AKP tarafından 2002 yılında kurulan 58. Hükümet’e kadar sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili veriler yıllardır istatistik yıllıklarıyla düzenli olarak kamuoyuyla paylaşılıyordu. Ancak

58. Hükümet ve o kabinenin Sağlık Bakanı Recep Akdağ ile birlikte, sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili veriler kamuoyundan 2011 yılına kadar saklandı,

paylaşılmadı. Dünya Sağlık Örgütü başta olmak üzere, Türkiye’nin üyesi olduğu uluslararası kuruluşların talebi üzerine, bir AKP Hükümeti ve Sağlık Bakanı olarak ilk defa 2011 yılında, 2008 yılına ait veriler “Sağlık Bakanlığı Sağlık İstatistikleri Yıllığı 2008” başlığında Bakan Akdağ’ın önsözüyle yayımlandı. O nedenle Türkiye’nin 2003-2007 yıllarına ait sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili verileri diğer yıllar gibi düzenli bir biçimde bugüne kadar paylaşılmadı.


Sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili istatistikler, 2011 yılından sonra, Sağlık Bakanlığı ve Türkiye İstatistik Kurumu (TÜİK) tarafından düzenli olarak yayımlanıyor. TÜİK, özelikle doğurganlık ve ölümlülükle ilgili verileri Merkezi Nüfus İdaresi Sistemi (MERNİS) üzerinden iller düzeyinde, sağlık harcamalarıyla ilgili verileri Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı ile Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (SGK) ve yerel yönetimlerden ve “Hanehalkı Bütçe Anketi” çalışması üzerinden, hastalıklarla ilgili verileri de “Türkiye Sağlık Araştırması” üzerinden sağlıyor. Sağlık Bakanlığı da bu verileri kullanıp yaptığı hesaplamaları ve sağlık kurumları, sağlık emekçileri, ilaç, sağlık hizmetleri kullanımı vb. verileri Türkiye’nin makro düzeyde ekonomik ve sosyo-ekonomik yapıya göre gruplandığı 12 bölge, İstatistiki Bölge Bilgileri Sınıflaması-1 (İBBS-1), üzerinden paylaşıyor. Bununla birlikte, 

Sağlık Bakanlığı kaynakları üzerinden 81 ilden herhangi birinin sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleri verilerini, durumunu öğrenebilmek mümkün olamıyor.

Çünkü Sağlık Bakanlığı illerin verilerini yayımlamayı uzun zamandır tercih etmiyor.


Tabip Odası Bebek Ölümlerine Önlem Paketini Açıkladı


25 Eylül 2008


Bebek ölüm hızı önemli bir toplumsal sağlık düzeyi göstergesidir


Toplumların sağlık düzeyinin değerlendirilmesi ve izlenebilmesi amacıyla “bebek ölüm hızı”, “beş yaş altı ölüm hızı” ve “doğumda beklenen yaşam süresi” uluslararası alanda sıklıkla kullanılan, kabul görmüş üç değişkendir. Bunlar aynı zamanda, ülkelerin gelişmişlik düzeyi göstergeleri arasında da yer almaktadır. Çünkü, bu üç gösterge bir ülkede, bölgede, ilde vb. öncelikle beslenme, barınma, alt yapı ve eğitim başta olmak üzere, sosyoekonomik koşulların durumu ve sağlık hizmetlerinin ulaşılabilir olup olmamasıyla sağlık hizmetlerinin niteliğinden doğrudan etkilenmektedir.


Gebeliğin herhangi bir döneminde, canlı doğan bebeğin, birinci doğum gününü göremeden ölmesi, nüfus bilim (demografi) ve tıp alanında bebek ölümü olarak kabul edilmekte, tanımlanmaktadır. title: Antiterro et psychiatrie : un bref récap de la loi Rodwell
content:
Quelques infos sur la loi Rodwell, ou loi Philippine, passée fin juillet 2026


La loi Rodwell ou loi Philippine (oui oui, Philippine comme la meuf assassinée par un type sortant de

CRA

 en septembre 2024, provoquant une campagne de haine raciste et xénophobe), ou loi du 27 juillet 2026, est une loi qui mixe le droit pénal, le droit de la santé et le droit des étrangers pour «

 

prévenir le passage à l'acte terroriste

 

» - ambiance minority report.


Pour résumer, c'est un renforcement ou une adaptation de mesures répressives qui étaient déjà souvent présentes - et mises en place - dans le droit français : il y a peu de choses complètement nouvelles. On trouve intéressant d'analyser ici quelques unes de ses principales mesures, notamment du fait des liens étroits entre répression et psychiatrie, qui sont très explicites dans la loi.


La loi met en place :


1) Une rétention de sûreté terroriste à l'issue de la peine : enfermement d'une personne dans des établissements «

 

socio-médico-judiciaires de sûreté

 

» après l'exécution complète de sa peine. Cette mesure concernerait les personnes condamnées à une peine d'au moins quinze ans pour un crime de terrorisme. Une commission, peu avant la fin de la peine, doit déterminer si la personne présente une «

 

particulière dangerosité

 

», concept carrément flou évalué notamment sur des critères encore plus flous comme le «

 

risque de récidive

 

», «

 

l'adhésion persistante à une idéologie terroriste

 

» et un «

 

trouble grave de la personnalité

 

»...


Comme pour la plupart des mesures d'enfermement dans des établissements assimilables à des

HP

, il n'y a pas de durée maximale prévue par la loi - en général c'est un an, reconductible à peu près indéfiniment (le principe c'est que la personne y reste jusqu'à ce qu'elle ne représente plus un danger pour la société...)


Il est intéressant de noter que des mesures similaires existaient déjà depuis 2008 pour certains crimes de «

 

droit commun

 

» : meurtre, viol, torture, actes de barbarie, séquestration et enlèvement. Ça concernerait très peu de personnes actuellement, mais on se doute que cette loi va permettre de renflouer les dispositifs existants.


2) Une injonction préfectorale d'examen psychiatrique : de ce qu'on comprend, à n'importe quel moment (pas besoin d'être en gav ou en examen, ou même d'avoir «

 

troublé l'ordre public

 

»), le préfet peut obliger une personne à subir un examen psychiatrique approfondi - par un psychiatre figurant sur une liste établie par la cour d'appel. C'est vraiment sur la base de suspicion de «

 

radicalisation

 

» et de «

 

troubles mentaux

 

». Et bon quand on sait que les fichiers d'Hopsyweb sur les personnes hospitalisées sous contraintes sont croisés avec ceux des «

 

fichiers de traitement des signalements pour la prévention de la radicalisation à caractère terroriste

 

», cela fait déjà une bonne liste de potentiels suspects. Si le certificat médical émis par le psychiatre va dans ce sens, le préfet peut décider d'interner la personne en

HP

 sans son consentement (mais ça, ça existait déjà bien avant). Autant préciser que cette visite au toubib n'est pas facultative : on a la possibilité de faire appel au juge administratif en théorie, mais si on refuse de voir le psychiatre ou si on ne s'y présente pas dans le délai imparti, c'est perquiz, pour se rendre au rendez-vous sous escorte.


3) Une mesure judiciaire de rétention pour les condamnés de droit commun «

 

radicalisés

 

» - là, la loi viserait spécifiquement les gens qui seraient passés par la taule (au moins 10 ans) pour des faits non-liés au terrorisme, mais se seraient «

 

radicalisés

 

» en prison. Là encore, en fin de peine, une commission évalue si le détenu présente une «

 

dangerosité particulière

 

». Si oui, et contrairement à la rétention de sûreté terroriste, la personne n'est pas ré-enfermée, mais elle a droit à l'équivalent d'un suivi

SPIP

 très renforcé, pour veiller à sa «

 

réintégration

 

» : ce suivi peut inclure une obligation de taff ou de formation, un suivi psychiatrique, l'obligation d'habiter dans une zone déterminée... En gros, un contrôle très approfondi de la vie de la personne dans ses moindres aspects.


4) Le renforcement des

MICAS

 (avec notamment moins de possibilités de les contester). Ce sont les «

 

Mesures Individuelles de Contrôle Administratif et de Surveillance

 

», qui incluent déjà la possibilité de …

¿QUÉ es el patriotismo? ¿Es el amor por el lugar donde uno nació, el lugar de los recuerdos y las esperanzas de la infancia, de los sueños y las aspiraciones? ¿Es el lugar donde, con ingenuidad infantil, contemplábamos las nubes fugaces y nos preguntábamos por qué nosotros tampoco podíamos correr tan rápido? ¿El lugar donde contábamos los miles de millones de estrellas centelleantes, aterrorizados ante la idea de que cada una de ellas fuera «un ojo» que traspasara lo más profundo de nuestras pequeñas almas? ¿Es el lugar donde escuchábamos el canto de los pájaros y anhelábamos tener alas para volar, como ellos, hacia tierras lejanas? ¿O el lugar donde nos sentábamos a los pies de nuestra madre, embelesados por maravillosos relatos de grandes hazañas y conquistas? En resumen, ¿es el amor por ese lugar, donde cada pulgada representa recuerdos queridos y preciosos de una infancia feliz, alegre y juguetona?

Si eso fuera patriotismo, pocos hombres estadounidenses de hoy en día podrían considerarse patriotas, ya que el lugar de juego se ha convertido en fábrica, molino y mina, mientras que los sonidos ensordecedores de la maquinaria han sustituido a la música de los pájaros. Tampoco podemos ya escuchar las historias de grandes hazañas, pues las que cuentan hoy nuestras madres no son más que historias de dolor, lágrimas y aflicción.

¿Qué es, entonces, el patriotismo? «El patriotismo, señor, es el último recurso de los sinvergüenzas», dijo el Dr. Johnson. León Tolstói, el mayor antipatriota de nuestro tiempo, define el patriotismo como el principio que justifica la formación de asesinos en masa; un oficio que requiere mejor equipamiento para el ejercicio del asesinato que para la fabricación de artículos de primera necesidad como zapatos, ropa y viviendas; un oficio que garantiza mejores beneficios y mayor gloria que el del trabajador medio.

Gustave Hervé [1], otro gran antipatriota, califica acertadamente el patriotismo de superstición —una mucho más perjudicial, brutal e inhumana que la religión—. La superstición de la religión tuvo su origen en la incapacidad del hombre para explicar los fenómenos naturales. Es decir, cuando el hombre primitivo oía un trueno o veía un relámpago, no podía dar una explicación a ninguno de ellos y, por lo tanto, concluía que detrás de ellos debía de haber una fuerza mayor que él mismo. Del mismo modo, veía una fuerza sobrenatural en la lluvia y en los diversos cambios que se producen en la naturaleza. El patriotismo, por el contrario, es una superstición creada artificialmente y mantenida a través de una red de mentiras y falsedades; una superstición que despoja al hombre de su autoestima y dignidad, y aumenta su arrogancia y vanidad.

De hecho, la vanidad, la arrogancia y el egoísmo son los elementos esenciales del patriotismo. Permítanme ilustrarlo. El patriotismo parte de la base de que nuestro planeta está dividido en pequeños rincones, cada uno rodeado por una verja de hierro. Quienes han tenido la suerte de nacer en un rincón concreto se consideran mejores, más nobles, más grandiosos y más inteligentes que los seres vivos que habitan en cualquier otro rincón. Por lo tanto, es deber de todo aquel que vive en ese rincón elegido luchar, matar y morir en el intento de imponer su superioridad sobre todos los demás.

Los habitantes …

I den ungsocialistiska pressen hade så tidigt som år 1907 agitation förts för syndikalismen. I majnumret år 1910 av den fackliga tidningen Bageriarbetaren gjorde bagarnas förtroendeman, Anders Sjöstedt, som var redaktör för nämnda tidning, ett försök att hindra syndikalismens spridning bland bagarna, vilka i stort antal gripits av den syndikalistiska agitationen. Då skrev undertecknad ett genmäle mot den mäktiga förbundschefens angrepp under rubriken: **.."Man säger... Genmäle på artikeln i majnumret."*

"Man säger, att bagarna skola vara med då det gäller att upplösa förbunden och bilda Lokala Samorganisationer", inledde vår förtroendeman Anders Sjöstedt, och tillade sedan: "Tack för erbjudandet, men skall man då behandla bagarna på samma sätt som man vill göra nu, tycker vi synd om bagarna." På detta sätt vill jag svara att aggressiva kommer arbetsgivarna alltid att vara oavsett vilken organisationsform arbetarna har, tills dess de får så kraftigt mothugg så de lugnar sina rovdjurskänslor. Och då behövs det sannerligen syndikalistiskt försvarskraft. Därför kan inte en förtroendeman, om än med stor vilja, uträtta något ensamt - utan en vaken, handlingsfull och slagkraftig organisation.

Lusten att krossa arbetarnas organisationer har icke saknats av de privata arbetsgivarna - ej ens från styrelser och föreståndare för kooperativa bagerier i södra Sverge. Närmare angivet Skåne. Där har till och med öppna strider utbrutit.

Alla arbetsgivare vill ha utgifterna så små som möjligt. Men inkomsterna så stora som möjligt. Detta får ju främst arbetarna, producenterna, lida för.

Vidare hade Sjöstedt skrivit: "Lyssna på styrelserna för 'Föreningsbagerierna' och och för en del kooperativa bagerier vilka diskutera om bagarna på ett utmanande sätt, när det gäller deras avtal."

För min del tyckte jag att bagarna icke skulle bry sig om vad dessa konservativa styrelsemedlemmar pladdrar om. Och är det någon underhandling de ej vill bry sig om och önskar de icke vara med om någon överenskommelse som vi vet att de kan gå med på, behöver vi icke kompromissa och springa och berusa dessa herrar i all evighet, och tigga om rätt till mänsklig existens. Vi ha förmåga att slå till! Vi äro de starka! Gör slut på fegheten! Det är vi som är producenter!

Därför behöva att omändra organisationerna till kampduglighet och smidig anpassningsförmåga efter de förhållanden som kan uppstå. Vad de Lokala Samorganisationerna angår så äro de mest praktiska, och kan med heder avlösa de gamla tungrodda byråkratiska fackföreningarna, som äro i majoritet i detta land.

Att inte organisationsfrågan är ett aktuellt spörsmål just nu, bland bagarna, är en lögn av stort mått. Den är aktuell och skall bliva det ännu mer när tiden är mogen. Trots vad Sjöstedt skriver! Och hans ångest som så tydligt märks!

Allt sedan de reformistiska organisationernas början har i regel "förts de korslagda armarnas strid", som de gamla ledana är så förtjusta i - till borgardömets fromma!

Detta har visat sig odugligt. Vi har ju bagerier, som är bojkottade ända sedan den tid som "Svenska Bageri- och Konditoriarbetareförbundet" startades. Och det var inte i går!

Vi har exempel på detta i Göteborg och i Uddevalla, ja lite varstans i detta land.

Det skulle taga allt för stort utrymme i anspråk att räkna upp alla. Och när uppgörelse kommer att träffas vet ingen! Och ingen gör något för att ändring skall ske. Ingen delar ut så mycket som en bojkottslapp för att upplysa allmänheten om förhållandet, att konflikt råder. Därför behövs det pigga organisationer i vilka medlemmarna äro socialistiskt skolade och nyktra. Då kan vi marschera framåt och vinna något, trots det att arbetsgivarna göra allt för att slå ned vår frammarsch. Detta få ingen glömma!

Man skriver så ofta och påstår att folk är så egoistiska, att de ej vill betala avgifterna till föreningarna …

author: 张皓翔
title: The Dislocation of Vendémiaire (II): The Illusion of National Economics and the Polarization of Political Economy【葡月的错位（二）国民经济学的幻象与政治经济学的极化】【A commentary on the French riots between September and October】
content: This essay, titled The Dislocation of Vendémiaire, explores the theoretical and practical contradictions within contemporary capitalist society, using the socio-political unrest in France as a backdrop. Grounded in Marxist philosophy and dialectics, the author critically examines the illusion of national economics and the polarization of political economy. By distinguishing between "national economics" (which obscures exploitation through material comfort) and "political economy" (which reveals the deep alienation of social relations), the text argues that modern digital capitalism has stripped workers of their "wealth of real relations" (现实关系的财富). The essay articulates a fundamental shift from the "first struggle" (economic demands for wages and welfare) to the "second struggle" (reclaiming the autonomy of labor production and resisting the reduction of human beings to mere production factors). Ultimately, it posits that the recent French protests represent a historical "dislocation"—an attempt at the second struggle without the necessary political foundation of the first.

 Приглашённый, почти вынужденный любезными настояниями выступить на заключительном заседании недавнего конгресса Итальянского синдикального союза, я сказал вещи, которые возмутили «чистых синдикалистов», не понравились некоторым товарищам – возможно, потому что были сочтены неуместными, – и, что хуже, вызвали более или менее заинтересованные аплодисменты других, посторонних Синдикальному союзу, которые очень далеки от моих идей и моих намерений.


 И всё же я лишь повторил мнения, которые высказывал тысячу раз и которые, как мне кажется, составляют неотъемлемую часть анархической программы!


 Полезно будет вернуться к этому ещё раз.


 Не следует смешивать «синдикализм», который хочет быть доктриной и методом решения социального вопроса, с созданием, существованием и деятельностью рабочих профсоюзов.


 Рабочие профсоюзы (лиги сопротивления и другие проявления рабочего движения) несомненно полезны: они даже являются необходимой фазой подъема пролетариата. Они стремятся дать трудящимся сознание их истинного положения эксплуатируемых и рабов, развивают в них желание изменить своё состояние, приучают их к солидарности и к борьбе и, благодаря практике борьбы, дают им понять, что хозяева – враги, а правительство – защитник хозяев. Улучшения, которых можно добиться путём рабочей борьбы, – конечно, малая вещь: они оставляют в силе принцип эксплуатации и угнетения одного класса другим и всегда находятся под угрозой быть сведёнными на нет или вовсе уничтоженными игрой преобладающих экономических сил; но даже ненадежные и иллюзорные, эти улучшения служат также тому, чтобы помешать массе приспособиться и отупеть в неизменной нищете, которая отнимает даже понятие и желание лучшей жизни. А революция, какой мы её хотим, совершаемая массами и развивающаяся действием масс, без навязывания открытых или замаскированных

[1]

 диктатур, вряд ли могла бы произойти и укрепиться без предшествующего существования широкого движения масс.


 Впрочем, что бы о нём ни думали, профсоюзное движение – это факт, который навязывает себя и не нуждается в нашем признании, чтобы существовать. Оно есть естественный плод, в нынешних социальных условиях, зарождающегося бунта угнетённых; и было бы нелепо, а также вредно, требовать, чтобы трудящиеся отказались от попыток добиться немедленных улучшений, пусть даже малых, в ожидании полного освобождения, которое должно стать результатом полного социального преобразования, совершённого путём революции.


 Поэтому мы, как анархисты, прежде всего озабоченные осуществлением нашего идеала, отнюдь не должны устраняться от рабочего движения, а должны принимать в нём активное участие и стараться, чтобы оно, приспосабливаясь к текущим потребностям повседневной мелкой борьбы, развивалось наименее противоречащим нашим стремлениям образом и становилось всё более действенным средством морального подъёма и революции.


 Но всё это не есть «синдикализм», который хочет быть доктриной и практикой самим по себе и утверждает, что рабочая организация, созданная для сопротивления и текущей борьбы за ныне достижимые улучшения, естественно, с её ростом и расширением, приведёт к полному преобразованию социальных институтов и будет условием и гарантией эгалитарного и либертарного общества.


 Вполне объяснима склонность каждого человека придавать наибольшее значение работе, которую он делает, роду деятельности, которым он занимается, – и если есть такие, кто, занимаясь антиалкоголизмом, неомальтузианством, реформой питания, международным языком и так далее и тому подобное, в конце концов увидел в своей крошечной, фрагментарной пропаганде панацею от всех социальных зол, то поистине нечего удивляться, что те, кто отдал весь свой энтузиазм, всю свою деятельность столь важному и обширному движению, как рабочее движение, часто кончают тем, что делают из него панацею, универсальное и достаточное средство.


 И действительно, были, особенно во Франции, анархисты, которые, войдя в рабочее движение с лучшими намерениями, чтобы принести наше слово и наши методы в массы, были затем поглощены и перекованы, подняли клич «

синдикализм достаточен сам по себе…

» и вскоре перестали быть анархистами. Не говоря о тех, кто сознательно предал, они перестали быть и синдикалистами и под предлогом

Священного Союза

[2]

 поставили себя на службу правительству и хозяевам.


 Но если синдикалистский …

author: Unknown
title: Martin H. - Barry Pateman: An Appreciation
content:
Author

: Martin H.

Title

: Barry Pateman: An Appreciation

Date

: 2026-10-21

Notes

: [First posted on the Kate Sharpley Library website]

Source

: https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/c2ft1b


 It’s important to appreciate those who have come before us. I first met Barry through Albert Meltzer, probably at a bookfair. I’d learned to trust that if Albert thought well of someone, he was probably right. Barry was an impressive man, physically and mentally, with the sort of self-deprecating humour instantly recognisable to anyone brought up in a British working class environment. And he was able to talk to people, without the sort of academic language that can be so off-putting.


 The times I saw him were few and far between but they were always memorable. Barry was brimming with ideas, whether about anarchist history, theory and practice, sport or wider culture. Like Albert he had a high regard for the autodidacts – especially those miner militants whose self-education far outstripped those who had had a university education. He was good company.


 It was perhaps telling that I learned of Barry’s death a few days after returning from Ron Marsden’s funeral. Both had been intimately involved in the tension between organising as anarchists and remaining accessible to ordinary people. It’s a tension that runs through most of the anarchist organising and groups that I have been part of in my life, and one I kept promising Barry I would write something about – the organisations that can never get above Dunbar’s number

[1]

 in membership without splitting, the affinity groups claiming to be membership organisations, the strategies designed for different times, the insights from Stuart Christie’s autobiography about affinity groups. Sorry, mate, life always seemed to get in the way, I am way too easily distracted….


 He was generous with his time and his thoughts. He had many strings to his bow – as you would expect from someone who admired those self-educated working class militants – as was so warmly described by the guy who knew him from the New Zealand Cricket Museum at the memorial service.


 Barry would regularly talk about how militant young miners from South Yorkshire were interested in the Direct Action Movement, during the height of the 1984–5 strike. But as they weren’t fully formed anarchists, DAM couldn’t accept them, despite their hard won experience of class struggle. It was this discussion that led DAM to become the Solidarity Federation (alongside other struggles like the Ardbride dispute 1986–87). Unfortunately, with a fabulous sense of timing, SF’s orientation towards labour movement militants happened at exactly the time the pool of labour movement militants shrank, following the catastrophic defeats of the 80s and early 90s. Barry saw the effects of these defeats first hand, as the mutual aid of the strike gave way to desperation and the destruction of former mining areas by a vengeful government. There were successes, most notably the Workmates group on the privatised part of the Tube, but that also swerved the same organisational question by staying independent – it wasn’t part of SF and as far as I know no one outside the originators ever joined SF. The arguments around SF’s industrial strategy, of building trust and organisation in a workplace and then tackling issues from that base are not new

[2]

 – but the obstacles to winning over new people to an anarcho-syndicalist project through this activity remain substantial.


 One of the commitments of the KSL has always been to uncover the motivations and actions of the unknown militants, who didn’t leave piles of writings for posterity. Barry was assertive that we hear the true voices of our forebears, not mediated by what we think now and what we want to bolster our own current views. We are much richer for that approach. The histories published by KSL are accessible to the general reader. The context is there. The achievements are many: Recognising the importance of Guillamon’s work on the Spanish revolution and ending the myth of the spontaneous uprising in 1936, achieved without any groundwork. And his work on the early 20

th

 century movement and Emma Goldman stands out.


 He kept looking for ways to spread the ideas of anarchism, and always in an outward-facing way. Whether through solidarity with strikers and others in struggle, through engaging with younger anarchists, or through the achievements of the Kate Sharpley Library he …

author: Majid00
title: روش‌های سازمان‌یابی کمونیستی
content:
This essay is the second part of The Dislocation of Vendémiaire, following Part I, “The Disruptors of the 21st Century and the Ideological Collusion.” While Part I interprets the 2026 France-centered student-led protest wave as a politically dislocated movement—one misread by mainstream discourse as a multi-class coalition when it is in fact an expression of fragmentation within the proletariat—Part II develops the theoretical argument behind that claim. Drawing on Marx’s thesis of society’s polarization into two hostile camps, it distinguishes between “property” and “proletarianization” in the sense of national economics and in the sense of political economy. The essay argues that class should be analyzed through the actual control over the production of labor-power, and that digital capitalism increasingly enables capital to dominate labor-power directly, beyond the mediation of formal ownership of physical means of production. On this basis, it explains why many who appear as middle-class or petty-producer subjects in national-economic terms—scholars, franchise shopkeepers, senior programmers, platform creators—are in political-economic terms being proletarianized, while carrying petty-bourgeois habits of political compromise, individualism, hostility to centralized discipline, and identity- or interest-based linkage. The result is a form of struggle that is radical in appearance but conservative and spontaneous in its core: it completes the first step of linkage through identity and affinity, but fails to return to the common ground of class interests and to connect with the broader industrial working class.
