author: infolibre
title: Παρεμβάσεις ενάντια στα εργοδοτικά εγκλήματα και την ακρίβεια, Παρασκευή 23/10
content:
>Συγκέντρωση ενάντια στις εργοδοτικές δολοφονίες στη Motor oil, 19:00 Προπύλαια


>Παρέμβαση ενάντια στην ακρίβεια και τις εργοδοτικές αυθαιρεσίες, 19:00 πλατεία Μαρτάκη (Παγκράτι – Βύρωνας)


Συγκέντρωση ενάντια στις εργοδοτικές δολοφονίες στη Motor oil


ΤΟ ΑΙΜΑ ΤΩΝ ΕΡΓΑΤΩΝ/ΤΡΙΩΝ – ΤΑ ΠΛΟΥΤΗ ΤΩΝ ΑΦΕΝΤΙΚΩΝ


Το πρωί της Παρασκευής 9 Οκτωβρίου ύστερα από έκρηξη στις εγκαταστάσεις της MOTOR OIL στους Αγίους Θεοδώρους τραυματίστηκαν σοβαρά 5 εργάτες εκ των οποίων ο ένας λίγες ώρες αργότερα κατέληξε, ενώ στις 11 Οκτωβρίου ένας ακόμα από τους πολυτραυματίες χάνει τη ζωή του. Την Πέμπτη 15 Οκτωβρίου μια νέα ισχυρή έκρηξη σημειώθηκε στις εγκαταστάσεις της Motor Oil, αφήνοντας πίσω της 4 τραυματισμένους εργάτες, 2 εκ των οποίων με πολλαπλά κατάγματα και εγκαύματα. Και αυτά τα προδιαγεγραμμένα φρικτά εργοδοτικά εγκλήματα έρχονται να προστεθούν στις ήδη περισσότερες από 140 δολοφονίες εργατών/τριών του 2026 (και πάνω από 220 τραυματίες) και στις αναρίθμητες των προηγούμενων ετών, στις οποίες αντανακλάται με κυνισμό η όξυνση της εργασιακής εκμετάλλευσης και η οικτρή πραγματικότητα των εργασιακών συνθηκών στις οποίες καλούμαστε να δουλέψουμε όλες και όλοι.


Η προώθηση των διαδικασιών της κρατικής και καπιταλιστικής αναδιάρθρωσης εντείνει με γοργούς ρυθμούς την επίθεση στον κόσμο της εργασίας με την ολοένα και μεγαλύτερη όξυνση των συνθηκών εκμετάλλευσης. Η επίθεση αυτή συντελεί στην εγκαθίδρυση ενός μεσαίωνα στην εργασιακή πραγματικότητα. Η εργοδοτική αυθαιρεσία σε συνδυασμό με την απελευθέρωση των απολύσεων επιτείνουν την επισφαλή και «μαύρη» εργασία, εντείνουν σε ακραίο βαθμό την εκμετάλλευση χιλιάδων εργαζομένων και θέτουν στο προσκήνιο τον διαρκή εκβιασμό της ανεργίας, την ίδια στιγμή που τα εξαντλητικά ωράρια οδηγούν στην συνεπακόλουθη μείωση ως και εκμηδένιση του ελεύθερου χρόνου όσων εργάζονται. Η κατάργηση των συλλογικών συμβάσεων και εργατικών κεκτημένων κατακερματίζει τις ταξικές αντιστάσεις και αποδυναμώνει τις συλλογικές διεκδικήσεις στους χώρους εκμετάλλευσης, γεγονός που σε συνδυασμό με την πλήρη αποθράσυνση των αφεντικών συντελεί στη ραγδαία αύξηση των εργατικών ατυχημάτων και δολοφονιών στα κάτεργα της μισθωτής σκλαβιάς στο βωμό της καπιταλιστικής και κρατικής κερδοφορίας και ανάπτυξης. Οι δεκάδες δολοφονίες εργατών στα κάτεργα της σύγχρονης δουλείας μαρτυρούν οτι οι εκμεταλλευόμενοι και οι καταπιεσμένοι συνεχίζουν να πληρώνουν με το αίμα τους τη διατήρηση και αναπαραγωγή του βάρβαρου εκμεταλλευτικού και καταπιεστικού συστήματος, που καταδυναστεύει, δολοφονεί, εξαθλιώνει. Αυτό ακριβώς καταδεικνύει η εργοδοτική δολοφονία 5 εργατριών στο εργοστάσιο της Βιολάντα στα Τρίκαλα, μετά από έκρηξη που διέλυσε τις εγκαταστάσεις στις οποίες εργάζονταν, και από την οποία τραυματίστηκαν άλλοι 7 εργάτες. Σήμερα, και αφού επιχειρήθηκε θεσμικά από την πρώτη στιγμή να συγκαλυφθούν οι ευθύνες της εργοδοσίας, το αφεντικό του εργοστασίου Τζιωρτζιώτης βρίσκεται ελεύθερος μετά από την απόφαση του συμβουλίου πλημμελειοδικών Τρικάλων με την οποία έληξε η προφυλάκισή του. Αυτό ακριβώς καταδεικνύει και η εργοδοτική δολοφονία 2 εργατών σε εργοστάσιο στον Ασπρόπυργο τον Ιούλιο του 2026 μετά από έκρηξη λόγω διαρροής εύφλεκτου αερίου, ο τραυματισμός άλλων 11, εκ των οποίων ο ένας νοσηλεύεται ακόμα με πολλά εγκαύματα. Η έκρηξη στα διυλιστήρια της motor oil, στη Βιολάντα και στον Ασπρόπυργο δεν είναι ούτε τυχαία γεγονότα, ούτε ατυχήματα, αλλά αντίθετα αποτελούν την κορυφή του παγόβουνου της άγριας ταξικής εκμετάλλευσης που επιβάλλεται στους χώρους δουλειάς, αποτελούν προδιαγεγραμμένα κρατικά και καπιταλιστικά εγκλήματα.


Οι εκατοντάδες δολοφονημένοι εργάτες/τριες στα κάτεργα της μισθωτής σκλαβιάς, οι χιλιάδες πρόσφυγες και μετανάστες/τριες, που όταν δεν βυθίζονται στη θάλασσα από το ελληνικό λιμενικό, βασανίζονται και φυλακίζονται σε στρατόπεδα συγκέντρωσης, οι 57 νέοι/ες που δολοφονήθηκαν στο κρατικό έγκλημα στα Τέμπη, οι απόκληροι που πέφτουν νεκροί στα αστυνομικά μπλόκα και οι χιλιάδες αγωνιστές/στριες που στους δρόμους και τις διαδηλώσεις χτυπιούνται με μανία από τους ένστολους δολοφόνους της δημοκρατίας αποτελούν μόνο ένα μικρό μέρος της πραγματικότητας της συνολικής βαρβαρότητας, που επιβάλουν στη μεγάλη κοινωνική πλειοψηφία κράτος και αφεντικά.


Το βάθεμα του σύγχρονου ολοκληρωτισμού εκδηλώνεται αφενός με τις συνεχείς και δυσμενέστερες αναδιαρθρώσεις σε κάθε πεδίο του κοινωνικού και ταξικού ανταγωνισμού αλλά και την προετοιμασία της κοινωνικής βάσης για μια εμπόλεμη κοινωνία, την εμπέδωση μιας συνθήκης σιωπής και ταυτόχρονα υποταγής …

author: Unknown
title: DEM Party criticizes the government over the process: Why are steps toward peace being delayed?
content:
The Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) spokesperson Ayşegül Doğan assessed the progress of the Peace and Democratic Society Process at a press conference following her party’s Central Executive Committee (MYK) meeting. Stating that the process was being delayed, Doğan said uncertainties surrounding democratization and legal reforms persisted despite statements from the government.


 


When will Abdullah Öcalan’s conditions be changed?


Recalling the call made by Nationalist Movement Party (MHP) leader Devlet Bahçeli in parliament on October 22, 2024, Ayşegül Doğan stated that no significant changes had been made to Öcalan’s conditions since then, apart from visits by the DEM Party’s Imrali delegation.


Doğan noted that family visits had not been placed on a regular schedule either.


“Since the call made on October 22, 2024, changes to Mr. Öcalan’s conditions have been limited to visits by the DEM Party’s Imrali delegation. Family visits are taking place, but there is no regular schedule for them. So, as a political party that frequently seeks answers to this question, we ask: When will these conditions change?”


Who is delaying the process?


Emphasizing that reciprocal steps are necessary for the process to move forward, Doğan recalled that the PKK had declared a ceasefire, convened its congress and announced its decision to dissolve, destroyed its weapons, and declared its withdrawal from Turkey.


Despite these developments, Doğan said, uncertainties surrounding the legal framework needed to pave the way for democratic politics had yet to be resolved.


“When will the Peace and Political Participation Council begin its work, and why is it being delayed? Who is holding up these efforts?” she asked.


Doğan added: “We want the process to move forward through new confidence-building steps that address the concerns of the public. All parties already acknowledge that everything causing the process to be prolonged must somehow be resolved. Because prolonging the process could, to use one of the most frequently employed terms in this context, infect the process itself. If all parties agree on this assessment, then what are we waiting for?”


Arbitrary obstacles to prisoners’ release


Ayşegül Doğan stated that human rights violations in prisons were also incompatible with the progress of the peace process. Citing data from the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD), she reported that prison administrative and observation boards had postponed the release of at least 90 prisoners over the past three months.


Doğan said that political prisoners at Ankara Sincan Women’s Closed Prison were being denied their right to conditional release and called on the Ministry of Justice to take concrete action rather than merely issue statements.


She stated that Şermin Demirdağ’s release had been blocked for the eighth time, while the release of Mehmet Sait Yıldırım, a seriously ill 75-year-old prisoner who has been incarcerated for 31 years, had been postponed on the grounds that he had not expressed remorse.


Doğan noted that the release of Ali Adıman, held in Bolu F-Type Prison, had been postponed because he used the phrase “Mr. Öcalan” in a petition.


Call for press freedom and release of imprisoned journalists


Ayşegül Doğan criticized the continued pressure on journalists, politicians, writers, and human rights defenders at a time when peace and democratization are being discussed. She noted that restrictions on access to social media accounts and the closure of television channels were continuing.


Calling for the release of imprisoned journalists and the removal of restrictions on access to information, Doğan emphasized that steps toward democratization must guarantee freedom of expression, freedom of association, and freedom of the press.

author: Unknown
title: Altun: We must dedicate 24 hours a day to Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom
content:
Kenan Altun, who had been imprisoned for 30 years, was released from Maltepe No. 1 L-Type Prison. Welcomed outside the prison, Altun said, “We have been released after 30 years, but Abdullah Öcalan is still inside. If we do not dedicate our 24 hours to Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom, we will not achieve results.”


 


Altun also delivered the following message: “All our friends send their greetings. On their behalf and my own, I thank you for welcoming me. Many of our friends inside are ill. I have just left behind a friend who is 84 years old and still in prison. Nevertheless, both I and all our friends are in very high spirits. They all send you their warmest greetings.


All our people must work together and dedicate our 24 hours to peace. We know that the burden we carry is very heavy. This is not a time to sit back; on the contrary, it is a time to intensify the struggle. For all the sacrifices we have made, for our future, and for our children, we must dedicate our 24 hours to the struggle.”

author: Rizomatica
title: Comunicado de los Presos políticos Mapuche de la cárcel de Temuco tras Marcha por la Resistencia del 12 de octubre
content:
«Nosotros los prisioneros políticos mapuche recluidos en la cárcel de temuko saludamos a nuestras autoridades tradicionales y a todos quienes fueron participe de la gran movilización llevada adelante, el lunes 12 de octubre en la ciudad de temuko.


Mediante este escrito, venimos a agradecer la gran convocatoria realizada este 12 de octubre en apoyo concreto a los PPM de la cárcel de Temuco y a sus demandas, por parte del movimiento social en toda su amplitud.


Agradecemos a todos aquellos y aquellas que pusieron sus ganas y newen para que todo resultara de la mejor manera: a nuestros familiares, pu afkadi, autoridades tradicionales, comunidades en resistencia de diversos puntos del wallmapu, wenuy y simpatizantes de nuestra causa.


Hoy, a días de la gran movilización, creemos que esta logró los objetivos esperados con creces. Por tanto, agradecemos a nuestro pueblo por demostrar su fuerza cuando se lo propone.


La unidad en el weichan la entendemos como aquella en la que todo nuestro pueblo tiene su espacio, en sus distintas formas, con sus aciertos y errores. Aquí tienen cabida todos quienes busquen ser partícipes de la unidad que, como pueblo mapuche, merecemos darnos. Desde el pichiche hasta los kuifiche, todo nuestro pueblo tiene su espacio cuando se trata de levantar un movimiento social mapuche sólido, capaz de reunir la fuerza necesaria para luchar por lo que nos pertenece.


Eso sí, esta unidad debe construirse siempre desde la transparencia y la honestidad, sin dar cabida a los personalismos ni a las supuestas cualidades morales particulares.


Reconocemos también a cada uno de los peñi, ka pu lamngen y wenny de la causa mapuche que destinaron un día que podrían haber utilizado para descansar o compartir con sus familias en casa, y que, en cambio, se dieron el ánimo de asistir para expresar su solidaridad consciente con los familiares y los PPM.


Extendemos, finalmente, nuestros agradecimientos a todo el movimiento social mapuche que, cuando se lo propone, demuestra que es posible confluir en ideas y aspiraciones que aglutinan y suman. Esto cobra especial relevancia en los tiempos que corren, en los que la atomización y el individualismo prevalecen por sobre la justa intención de juntarse y organizarse, con el propósito de ser partícipes concretos del movimiento social mapuche autónomo.


Fei taiñ feipiaiñ may. Chaltu may kom eimun!


¡¡KIÑEWKULEAIÑ WEICHAN MEW!!


Fin a las altas condenas


Fin a la dispersión de los ppm


Fin al estado de excepción en wall mapu


No a la aplicación de la ley antiterrorista


A más de 500 años de resistencia no pudieron ni podrán borrar la memoria del mapuzungun. «


*Enviado a la radio.


Esta información se publicó en

Radio Kurruf

.

author: Unknown
title: Emir: SPK, 455 bin 758 mağdurun hakkını gasbedenlere kalkan olma derdinde
content:
Yeni Parti Grup Başkanvekili Murat Emir, "Suçüstü yakalanan Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), gece yarısı önergesini aklamak için bugün panikle bir duyuru yayımlamış ama kendi kendini ele vermiş. Onca manipülasyon olurken koltuğunda oturup seyreden SPK yönetimi, şimdi kelime oyunlarıyla 455 bin 758 mağdurun hakkını gasbeden gece yarısı önergesine kalkan olma derdinde" dedi.

Emir, SPK'nın "Takas kesinliği ve PBLK husularına ilişkin basın duyurusu" başlıklı açıklamasına sosyal medya hesabından tepki gösterdi. SPK'nın kendini ele verdiğini söyleyen Emir, şunları kaydetti: "Suçüstü yakalanan SPK, gece yarısı önergesini aklamak için bugün panikle bir bir duyuru yayımlamış ama kendi kendini ele vermiş. SPK duyurusunda 'Sermaye Piyasası Kanunu 79. maddesine göre takas talimat ve işlemleri tasfiye halinde dahi geri alınamaz ve iptal edilemez ama PBLK’da bekleyen satış talimatları takasın başladığı anlamına gelmez' diyor. O zaman size sormak isterim; kanunun 79. maddesi sadece tamamlanmış işlemleri değil, açıkça 'takas talimatlarını' da koruma altına alıyor. Yatırımcının payını TEFAS İşlem Blokaj Alt Hesabına (PBLK) alıp bloke koymak takas sürecini başlatmak değilse nedir? AKP’nin gece yarısı önergesinde tam 4 defa 'ilgili fonun temerrüdü' yazarken, SPK bugünkü duyurusunda 'temerrüt' kelimesini neden sansürleyip metinden tamamen çıkardı? Çünkü ortada doğmuş bir nakit borcu olmadan temerrüt olmayacağını kendileri de çok iyi biliyor. Madem PBLK’daki 250 bin mağdur zaten alacaklı değil ve doğal olarak fon pay sahibi sayılıyordu, o zaman dün gece mahkeme yolunu kapatmak için neden apar topar kanuna madde eklediniz? Onca manipülasyon olurken koltuğunda oturup seyreden SPK yönetimi, şimdi kelime oyunlarıyla 455 bin 758 mağdurun hakkını gasbeden gece yarısı önergesine kalkan olma derdinde."

title: TBMM Başkanı Kurtulmuş: Süreç planlandığı gibi ilerliyor, hiçbir şey geç kalmıyor
content:
Ankara - Türkiye Büyük Millet Meclisi (TBMM) Başkanı Numan Kurtulmuş, Türkiye’yi ziyaret eden Lüksemburg Temsilciler Meclisi Başkanı Claude Wiseler ile düzenlediği ortak basın toplantısında, çözüm sürecine ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulundu.

Sürecin Türkiye’nin en önemli sorunlarından birinin çözümüne yönelik yürütüldüğünü vurgulayan Kurtulmuş, Meclis’teki siyasi partilerin katılımıyla hazırlanan raporun kabul edilmesini demokratik açıdan önemli bir başarı olarak nitelendirdi.

Kurtulmuş, sürecin planlandığı şekilde ilerlediğini belirterek, Meclis bünyesinde kurulması öngörülen izleme kuruluna ilişkin siyasi partilerle görüşmelerin sürdüğünü ve kurulun önümüzdeki günlerde oluşturulacağını açıkladı.

Kurtulmuş şunları söyledi; "Bir taraftan örgütün silahsızlanması, fesih sürecinin devam ettiği; bir taraftan da bu sürecin özellikle uygulamada nasıl seyredeceğine ilişkin oluşturulan üst kurulun çalışmalarına devam etmesi zaten planlandığı gibi gidiyor. Bunun bir ayağı da Türkiye Büyük Millet Meclisi ayağıdır. Biz başından itibaren bir iddiada bulunuyoruz: Bu model özgün bir modeldir ve Türkiye modelidir. Bu modelin nasıl işlediği, bu sürecin nasıl yönetildiğine ilişkin asla dışarıdan bir göz olmayacak. Asla üçüncü bir göz işin içerisine müdahil olamayacaktır. Milletin tamamı adına Meclis bütün farklılıklarıyla, partileriyle bu süreci yönetecek”

Meclis'te de yasanın gerektirdiği izleme kurulu kurulacağını belirten Kurtulmuş; “Önümüzdeki günlerde bu kurulu kurarız. Nasıl olacağı ile ilgili olarak siyasi partiler ile zaten yasanın çıktığının ertesi gününden itibaren müzakerelerimizi yapıyoruz. Önümüzdeki günlerde bu konu ete kemiğe bürünür. Ben bir şey söylemiştim, onu bilerek söyledim: Her şey kendi yolunda tıkır tıkır işliyor. Hiçbir şey geç kalmıyor. Böylesine önemli bir konuda herkes üzerine düşen sorumluluğu yerine getirsin. Kimse bir diğerine ödev vermeye kalkmasın. Terör örgütü silahsızlanma sürecini sürdürecek ve bunu sonlandıracak. Siyaset üstüne düşen sorumluluğu şimdiye kadar yaptığı gibi bundan sonra da başarıyla yapacak ve inşallah bu süreç tıkır tıkır işleyecektir, sonlanacaktır. Milletimizin bu konuda büyük bir beklentisi ve büyük bir desteği vardır. Kimse bu desteği boşa çıkaracak sözlerin içerisinde olmasın” dedi.

Mekke Ortak Savunma Anlaşması'nda sürecin nasıl işleyeceğinin sorulması üzerine ise Kurtulmuş, "Mekke Anlaşması bildiğiniz gibi Türkiye, Pakistan ve Suudi Arabistan'ın uzlaşmaya vardığı bir anlaşma. Cumhurbaşkanlığı'ndan bu konuyla ilgili yasa teklifi bize geldiği zaman ben de hemen bunu Türkiye Büyük Millet Meclisi'ne, önce komisyona, sonra da Genel Kurula geçecek. Dolayısıyla önce komisyonda tartışılacak. Komisyonda kabul edilirse Türkiye Büyük Millet Meclisi Genel Kuruluna gelecek ve Türkiye Büyük Millet Meclisi'nde yapılan müzakereler sonrasında da kabul edilirse yasalaşacak. Süreç budur, usul budur ve her şey usulüne uygun bir şekilde işliyor" ifadesini kullandı.

Lüksemburg Temsilciler Meclisi Başkanı Claude Wiseler ise "Son dönemde özellikle başta Fransa olmak üzere Avrupa'nın birçok başkentinde artan şiddetli protestoları görüyoruz, dikkat çekiyor. Bununla birlikte Avrupa'daki bu artan tansiyonu, artan gerilimi nasıl değerlendiriyorsunuz? Ayrıca bu gelişmelerin Avrupa'nın siyasi ve toplumsal geleceğine etkileri hakkında ne düşünüyorsunuz" sorusunu şöyle yanıtladı:

"İlk olarak, şimdi Lüksemburg'da böyle bir gerilim yok hâlihazırda. Toplum olarak barış, huzur içerisinde yaşıyoruz kendi ülkemizde, Lüksemburg sınırları içerisinde. Yani Lüksemburg'la ilgili bir soru değil ama tabii ki diğer ülkelerde gerçekleşen durumlar, tabii ki ekonomik durum, buna yönelik baskılar; tabii ki işte petrol fiyatlarının, bazı ülkelerdeki konut fiyatlarının artıyor olması sosyal anlamda birçok soruna neden oluyor ve bunlar da tabii ki bazı ülkelerde bu şekilde daha belki şiddetli bir şekilde vuku buluyor. Bunun tabii ki ülkelerin siyasetlerine etkisi var. Başka ülkelerin siyasetlerine de etkisi olabilir ama daha ziyade ülkelere münferit bakmak gerekiyor. Ve bu sorunların tabii ki çözülmesi için ekonomik olarak, sosyal olarak çalışmak gerekecektir."

author: Unknown
title: Ümit Özlale, Taha Çakmak'a sordu: Kamu kaynaklarıyla fondan erken çıkışlar finanse edildi mi?
content:
Yeni Parti İzmir Milletvekili Ümit Özlale, fon vurgunu soruşturmasında iki özel kalem personeli gözaltına alınan, kendisi de istifa eden eski Türkiye Sigorta Genel Müdürü Taha Çakmak’a, Karayipler’deki Artsmrkts Ltd, Londra’daki GildenCrest ve İsviçre’deki Century City Securities üzerinden hesabına veya menfaatine işlem yapılıp yapılmadığını sordu. Kişisel yatırımlarıyla yönettiği şirketlerin fon yatırımları arasında çıkar çatışması bulunup bulunmadığını soran Özlale, Türkiye Sigorta ve Türkiye Hayat ve Emeklilik kaynakları ile BES fonlarından TERA ve bağlantılı kuruluşlara yapılan yatırımların açıklanmasını istedi.

Özlale'nin sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamalar ve gündeme taşıdığı sorular şöyle:

"Taha Çakmak’ın kamu kaynaklarıyla kişisel yatırımlarının yolları kesişti mi? Taha Çakmak, fon vurgunundaki en kritik isimlerden biri ve sahibi bu ülkenin vatandaşları olan Türkiye Sigorta ile Türkiye Hayat ve Emeklilik’in geçen haftaya kadar genel müdürüydü. Daha önce de BDDK ve Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası (TCMB) Başkan Yardımcılığı gibi en kritik makamlarda oturdu. Cebimizdeki 50 TL’lik banknotlarda imzası bulunan bir isimdi. Bugün ise Taha Çakmak’ın özel kalem personelleri Fahri Uğur ve Hakan Eryılmaz aynı fon ve hisse soruşturması kapsamında gözaltına alındı.

Kamuoyunu aydınlatmak için Çakmak’a ve yetkililere şu soruları yöneltiyoruz: BDDK’de üst düzey yöneticiyken TERA Yatırım’da kendi adınıza, BDDK’deki resmi e-posta adresinizin kayıtlı olduğu bir müşteri hesabı açtınız mı? TERA Yatırım, Londra merkezli GildenCrest (Tera Europe) veya bunlarla bağlantılı kuruluşlarda kendi adınıza ya da başkası üzerinden kullandığınız yatırım hesaplarınız oldu mu? Görev yaptığınız dönemde Türkiye Sigorta ve Türkiye Hayat ve Emeklilik’in kendi kurumsal kaynaklarından ve yönettikleri bireysel emeklilik (BES) fonlarından TERA’ya veya bağlantılı fonlara toplam ne kadar para yatırıldı? Bu yatırımların kararını kim verdi? Bugün gözaltına alınan özel kalem personelleriniz Fahri Uğur ve Hakan Eryılmaz’ın bu süreçteki rolü ve talimat trafiği nedir? Yatırım komitesi kararlarını ve risk değerlendirme raporlarını açıklayacak mısınız?

Türkiye Sigorta ve Türkiye Hayat ve Emeklilik bu yatırımlara karar verirken sizin de aynı fonlarda veya bu fonların aldığı hisselerde yatırımınız var mıydı? Varsa kendi mali çıkarınızın da bulunduğunu yöneticilere ve denetçilere bildirdiniz mi? Bu kararların alınmasına katıldınız mı, yoksa karar sürecinin dışında mı kaldınız? Karayipler’deki Saint Vincent adasında kurulu Artsmrkts Ltd hesabında bugün özel kalemlerinizin gözaltına alındığı soruşturmada geçen Vişne Madencilik ve TERA/Hedef hisseleriyle aynı sepette 15,5 milyon lot Türkiye Sigorta pozisyonu taşındığından haberiniz oldu mu? Daha anlaşılır soralım: Maslak’tan yönetilen Artsmrkts, Londra’daki GildenCrest ve İsviçre’deki Century City Securities ile herhangi bir hesap, para transferi, yatırım veya talimat ilişkiniz oldu mu? Bu kuruluşlar üzerinden sizin hesabınıza ya da menfaatinize işlem yapıldı mı?

Yönettiğiniz kamu bağlantılı şirketler bu fonlara para yatırırken siz kendi hesaplarınızdaki fonları veya hisseleri satıp paranızı çektiniz mi? Şirketlerin para yatırdığı tarihlerle sizin satış yapıp para çektiğiniz tarihleri karşılaştırmalı olarak açıklayacak mısınız? Bu kurumsal yatırımların karşılığında hangi varlıklar alındı, kimlerin fon iade talepleri ödendi? Kamu şirketlerinin yatırdığı 100 milyon TL’nin fonda batık kalırken sizin ve diğer imtiyazlı yatırımcıların fondan erken çıkışını (nakde dönmesini) finanse edip etmediği araştırıldı mı? TERA ve bağlantılı fonlara yapılan yatırımlar konusunda risk birimleri veya denetçiler sizi uyardı mı? Uyardılarsa hangi önlemleri aldınız? Önlem alınmadıysa neden alınmadı? Türkiye Sigorta’nın bilançosunun açıklanmasının ertelendiği ve 4 milyar TL’lik geri alım maliyeti oluştuğu yönündeki iddialar doğru mu? Doğruysa bu gelişmelerin söz konusu yatırımlarla bağlantısı nedir ve sorumluluğu kim taşıyor?”

author: Caitlyn Clark
title: Interview: How We Beat Back Nonunion Subcontracting at Kroger
content:
After more than six months fighting against Kroger’s use of non-union subcontractors, members of Food and Commercial Workers (UFCW) Local 700 in Indiana won a

victory

 in August, when Kroger announced it would be ending the Retail Odyssey direct store delivery (DSD) program entirely.


This means more hours for union members—thanks to those who organized to enforce the contract, file grievances, and educate their co-workers. In this interview conducted by Caitlyn Clark of the reform group Essential Workers for Democracy, shop stewards Andrea Reynolds and Kristen Jackson explain how they did it.


Essential Workers for Democracy: What is Retail Odyssey and why is it a problem?


Andrea Reynolds:

 Retail Odyssey is a nonunion third-party contractor that solely services Kroger stores. Normally RO does things like rearranging a store layout or auditing whether products are displayed the way the brand wants.


A few months ago, the Kroger Central Division here in Indiana developed a new program utilizing RO employees to stock direct store delivery vendor items on weekends. [

DSD items are delivered straight to the store by the supplier, rather than coming through a Kroger warehouse.

]


Why is this a problem? Kroger has employees who need hours. This isn't “extra help.” Kroger wants to phase nonunion third parties into the stores to cut hours of its union employees. If we don't speak up, it will only get worse. We’ve seen this happen already with cut fruit vendors, outdoor floral products, floor cleaning, and gift cards, just to name a few.


How did you and your co-workers start taking on Retail Odyssey?


Reynolds:

 We immediately started gathering as much accurate information as we could and passing it along to our co-workers. We shared information in our Facebook group and we shared flyers with our co-workers.


We wanted them to know why this was a problem and what they could do about it. The company wants us to think that third parties are there to make our jobs easier. But time and time again, we see our hours cut and wonder why.


We also passed along the feedback of our vendors. Their products were being damaged, mixed with other vendors, and stocked incorrectly.


Kristen Jackson:

 Although in the pharmacy, I am not as impacted, my union brothers and sisters are. As a steward, I try my best to let others know what is wrong with RO taking our work.


I walked around and talked to my co-workers about what the RO workers were allowed to stock. I told them if they saw them, to please take pictures, talk to the RO workers, and be nice.


By having a standardized report form, members could make sure grievances were airtight.


How did you collect information to file grievances? How did you make sure grievances got filed and processed?


Reynolds:

 Retail Odyssey was scheduled to work Friday through Sunday, noon to 6 p.m. I had a lot of conversations with members I knew were normally there during those hours.


I instructed them to take photos, make note of the day, time, duration of stocking, what non-vendor products were stocked, and anyone who witnessed it. We had them send this info to our stewards or trusted employees who could contact our union rep.


Every week after the grievance was filed, we messaged our reps asking for status of the grievance. We didn't want it to fall through the cracks.


Jackson:

 I just went up to the RO workers, introduced myself as a steward, and let them know I would be taking pictures of them and why. I explained, “I'm not against you having a job. I'm here to document Kroger violating our contract.”


The RO workers were understanding, and would tell me that the manager told them to stock our product and let me file the grievances. The RO worker at my store location would tell me exactly what he stocked, so I could file the grievances effectively. We filed three grievances at my location.


What advice would you give to anyone dealing with non-union subcontracting?


Reynolds:

 Document, document, document! You need to prove there was a contract violation.


Talk with your co-workers about how to document. Contact your rep. Don't hesitate to ask for help from a steward or a trusted member.


You have power in your numbers. The more members speaking up, the better! We filed so many grievances in six months that the third-party DSD program has officially ended. When we fight, we win.

author: Jen Fifield
title: Ballot Rejections Soared in Rural Counties After USPS Cost-Cutting Measures
content:
The rates of primary ballots rejected for arriving late this year doubled or tripled in some areas compared to 2022.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

In early August, election workers north of Spokane, Washington, went across the street to the post office to check for late mail-in ballots. It was three days after the primary and they were expecting no more than a few dozen.

Instead, their mailbox was brimming with envelopes — more than 500 of them, each a vote that wouldn’t count. The sight was “jarring,” said Auditor Lori Larsen, a Republican who oversees voting in Stevens County.

Across the region, other election officials were getting similar jolts. In the 11 predominately rural counties in eastern Washington, nearly 2,000 ballots came in late, compared to about 600 in 2022, the previous midterm primary.

In recent weeks, concerns about mail-in voting disruptions have focused almost entirely on President Donald Trump’s now-shelved plan to sharply restrict who can vote by mail.

But a ProPublica data analysis shows that delays resulting from the U.S. Postal Service’s cost-cutting measures have endangered the validity of ballots cast in rural areas, not only in Washington, but across the country.

Over the past three years, as mail volume continued to plummet and annual deficits ballooned, the Postal Service started consolidating the processing of first-class mail at larger regional plants instead of at smaller hubs closer to local post offices. Then, in a little-noted switch that mostly took effect after the 2024 election, the agency cut the frequency of mail pickups in half at many post offices 50 miles or more from these processing plants, from twice daily to once.

The changes often added a day or more to delivery time and, most importantly for ballots, pushed back postmarking, which doesn’t happen until mail reaches the regional centers.

In this year’s primary, the effects of the cuts were clearest in five states that make detailed data on mail-in ballots available: Washington, California, Ohio, North Carolina and Oregon. All have or recently had grace periods allowing ballots to count if they come in after Election Day as long as they’re postmarked by the deadline.

In these states, the number of ballots rejected for arriving late soared in counties affected by the service changes compared to 2022, ProPublica’s analysis showed.

Rejection rates in counties where services were cut doubled or tripled from what they were four years ago, dwarfing any increases in counties where postal pickups remained as they were, our analysis showed. In urban Spokane, for example, the number of ballots rejected for being late actually dropped this year.

Across the five states, the delays have had the most substantial effect in areas that voted for Trump in 2024, ProPublica’s analysis shows. In Washington, Secretary of State Steve Hobbs, a Democrat, said he sees the service changes directed by Republican appointees leading the Postal Service as a way to undermine mail-in voting.

“I don’t think they realized how much it was going to affect their voter base,” he said, adding that Washington has “a lot of rural Republican voters.”

Postal Service leaders say such delays are less likely in the Nov. 3 general election because of “extraordinary measures” the agency puts into place for these votes, when there’s typically far more turnout. They have circulated a memo to the nation’s more than 30,000 post offices saying that for the 10 days before the election, managers should separate completed ballots from other first-class mail and deliver those intended for local election offices the day they come in.

At an Oct. 15 news conference, Postal Service leaders emphasized the agency’s longstanding recommendation that voters mail ballots back at least a week before their states’ deadlines, while defending the agency’s ability to fast-track ballots through the system.

“We work to identify and address issues quickly,” said Amber McReynolds, chair of the Postal Service board of governors, “so ballots can continue to move swiftly from election offices to voters and from voters back to election offices.”

title: «No Data Center»: maxi scritta di Extinction Rebellion sull’edificio in cui dovrebbe sorgere il più grande data center d’Italia
content:
Riceviamo e pubblichiamo il comunicato stampa di Extinction Rebellion Torino.


22 ottobre 2026, Moncalieri (Torino) –

Extinction Rebellion ha realizzato delle enormi scritte “No Data Center” sullo stabilimento dismesso dell’ex Ilte e appeso uno striscione con la frase “Fermare l’ecocidio”. Una protesta per denunciare l’impatto ambientale, sanitario e sociale dei data center e di quello che potrebbe diventare il più grande impianto del Paese. «In un mondo che sta collassando, non c’è spazio per altre strutture ecocide»


“No Data Center”. È l’enorme scritta realizzata da Extinction Rebellion sulla facciata dello stabilimento ex-Ilte di Moncalieri, alle porte di Torino, edificio al centro dell’iter per la realizzazione di quello che potrebbe diventare il

più grande data center

 d’Italia. Accanto alla scritta principale, visibile anche dall’autostrada e da Moncalieri, una seconda scritta “Stop Tech Fascism” (Stop tecno-fascismo) è stata realizzata sulla facciata laterale e uno striscione srotolato su una terza facciata con scritto “Fermare l’ecocidio”.


«Lasciamo qui questo messaggio affinché sia visibile ovunque e serva da monito a tutte le amministrazioni»,

 spiega Extinction Rebellion.

«Un data center di queste dimensioni ha impatti ambientali, sanitari e sociali pericolosissimi ed è incompatibile con qualsiasi obiettivo climatico. In un mondo che sta collassando e in cui il costo della vita sta soffocando la maggioranza della popolazione, non c’è spazio per investimenti miliardari per strutture ecocide».

 Al centro della protesta ci sono gli enormi consumi energetici e idrici dei data center, oltre ai possibili effetti sociali e sanitari. Un impianto come quello ipotizzato a Moncalieri, da 527 megawatt e 4,5 miliardi di euro, consumerebbe tanta energia

quanto tutte le famiglie

 piemontesi. A ciò si aggiunge l’acqua necessaria a raffreddare i server, in una regione alle prese con una siccità cronica, che ad agosto ha

avviato le procedure

 per chiedere lo stato di calamità naturale per l’emergenza idrica. Anche i refrigeranti identificati come soluzione al consumo d’acqua possono in realtà comportare rischi:

molti contengono

 PFAS, le cosiddette «sostanze chimiche eterne», che si disperdono nell’ambiente e si accumulano nel corpo umano. Un problema che il Piemonte conosce bene: a Spinetta Marengo, nell’Alessandrino, la produzione di PFAS dello stabilimento Solvay

ha già esposto

 gli abitanti alla contaminazione, e queste stesse sostanze

sono state rilevate

 anche nell’acqua potabile di oltre 70 comuni del torinese. In ultimo, i data center sono diventati veri e propri

bersagli militari strategici

 negli ultimi anni, trasformando le infrastrutture digitali e l’Intelligenza Artificiale in nuovi teatri di guerra.


«Moltiplicare queste enormi infrastrutture è folle: significa aumentare la pressione sulle risorse naturali e la dipendenza dai combustibili fossili, proprio quando la crisi climatica impone di azzerare le emissioni e contenere i consumi»,

 aggiunge Extinction Rebellion. Nel

rapporto «Energy and AI»

 del 2025 dell’Agenzia Internazionale dell’Energia (IEA), la domanda dei maxi data center è infatti indicata come uno dei motori della crescita della produzione elettrica da gas e carbone fino alla fine del decennio. Lo stesso assessore regionale all’Ambiente, Matteo Marnati, ha ammesso che le rinnovabili non basteranno e ha annunciato che

chiederà al governo

 di escludere i consumi dei data center dal calcolo degli obiettivi di decarbonizzazione. Durante un convegno all’Ordine degli Avvocati di Torino

ha poi dichiarato

 che per alimentarli «è imprescindibile pensare all’energia nucleare».

«Le scelte del governo e della Regione sono surreali: prima creano il problema, poi impongono una soluzione che ne genera un altro, ancora più grave, spacciandola per inevitabile»,

 replica Extinction Rebellion.


Il progetto del più grande data center di Italia ha già incontrato i primi ostacoli: a ottobre il sindaco di Moncalieri lo

ha definito

 «non accoglibile», anche se il Comune ha tempo fino a fine mese per la decisione. Per questo la protesta è andata in scena proprio sullo stabilimento: mentre l’iter prosegue, la scritta resterà lì, visibile a tutti. Intanto i cittadini del posto

hanno lanciato

 una raccolta firme per fermare il progetto. La richiesta di Extinction Rebellion è netta: fermare il maxi data center, bonificare l’area e restituirla alla comunità.

author: David Venn
title: QEC announces planned power outages in Kimmirut, Resolute Bay
content:
Qulliq Energy Corp. is planning outages in Kimmirut and Resolute Bay this weekend, with the possibility of an outage in Iqaluit as well.


The corporation announced the outages in a series of public service announcements Thursday as it gears up for a weekend of work.


In Resolute Bay, QEC is carrying out maintenance on the power lines to get them ready for winter. A planned outage is set to take place Saturday and Sunday from 7 a.m. to 11 a.m. to allow for this work.


In Kimmirut, QEC is installing a new generator in the hamlet’s power plant. An outage is scheduled for Sunday, from 6 a.m. to 9 a.m.


In Iqaluit, QEC says it expects to be able to connect a new generator to its power plant without interrupting power to the community.


“However, a temporary outage remains possible in the event of an unexpected equipment malfunction,” the announcement said.


The scheduled work in Iqaluit is scheduled for Saturday and Sunday, from 6 a.m. to 8 a.m.

title: DBP engages with the public on peace: ‘We will develop a roadmap’
content:
The Democratic Regions Party (DBP) is holding public meetings in various cities under the slogan “Building the language of peace together with the people” to promote broader public participation in the peace and resolution process. The meetings, attended by party leaders, co-chairs, members of the Central Executive Committee (MYK), and Party Council members, are continuing across numerous cities in Kurdistan.


Aiming to reach a broad cross-section of society, from workers and civil society organizations to different faith communities and political groups, the DBP seeks to listen to the public’s expectations and proposals during these meetings and develop new policies concerning the process.


‘We aim to reach all segments of society through these meetings’


Speaking to ANF on the scope of the initiative, DBP Party Council member Bünyamin Şeker emphasized that the public meetings go beyond simply organizing gatherings. The activities are not limited to a single day, but involve extensive programs held across different parts of each city. Through these programs, the party aims to reach all segments of society and shape the discourse on peace together with the people.


Şeker pointed out that the primary objective of the public meetings is to help society understand the process, adding that the party has been working toward this goal since the February 27 declaration.


Şeker said: “We are engaged in continuous efforts, mobilizing to ensure that people understand this process. The state is not making sufficient efforts to encourage broader public participation in the process. Claims that society is not ready for the process are also incorrect. Through these meetings, we are trying to reach even those who remain skeptical of the process. At these public meetings, we are shaping the discourse on peace together with the people. We are receiving tremendous support from our people. There is strong public participation, with people openly expressing their views and expectations.”


https://1649452211.rsc.cdn77.org/20261020092554_2026-10-21-amed-bunyamin-seker-dbp-parti-meclisi-uyesi-baris-ve-demokratik-toplum-sureci-1.mp4


‘We are developing new policies’


Şeker stated that the views expressed during public meetings play a decisive role in shaping new policies. The meetings are not merely intended to provide information but also to identify the needs and expectations of the people, he added.


“The people themselves express what they expect and how they believe the process should proceed. As their representatives, we develop new policies based on the conclusions drawn from these discussions. We assess the debates and outcomes concerning what needs to be done to move the process forward and seek to formulate new policies accordingly,” Şeker said.


‘The lack of concrete steps is increasing concerns’


Şeker emphasized that distrust of the state is among the main concerns raised during the meetings, linking this distrust to existing policies and the failure to take concrete steps.


“We can see that the people have a clear understanding of the process. The fact that the state has taken no action has left them waiting with growing conern. When we look at the government’s policies and the way it is managing the process, it becomes clear that the people’s concerns are justified,” he said.


‘We will develop a roadmap based on the people’s demands and criticisms’


Bünyamin Şeker stated that the lack of concrete steps and the perception that the process is being conducted unilaterally are among the main concerns expressed by the public. He added that another important issue discussed during the meetings is the potential gains that could emerge if the process succeeds.


Emphasizing that the public has particularly strong expectations regarding identity and language rights, Şeker said: “This struggle has been going on for many years. For more than a century, the state has pursued policies of denial and rejection. At various times, policies of annihilation were also implemented. Will all of this come to an end through this process or if the process succeeds? Will we be able to freely express our identity and use our language? These are the questions people are asking. Their demands and criticisms will be collected and analyzed, and a roadmap will be developed accordingly.”

title: TJA stages torchlight marches in Istanbul for Öcalan’s freedom
content:
The Free Women’s Movement (Tevgera Jinên Azad, TJA) held simultaneous torchlight marches in three Istanbul districts, demanding an end to Abdullah Öcalan’s isolation and his physical freedom. The demonstrations in Küçükçekmece, Gaziosmanpaşa, and Sancaktepe also called on the Turkish government and parliament to establish the legal and political conditions necessary for lasting peace. Police blocked the marches in all three districts.


Alongside numerous women, representatives of political parties and civil society organizations also took part in the demonstrations. Participants lit torches and unfurled banners bearing slogans such as “Now Is the Time to Win – Time to Meet the Free Leader” and “Now Is the Time for Women.” They also chanted slogans including “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” [Woman, Life, Freedom], “Bijî Serok Apo” [Long Live Leader Öcalan], and “A Thousand Greetings to Imrali.”


In Gaziosmanpaşa, police prevented the planned march from taking place at Karayolları Square. Gatherings in Küçükçekmece and Sancaktepe were also blocked by police barricades. Participants protested the police intervention by chanting slogans.


https://1649452211.rsc.cdn77.org/20261021202103_2026-10-21-istanbul-tja-abdullah-ocalana-tecride-karsi-siyariyla-3-yerde-eylem-duzenledi_1.mp4


Legal guarantees demanded for Öcalan’s role in the peace process


A joint statement by the Kurdish women’s movement was read aloud at all three rallies. In Küçükçekmece, TJA activist Suna Kalmaz delivered the statement, while in Gaziosmanpaşa, Leyla Eser and Selcan Saygı read it in Kurdish and Turkish, respectively. In Sancaktepe, the statement was read by Züleyha Çengel.


The central demand was an immediate end to Abdullah Öcalan’s isolation on the prison island of Imrali. The TJA called for regular meetings with his lawyers, as well as access for journalists, women’s organizations, intellectuals, and representatives of democratic institutions. It also demanded that Öcalan’s physical freedom be guaranteed and that his role in the peace process, including his legal and political status, be formally secured.


“Lasting and dignified peace can only be achieved through democratic and political means,” the women’s movement declared. It called on the state, government, and parliament to establish the conditions necessary for negotiations and to stop delaying the required legislative and political measures.


Women demand a leading role in the peace process


The TJA also emphasized that women must not be relegated to a supporting role in the peace process, saying: “As a driving force behind social change, women must be directly involved in negotiations and political decision-making. A peace process that excludes the will and organized strength of women cannot guarantee lasting peace.”


The women’s movement advocated a democratic future in which freedom, equality, and self-determined coexistence replace war, violence, and denial. It stressed that Öcalan’s physical freedom and a free and equal future for all peoples are inseparably linked.


A free future for the peoples!


The TJA announced that it would continue its demonstrations for Öcalan’s freedom in streets and public squares and remain committed to building broader public support for the peace process. It also called on women, democratic organizations, and the wider public to take a stand against his isolation and assume responsibility for achieving a democratic solution.


The statement concluded with the words: “We women do not wait for peace; we build it and lead the way! Freedom for Abdullah Öcalan, a free future for the peoples! The gates of Imrali must be opened immediately, the isolation must end, and the way must be cleared for a dignified and lasting peace!”

title: DBP: Kurdish unity is critical in the face of multidimensional warfare
content:
The Democratic Regions Party (DBP) released the final declaration of its Party Council (PM) meeting held in Amed (tr: Diyarbakır) on October 18.


Published under the title “Kurdish Unity Is Critical in the Face of Multidimensional Warfare,” the declaration assessed global and regional developments, including those in the Middle East and Kurdistan, and outlined the party’s plans for the coming period.


“Mr. Öcalan’s vision of a democratic society has created an important historical foundation for ending conflicts and strengthening democratic politics, both in the Middle East and in Turkey,” the declaration said.


Call to intensify the struggle for freedom, equality, and peace


Emphasizing that the Middle East does not need new wars, new borders, or new hegemonic relationships, the final declaration stated:


“What the peoples of the Middle East need most is a new social paradigm that strengthens grassroots organization, prioritizes women’s freedom, defends ecological living, reinforces democratic politics, and builds a shared future for all peoples. Democratic local organizations and the collective will of the peoples represent the strongest democratic alternative to both imperialist interventions and authoritarian regimes. For this reason, we invite all peoples to become active participants in building a democratic society and call on them to intensify the struggle for freedom, equality, and peace.”


‘Failure to secure free conditions for Öcalan is a shortcoming’


Emphasizing that unity among the Kurdish people is of critical importance in the face of multidimensional warfare, the DBP statement continued:


“The Kurdish people, who have faced policies of denial and annihilation for centuries, have reached a stage where they can play an active role in building peace and a democratic society thanks to their efforts, struggle, and sacrifices. Today, too, the Kurdish people and their friends, regardless of borders, will undoubtedly honor these sacrifices and further strengthen their efforts and struggle.


The Peace and Democratic Society Process has progressed to this point thanks to the historic initiative, determined stance, and calls made by Mr. Abdullah Öcalan. He has been playing a one-sided game of chess, making tremendous efforts to build a Democratic Republic in which all parties and oppressed groups can live as equal citizens. Advancing this vision and democratizing the Republic are fundamental responsibilities of ours and of all democratic forces.


The fact that Mr. Öcalan, the Coordinator of Peace and Political Participation, has still not been provided with the conditions necessary to work freely and that his legal status has not been established constitutes a historic shortcoming.”


‘The path of women’s freedom’


The statement emphasized that the process provides a foundation on which all segments of society can live freely with their own identities. It continued:


“Freedom of identity, one of Turkey’s greatest needs today, is key to addressing interconnected issues such as justice, equality, women’s freedom, ecological destruction, and poverty. With this understanding, the process represents a historic opportunity that must be embraced and advanced by all those who wish to transform Turkey into a country in which they want to live.


Embedding peace in society, securing broad public support for the process, and establishing legal and legislative guarantees are not steps that should be postponed or made conditional. Social transformation can only become lasting when it is founded on a strategy of women’s freedom. We can build peace by fostering a culture that upholds the right to a life free from violence.


We reaffirm our commitment to continuing our struggle to ensure that women’s leadership and the principles of women’s freedom become decisive in every sphere of life, as essential foundations for embedding peace in society and building a democratic society.”


Process of democratic unity


The Peace and Democratic Society Process initially generated great excitement and hope among the people. The primary aim of those opposing the process, both in their thinking and their actions, is to undermine society’s expectations of it.

title: O ecocídio por trás de Flávio Bolsonaro
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Ligando os pontos, enviada toda quinta-feira. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui

O engenheiro florestal Argemiro Teixeira Leite-Filho, do INPE,  que há anos tem estudado os impactos do desmatamento da Amazônia sobre as chuvas que alimentam o Sudeste e o Centro-Oeste cunhou um termo que explica o risco do crescimento econômico a qualquer custo – o agrossuicídio. 


O que esta palavra explica é como a perda da floresta influi diretamente na quantidade de água que cai sobre as maiores lavouras e pastagens do país. Provou com

análises de imagens de satélite

 que, nas partes mais desmatadas de Rondônia e Mato Grosso, o clima está mais seco. Ou seja, aqueles produtores que derrubaram e queimaram por ganância, no longo prazo estão perdendo seu principal insumo – a água. Sem os rios voadores criados pela umidade da floresta, o agronegócio, considerado o motor econômico do Brasil, pode se tornar inviável.


Ao ouvir as propostas do candidato à presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), tenho convicção de que o Brasil pode cometer um suicídio ecológico.

Por trás de seus discursos que prometem simplificar a vida do empreendedor e do produtor rural, há uma mensagem de que um eventual governo vai liberar geral: pode desmatar que não haverá multas, pode garimpar que não haverá fiscalização, pode grilar que terra roubada vai ser regularizada.


Foi

o que aconteceu no governo de Jair Bolsonaro

. O antigo presidente perseguiu os fiscais do Ibama e congelou a cobrança de multas por crimes ambientais. As áreas de garimpo ilegal cresceram 92% em quatro anos, como mostrei em uma coluna há duas semanas. Muitas outras boiadas passaram e o resultado deste projeto destrutivo se revelou nas taxas de desmatamento: no governo Bolsonaro as derrubadas na Amazônia aumentaram 59,6%.


Nas redes de desinformação bolsonaristas há uma tentativa de emplacar a mentira de que foi no governo Lula que aconteceu a tragédia dos garimpos na Terra Indígena Yanomami. Ou ainda que, nestes últimos anos, o desmatamento bateu recordes. Apenas dando um google, pode-se checar estes dados e comprovar que políticos aliados de Flávio seguem mentindo sem pudor. 


Foi a fiscalização do Ibama e do Exército do atual governo que conseguiu expulsar os garimpeiros do território Yanomami. Foi no governo Lula que as derrubadas voltaram a cair. Na semana passada, tivemos a ótima notícia de que o desmatamento na Amazônia e no Cerrado chegou ao

nível mais baixo da história

. 


É possível dizer que, durante o governo de Bolsonaro, o Brasil estava caminhando a passos largos para um ecocídio. Este também é

um termo já existente

. É utilizado como um conceito que embasa processos levados à Corte Penal Internacional. Juristas e ONGs buscam neste momento imputar responsabilidade a governos e empresas que, com suas atividades destrutivas, tornam a vida no planeta insustentável. 


Pense nas mudanças climáticas. Nunca estivemos num momento tão crítico no balanço entre o clima e a saúde humana. Nesta semana, por exemplo,

uma análise de dados sobre a frequência

 e intensidade das ondas de calor revelou que, enquanto nos anos 1960 havia em média cinco eventos de calor extremo no mundo, no ano passado foram 102 episódios de “tempestades de calor”. Frente a este cenário de emergência, o que encontramos em Flávio Bolsonaro? Um negacionista desonesto que repete a ladainha de Trump que o mundo está esfriando. É uma postura ultrajante e perigosa. O Brasil, país que detém a maior floresta tropical úmida do planeta, não pode aderir a um governo que feche os olhos para a emergência climática.


Se já temos indícios de que a Amazônia, o Cerrado e o Pantanal estão sofrendo com a falta de chuvas, um projeto de poder bolsonarista, que não respeita as regras ambientais, apenas nos empurra para a beira do abismo. Não é exagero pensar que o suprimento de água, energia e mesmo a disponibilidade de comida barata estão diretamente ameaçadas pela eleição de Flávio Bolsonaro.


É muito grave sua afirmação de que, caso eleito, não vai demarcar novas terras indígenas. Se o Brasil ainda tem florestas preservadas e rios limpos, isso se deve em grande parte ao cuidado que os povos indígenas tiveram com seus territórios. Privá-los do que já é garantido pela Constituição já seria um crime de violação aos seus direitos. Mas promover a destruição e a invasão destes territórios é algo que afetará a todos os …

author: Claudia Castillo
title: How can a “broken” body cross the world?
content:
How can a “broken” body cross the world?

 


(My experience participating in Women Deliver 2026)


By Gianna Agostina Mastrolinardo

 


(SCROLL DOWN FOR ORIGINAL TEXT IN SPANISH)


 

For me, as woman with a disability, participating in the last edition of Women Deliver in Melbourne, Australia wasn’t simply about attending a conference. This was an intense and transformative experience that tested my own limits, and it also meant that me and my body had to navigate structural barriers that restrict the participation of young women with disabilities in global events such as this one. 

 


 

One full day of traveling, three flights, more than 12,000 kilometers of flying. Never having traveled so far, the magnitude of the event, and not speaking English that fluently all could have been reason enough to justify saying no to this opportunity. However, I decided to say yes. Even though I was afraid, I said yes with the conviction that we must occupy those spaces, because our presence transforms them. 

 


 


My desire to cross the world and be part of what was happening in Naarm was not enough for me to stop thinking of it as something impossible. Support and collective effort were crucial to stripping that last word of the prefix that imprisons dreams. And now that I think of this experience again, an inescapable feeling comes to me: the relief of knowing I don’t have to think about disability in isolation. 

 


 


 I am a Latin American “lisiada” cripple from Córdoba, Argentina, I am 23 years old and I live my daily life fighting for the effective realization of the rights of people with disabilities with the certainty that every roll of my wheels is possible because there are many people who work with me, who accompany me, who care for me and who even believe and trust in me when I simply cannot.  

 


WEI not only generously approached me with this opportunity. They also worked with Women Deliver so that this experience did not become only about managing how to overcome barriers, but rather, that it could be about enjoyment, learning, and the wonderful opportunity to find each other regardless of our languages or the physical distances between the places we come from.

 


 


Without a doubt, this experience was challenging. However, the availability of support, the design of dialogue spaces, and the warmth that was present throughout the process reaffirmed my belief that there is something extremely political about spaces having to take steps to ensure accessibility. When facing barriers stops being an individual issue and instead creating ways in which everyone can participate becomes a collective responsibility, the world we dream of achieving becomes a reality. 

 


 


To be in Melbourne was to live for a few days in that world. I had never before experienced such an accessible city. Sidewalks, ramps, public transport, and a quality of life I thought existed only in my fantasies. I did not have to worry about managing how to move with my wheelchair or  do research ahead of time to make sure there were accessible bathrooms. Where I live, I cannot use public transportation because even when we manage to find accessible transport, getting to the bus stop is impossible. But in Australia, I even saw accommodations that I had never imagined (like a button that opens heavy doors! I definitely need that in my life). Having so many resources translates into immeasurable freedom, and I am aware that experiencing them was a great privilege.

 


 


The political support from my organization:

La Mesa de Trabajo en Discapacidad y Derechos Humanos

was another essential element to making this possible, because they accompanied me during the trip and in everything that came before it. They were there every step of the way; they helped me to practice my English and t

o gauge the implications of a convening of this nature, to understand the discussions, and to consider my own contributions. This helped me feel a sense of security and confidence. My colleague Bri put her body in every part of the process with me. She was there not only during the trip, but also when, out of nowhere, I was asked to take medical exams for my visa. She was there when we discovered that my wheelchair couldn’t come with me due to airline restrictions and when—during the trip— the wheelchair I did travel with broke. She listened to me and offered me her words and physical and emotional support when I felt nervous, anxious, or frustrated …

author: Unknown
title: Introducing the NSPM-7 Defendants Union
content:
Earlier this month,

The Guardian


announced

 the existence of the

NSPM-7 Defendants Union

, a new experiment in movement defense. We reached out to the organizers for an overview of their project, which we present here.


Announcing the NSPM-7 Defendants Union


National Security Presidential Memorandum 7 (NSPM-7) is a government-wide strategy to investigate, disrupt, and prosecute what the Trump administration calls “left-wing political extremism.” They have already used it to justify publicly killing Minneapolis anti-ICE rapid responders Renee Good and Alex Pretti,

raiding the homes

 of University of Michigan students protesting the genocide of Palestinians, and

re-indicting

 Stop Cop City protesters.


But by the tens of thousands, newly politicized people are learning to fight: Minnesotan moms tracking BORTAC agents, students throwing back tear gas outside

Delaney Hall

, nurses making split-decisions to help people escape from ICE. Especially in the movement against Trump’s deportation agenda, thousands of people are taking brave actions for the first time.


NSPM-7 is intended to turn their lives upside down. We want to make them stronger.


For decades, social movements have developed strategies to withstand repression, learn, and propagate revolutionary politics. Those of us who have had our homes raided, organized collective defense,

resisted grand juries

, built

support committees

, devised

media strategies

, and stayed active through periods of repression have something valuable to offer the growing list of NSPM-7 defendants. That’s why we built the NSPM-7 Defendants Union.


We aim to make our social movements resilient. To do so, we need to make everyone aware of Trump’s strategy to crush dissent and mount a common defense against it while recentering the discussion about what Trump calls “antifa” on our own terms, so that we can speak proudly and publicly in defense of our politics and our resistance.


The Defendants Pledge


NSPM-7 treats Trump’s adversaries as if they all comprise a single united movement. We should use that to our advantage. We want a critical mass of new defendants across the country to adopt a shared framework to fight their cases. If everyone embraces bold, political publicity and commits to collective defense, we could amass leverage across hundreds of cases.


We want you to take this

pledge

 if you are a political defendant, if you have been contacted by the police or federal agents, if you are under surveillance, or if you believe that any of these things could happen in the foreseeable future. We take this pledge across movements, as a promise to each other.


I pledge:


To Go Public with My Case

: I will not be quiet. I want as large an audience as possible to know about my case.


To Benefit the Movement

: When I talk about my case, I will link it to the larger movement. I will use the platform of my case to spread the ideas and values of the movement, so that many more people can learn what I believe in and be inspired by those ideas as well.


To Share Lessons Learned

: I will talk openly within the movement and to the public about the repressive strategies I learn about in the course of my case, so that everyone can learn how the state is targeting activists.


To Take the Offense

: I will take an aggressive legal and media strategy to beat my case, call the state’s bluff, and politicize others.


To Pursue Collective Defense

: I will prioritize legal strategies leveraging collective defense so that we all beat the charges, together. I will encourage my lawyer to communicate with my co-defendants’ lawyers and other elements of the movement. When possible, I will utilize joint-defense agreements with my co-defendants.


Not to Denounce Others in the Movement

: I will not publicly denounce the tactical choices of anyone accused of actions I don’t personally agree with.


Not to Cooperate with Law Enforcement

: I will not cooperate with any investigatory or prosecutorial arm of the state. If I am pressured to do so, I will refuse. I will go public and tell the movement if law enforcement visits me.


Our goal is to make these ideas hegemonic. We want this pledge to reach far and wide. Print it out and read it with your friends. Paste it up at encampments. Go on the news and recite it. Distribute it at a No Kings march. Read it aloud at a court support event. Tag it across your city. Hang it by your front door. Get creative.

title: Il 30 ottobre scendiamo in piazza uniti!
content:
Il

30 ottobre sarà sciopero generale.

 Sarà una grande occasione per tornare in piazza, in tanti e tante, in tutte le piazze d’Italia per far sentire la voce di questo grande movimento che sta nascendo contro la guerra e il carovita. Grazie all

’Unione Sindacale di Base

 ci sarà la possibilità per molti di poter scioperare e non entrare a lavoro e a scuola. 


Gli studenti bloccano e occupano le scuole da settimane  scendendo in strada a migliaia.  A Milano, Torino, Bologna, Brescia e in tante altre città e paesi i giovani hanno travolto le strade con la propria vitalità, voglia di contare e farsi sentire. I giovani di questo paese stanno mostrando a tutti che per essere ascoltati bisogna essere visibili: bisogna destare clamore. Intanto, al Sud, gli autotrasportatori e gli agricoltori hanno bloccato le autostrade e i rifornimenti della grande distribuzione per difendere il loro lavoro e la loro dignità.

 Il 30 ottobre sarà l’occasione per unire queste lotte: generazioni diverse ma con gli stessi problemi e gli stessi nemici.


Oggi, a mettersi in movimento, sono masse di persone in Francia, Spagna, Albania, Italia e questo

fa tremare i potenti di ogni paese europeo

 e le élites che comandano l’Unione Europea.

Tremano perchè dal basso arrivano richieste chiare: basta soldi per la guerra e il genocidio, basta alimentare la guerra in Ucraina, le risorse vadano per migliorare le condizioni di vita del popolo.

 Se il movimento avrà la forza di imporre queste richieste senza indietreggiare, l’intera architettura del loro potere può crollare. Anni di prese in giro verranno smascherate e soprattutto sarà possibile aprire un orizzonte collettivo in cui sapremo che dal basso si possono cambiare le cose. 


Il Governo Meloni, risponde alle proteste con razzismo e polizia, cerca di isolare i giovani che hanno dimostrato forza e un profondo senso politico di cos’è la lotta

. Il nostro compito collettivo deve essere quello  di contrastare i tentativi di isolare e perimetrare la parte più importante di questo movimento: occorre costruire legami e difendere tutti i modi di stare in piazza. Perché che sia un blocco, un esproprio, una stazione occupata, un trattore in autostrada o un semplice corteo tutto sta contribuendo a far sentire forte la voce di chi sta in basso.


Invitiamo tutti e tutte a scendere in piazza il 30 ottobre, lasciando da parte le divisioni politiche tra organizzazioni e collettivi, la spontaneità delle piazze di queste settimane ci dimostra che l’unità e la forza sono già fra di noi.

Organizziamoci insieme per bloccare tutta l’Italia. Blocchiamo i porti, le fabbriche, le autostrade, le scuole, le università. Obblighiamo il Governo, i politici, i padroni delle aziende, i presidi delle scuole, i rettori delle università a fare i conti con il popolo. 


Contro il carovita di guerra! Contro il Governo Meloni! Blocchiamo Tutto.

author: Jon Letman
title: Trump’s Anti-DEI Agenda Threatens to Slash Land Mine Disposal Efforts Globally
content:
The Trump administration’s expansion of its global gag rule threatens to derail NGOs’ crucial land mine removal work.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

US funding for overseas nongovernment organizations (NGOs) is now at risk. Due to a global gag rule that the Trump administration introduced early in 2026, government funding for certain foreign aid programs is subject to more stringent restrictions on activities related to diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI); abortion access; and what the Trump administration calls “gender ideology” (which includes gender-affirming counseling and care, as well as basic inclusion of and respect for transgender people). These restrictions are all occurring under what the State Department calls the Promoting Human Flourishing in Foreign Assistance policy.

Norwegian People’s Aid (NPA), a leading NGO doing land mine removal and disarmament work around the world, announced it will decline U.S. funding due to these new restrictions. In a press release, NPA Secretary General Raymond Johansen said the new requirements run contrary to the organization’s commitment to its core values including gender equality and diversity; therefore, it was forced to forego critical U.S. government support.

“We comply with Norwegian law and Norwegian policy, and our values are not for sale,” Johansen said.

The loss of financial support will have a major impact on NPA’s work removing anti-personnel land mines, cluster munitions, and unexploded ordnance left over from past wars and conflicts. The loss of 400 million Norwegian kroners (NOK) — around $42 million in U.S. dollars — in support from the State Department represents around 40 percent of NPA’s budget for clearing mines and bombs in 20 countries.

Overseas funding restrictions have existed under past presidents going back to the Reagan administration in 1984, but with the expansion of the gag rule, new requirements won’t only affect funding for U.S. programs, but will impact all NPA programs, Gry Ballestad, NPA’s director of policy and communications, told Truthout in an interview. “It will affect everything we do globally and this is what makes it different,” Ballestad said. NPA expects the loss of funding to result in 1,700 job cuts globally, including over 1,000 staff in Laos.

Although U.S. government funding for NPA is limited to mine removal programs, the new requirements could impact its global work, which includes international development programs and working with women’s organizations that may support abortion rights, LGBTQ rights, and anti-racism activities in Norway and elsewhere. NPA programs include refugee and integration, support for humanitarian aid, and addressing gender wealth disparities.

The loss in support from the State Department represents around 40 percent of NPA’s budget for clearing mines and bombs in 20 countries.

The loss of U.S. funding will have a major impact not only on NPA mine programs, but on the entire organization, Ballestad said, adding that while most donors impose conditions, the new restrictions run contrary to past requirements and may contradict those of other donors. She called the imposition of these funding requirements a political decision which has the potential to wield control over 400 million NOK for mine removal programs — and which could place NPA’s total budget of more than 1.6 billion NOK in legal jeopardy.

Ballestad said this represents a greater challenge to norms and regulations going back many decades: “We’ve never seen this before from a donor putting requirements that will affect the rest of your funding.”

Speaking Out for Democracy and Freedom

After months of legal consultations with lawyers in the U.S. and an unsuccessful attempt to receive a waiver for Southeast Asia where it does the majority of its mine work, NPA determined it had no choice but to uphold its principles, values, and obligations to its membership. “We can’t just change that because there’s a new American administration that comes up with new regulations … We’re a democratic organization,” Ballestad said. NPA’s outspoken position has received widespread support from labor unions and the Norwegian public.

NPA surveyed more than 5.3 million square meters for cluster munition contamination in 2025. Now that work will end.

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Makivvik wants to end time changes in Nunavik — but eyes next year for it
content:
People across Nunavik will be changing their clocks when daylight saving time ends on Nov. 1.


This is a pivot from Makivvik’s earlier plans, announced Oct. 30, 2025, for Nunavik to stay on daylight saving time year-round, starting this year.


Technical and administrative issues prevented the move, Makivvik announced Oct. 14 in a news release.


Now, the organization that represents Inuit across Nunavik is targeting November 2027 to end seasonal time changes in the region.


Makivvik launched a survey in January 2025 that asked Nunavimmiut whether the region should abolish seasonal time changes and, if so, whether it should remain on daylight saving time or standard time.


The clocks move forward during daylight saving time, creating more daylight hours in the evening, but later sunrises. Standard time brings earlier sunrises, but earlier sunsets too.


The organization said it will continue working through the legal and practical steps needed to make the change, the release said.


Clocks will move forward again on March 14, 2027, when daylight saving time resumes, the release said.

title: Strategien gegen Rechts (in Ostdeutschland): Erlebte Handlungsfähigkeit im Betrieb und (anti)demokratische Einstellungen
content:
Dossier


„Weite Teile der ostdeutschen Arbeitswelt sind durch geringe Tarifbindung, disruptive Transformationsprozesse und einen patriarchalen Führungsstil geprägt. Dabei kann die Erfahrung einer Mitbestimmungskultur im Berufsleben helfen, die oft kritisierte Verbreitung von extrem rechten Einstellungen zu senken. Insbesondere „Ausländerfeindlichkeit“, also die Abwertung von Menschen, die nicht zur Eigengruppe „der Deutschen“ gezählt werden, wird durch Beteiligungserfahrung am Arbeitsplatz reduziert. Das zeigen die neuen Daten unseres Arbeitspapiers, das die Ergebnisse zur „industrial citizenship“ der Leipziger Autoritarismus-Studie 2020 aufgreift und fortführt. Wer den Einsatz für Demokratie und gegen die extreme Rechte in den neuen Bundesländern ernst meint, sollte also auch den Ausbau der institutionellen Mitbestimmungsmöglichkeiten in ostdeutschen Firmen konkret fördern.“


Hinweis der Otto-Brenner-Stiftung


 auf die am 12. Dezember 2023 veröffentlichte Studie – siehe diese und weitere Informationen:


[„Sachsen-Anhalt ist ein Alarmsignal für die Gewerkschaften“] Solidarität muss man erfahren


„

Die AfD gewinnt weit über ihr rechtes Kernmilieu hinaus – besonders unter


Arbeiter:innen. Wer darauf nur mit Aufklärung über ihr Programm und Bekenntnissen zur Demokratie antwortet, unterschätzt das Problem. (…) Denn die Rede davon, Arbeiter:innen würden »gegen ihre eigenen Interessen« wählen, setzt voraus, dass aus einer sozialen Lage eindeutig folgt, worin das eigene Interesse besteht. Aber so funktioniert politisches Bewusstsein nicht. (…) Klassenlage produziert kein Klassenbewusstsein. Objektive Interessen sprechen nicht für sich selbst. Sie müssen erkannt, interpretiert und organisiert werden. Genau hier setzt die AfD an. Sie spricht Teile der arbeitenden Klasse gezielt an, artikuliert deren Interessen aber nicht als gemeinsames Klasseninteresse. Sie übersetzt soziale Erfahrungen in Gruppeninteressen, die gegeneinander in Stellung gebracht werden (…) Es reicht nicht, Beschäftigten ihre »richtigen« Interessen zu erklären. Wenn Menschen mehrere, teilweise widersprüchliche Interessen haben, ist die politische Aufgabe nicht pädagogisch, sondern organisierend. Sie besteht darin, unterschiedliche Interessen so miteinander zu verbinden, dass gemeinsame Handlungsfähigkeit entstehen kann.

Das ist der Kern von Klassenpolitik

Laut Nachwahlbefragungen machten im Februar 38 Prozent der Arbeiter ihr Kreuz bei der Partei – mehr als bei jeder anderen. Auch Gewerkschaftsmitglieder wählen zunehmend die AfD. Bei der letzten Bundestagswahl fiel die SPD erstmals in der Gunst der Gewerkschaftsmitglieder hinter CDU und AfD zurück. (…)


Gewerkschaften können dem Rechtsruck nicht allein mit Argumenten begegnen. Entscheidend sind erfolgreiche Kämpfe, Selbstermächtigung und eine klare Haltung gegen Spaltung. title: Li Amedê berxwedana li dijî projeya GESê: Welatiyan dest bi nobetê kirin
content:
Şîrketa bi navê Zenkarê dixwaze li gundê Arzoxliya navçeya Sûra Amedê Projeya Santrala Enerjiyê ya Rojê(

GES

) weke ZENKAR-1 û ZENKAR-2 çêbike. Berxwedana li dijî projeyê di roja duyemîn de ye. 


Pêvajoya hiqûqî ya li dijî biryara "ÇED Erênî ye" ya projeyê dewam dike. Xebatkarên şîrketê li gel jendermeyan û hêzên polîsan ketin qada kar.


Li ser vê yekê şêniyên taxê bi nûnerên partiyên siyasî û saziyên civakî yên sivîl û parêzvanên ekolojiyê ber bi qada projeyê ve meşiyan. Di çalakiyê de dirûşma "Axa me, ava me, hebûna me" hate qîrîn.


Li Arzoxliya Amedê li dijî GESê bertek hat nîşandan: "Ev qad çavkaniya debara me ye"


13 Adar 2026


“Destûrê nadin ku em biçin ser zeviyên xwe”


Şênî li cihekî nêzî qada projeyê li astengiya jendermeyan rast hatin û xwestin, ku sparteya hiqûqî ya karê li herêmê tê meşandin bê eşkerekirin. Serokê Komîsyona Bajar û Hawirdorê ya Baroya Amedê Ahmet Înan diyar kir ku astengî ne tenê li qada projeyê ye, her wiha li derveyî qada kar jî şênî nikarin biçin nava zeviyên xwe.


Parlamenterê Amedê yê DEM Partiyê Berdan Ozturk jî anî ziman ku ew li dijî projeyê ne, mafê jiyanê yê gundiyan ji wan tê standin û tê xwestin ku mirov ji cih û warê xwe koç bikin.


Şêniyên taxê jî diyar kirin ku ew debara xwe bi çandinî û sewalkariyê dikin û destnîşan kirin ku santral li ser tenduristî, sewalkarî û paşeroja wan gef e. Şêniyan ragihandin ku li hemberî karê şîrketê wê xak û çêrgehên xwe biparêzin û ew projeyê naxwazin.


Têkoşîna hiqûqî


Serokê Komîsyona Bajêr û Hawirdorê ya Baroya Amedê Ahmet Înan diyar kir ku li dijî destûra dayina çêrgehê, plana îmarê û rapora ÇED'ê doz vekirine û pêvajoya hiqûqî dewam dike. Înan anî ziman ku wê hemû hewldanên xwe yên hiqûqî dewam bikin û ji bo nobeda kon jî bê mezinkirin bang li saziyên demokratîk û parêzvanên jiyanê kir.


Piştî daxuyaniyê şêniyên taxê li qada projeyê dest bi nobeda kon kirin. Şêniyan diyar kirin ku ji bo parastina xak û qada xwe ya jiyanê wê berxwedana xwe dewam bikin.

author: Redazione_web
title: Schegge biografiche. Melchor Rodríguez García (1893-1972)
content:
Nato a Siviglia nel 1893 da famiglia povera, giovane operaio carrozziere, ex-torero, militante anarcosindacalista e della Federación Anarquista Ibérica, Melchor Rodríguez fu un militante dalla storia davvero singolare. Testardo, sensibile, ricco di pregi e difetti, finì più di trenta volte in carcere sotto tutti i regimi da lui subiti: monarchia, dittatura, repubblica, franchismo

.

Nel 1936, durante la guerra civile spagnola, fu nominato dal ministro della Giustizia, l’anarchico Juan García Oliver, come delegato speciale per le prigioni repubblicane, dove svolse il suo incarico con grande umanità e fedele alle sue parole, diventate poi celebri:

si può morire per delle idee, mai uccidere per esse

. La vita di Melchor – inseparabile dalle questioni del rapporto col potere, dalla relazione tra violenza e umanità, dal dilemma della giustizia e delle prigioni, dalla difesa della rivoluzione – continua ad interrogare chiunque desideri oggi la trasformazione dell’organizzazione sociale in senso libertario. Che queste schegge biografiche, raccolte in poco più di venti pagine, contribuiscano alle iniziative per il novantesimo della rivoluzione spagnola.


Dentro e fuori le prigioni, schegge biografiche su Melchor Rodríguez García.
